questions.q: Which of the following equations represents integrated rate law for zero order reaction?
questions.solution:
Let us consider a zero order reaction,
\begin{aligned} & -\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{A}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]^0 \\ & -\frac{\mathrm{d}[\mathrm{A}]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]^0=\mathrm{k} \\ & -\int \mathrm{d}[\mathrm{A}]=\int \mathrm{kdt} \\ & -[\mathrm{A}]_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{kt}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \text { at } \mathrm{t}=0 \quad \quad[\mathrm{~A}]_{\mathrm{t}}=[\mathrm{A}]_0 \\ & -[\mathrm{A}]_0=\mathrm{k} \times 0+\mathrm{C} \\ & \mathrm{C}=-[\mathrm{A}]_0 \end{aligned} On substituting the value of $C$ \begin{aligned} & -[\mathrm{A}]_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{kt}-[\mathrm{A}]_0 \\ & {[\mathrm{~A}]_{\mathrm{t}}=[\mathrm{A}]_0-\mathrm{kt}} \\ & \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{mx} \\ & {[\mathrm{A}]_0-[\mathrm{A}]_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{kt}} \\ & \mathrm{k}=\frac{[\mathrm{A}]_0-[\mathrm{A}]_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{t}} \end{aligned}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A reaction is first order with respective to A and second order with respective to $B$. What is the effect on reaction rate if concentration of B is increased 3 times?
questions.solution:
Rate law of reaction,

\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]^{\prime}[\mathrm{B}]^2

If concentration of $\mathrm{B}$ is increased 3 times,

\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{B} \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{~B} \\
& \mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{New}}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}][3 \mathrm{~B}]^2 \\
& \frac{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{New}}}{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}][3 \mathrm{~B}]^2}{\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}][\mathrm{B}]^2} \\
& \frac{\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{New}}}{\mathrm{r}}=3^2 \\
& \mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{New}}=9 \mathrm{r}
\end{aligned}

Rate increase 9 times.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The highest peak in energy profile diagram for mechanism of alkaline hydrolysis of tertiary butyl bromide represents
questions.solution:
The alkaline hydrolysis to tert-butyl bromide with aqueous alkali such as $\mathrm{NaOH}$ or $\mathrm{KOH}$ is as follows.
The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of the tert-butyl bromide and is independent of the concentration of alkali added. Rate $\alpha\left[\left(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\right)_{3} \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Br}\right]$ Rate $=\mathrm{K}\left[\left(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\right)_{3} \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Br}\right]$ This is a first order reaction because rate of hydrolysis of $\left(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\right)_{3}-\mathrm{Br}$ is independent of the concentration of alkali or $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions. This can be explained by two-step mechanism shown below. Each step is an elementary reaction with its own rate constant, step 1 proceeds much more slowly than step 2 .
Rate of reaction $=\mathrm{k}_{1}\left[\left(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\right)_{3} \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Br}\right]$ The first step consists of breaking of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Br}$ bond and it determines the rate of overall reaction. So, step 1 is called the rate-determining step. The rate determining step in this reaction involves only a single molecule, therefore, it is said to be unimolecular. Also, this type of mechanism is known as $\mathrm{SN}^{1}$ mechanism(substitution, nucleophilic, unimolecular).
Rate of reaction $=\mathrm{k}_{2}\left[\left(\mathrm{CH}_{3}\right)_{3} \mathrm{C}^{+}\right]\left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]$ The second step involves the attack of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ion. This is the fast step, since it is the bond formation step. Energy profile diagram of $\mathrm{SN}^{1}$ mechanism shows that rate of a reaction is independent of the concentration of nucleophile. The first step requires larger activation energy $\left(\Delta \mathrm{E}_{1}\right)$ than the second step $\left(\Delta \mathrm{E}_{2}\right)$. The first step to form carbocation determines the rate of overall reaction. The second step, which is the attack of nucleophile on carbocation is exothermic i.e., it is a lower energy transition state. The intermediate carbocation appears at a low point in the diagram. The conditions and reagents which favour the formation of carbocation will accelerate the $\mathrm{SN}^{1}$ reaction. The energy difference between products and reactants is $\Delta \mathrm{H}$, i.e., Heat of reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The first order integrated rate equation is
questions.solution:
For first order,

\text { rate }=\frac{d[R]}{d t}=k[R]

or

\frac{d[R]}{[R]}=k d t

On integrating Eq. (i)

\begin{array}{l}
\int \frac{d[R]}{[R]}=k \int d t \\
\ln [R]=-k t+C
\end{array}

$\ldots$
\text { At } t=0,[R]=\left[R_{0}\right]

[where, $R=$ final concentration, ie, $a-x$ and
$R_{0}$ is the initial concentration, $\left.i e, a .\right]$
\ln \left[R_{0}\right]=C

On putting the value of $C$ in Eq. (ii), we get

\begin{array}{r}
\ln [R]=-k t+\ln \left[R_{0}\right] \\
-k t=\ln [R]-\ln \left[R_{0}\right] \\
k t=\ln \left[R_{0}\right]-\ln [R]
\end{array}

or

\begin{aligned}
k &=\frac{1}{t} \ln \frac{\left[R_{0}\right]}{[R]} \\
or k&=\frac{1}{t} \ln \frac{a}{a-x}
\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a first order reaction, the half-life period is
options: dependent on the square of the initial concentration
dependent on first power of initial concentration
dependent on the square root of initial concentration
questions.solution:
$t_{1 / 2}=\frac{1}{(a)^{n-1}}$
where, $n=$ order of reaction $a=$ initial concentration For first order reaction,

\begin{aligned}
n &=1 \\
t_{1 / 2} &=\frac{1}{a^{1}-1} \\
a &=\frac{1}{a^{0}}=0
\end{aligned}

Thus, for a first order reaction, $t_{1 / 2}$ is independent on initial concentration.

questions.solution: Rate constant $k=1.155 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}k=\frac{2.303}{t} \log \frac{a}{(a-x)} \quad \because a=a,(a-x)=\frac{a}{2}\begin{aligned} t_{1 / 2} &=\frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{a}{a / 2} \\ &=\frac{2.303}{1.155 \times 10^{-3}} \log 2 \\ &=\frac{2.303}{1.155 \times 10^{-3}} \times 0.3010 \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} &=\frac{0.693 \times 10^{3}}{1.155} \\ \text { or } t_{1 / 2} &=\frac{0.693}{k}=\frac{0.693}{1.155 \times 10^{-3}} \\ &=600 \mathrm{~s} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical name of Aspirin?
questions.solution:
Aspirin is prepared by the acetylation of salicylic acid using acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst.

The chemical name of Aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid (or 2-acetoxybenzoic acid).

Answer: acetyl salicylic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify antimicrobial compound from following.
questions.solution:
Cinnamaldehyde is the main active component of cinnamon oil and is widely recognized in chemistry for its strong antimicrobial properties against various bacteria and fungi.

Curcumin is primarily known for its antioxidant properties.

Methyl salicylate is an analgesic used for pain relief.

Ascorbic acid is Vitamin C, which acts primarily as an antioxidant.

Thus, cinnamaldehyde is the antimicrobial compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following plants is useful to extract analgesic compound from it ?
questions.solution:
Wintergreen oil contains methyl salicylate, which is widely used as an analgesic compound in various pain-relieving ointments and balms.

Turmeric contains curcumin, which is primarily known for its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties.

Cinnamon contains cinnamaldehyde, used mainly as a flavoring agent and has antimicrobial properties.

Citrus fruits are rich in citric acid and vitamin C.

Therefore, wintergreen is the plant useful for extracting an analgesic compound.

Answer: Wintergreen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which medicinal property is exhibited by methylsalicylate?
questions.solution:
Methyl salicylate, commonly known as oil of wintergreen, is widely used in medicine as an analgesic.

It is applied topically in the form of ointments and liniments to relieve muscle and joint pain.

Therefore, it exhibits analgesic properties.

Answer: Analgesic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following detergents is used as germicide?
questions.solution:
Cationic detergents are quaternary ammonium salts of amines with acetates, chlorides, or bromides as anions.

They possess germicidal properties and are often used in hair conditioners and other cosmetic products.

An example of a cationic detergent is cetyltrimethylammonium bromide.

Therefore, cationic detergents are used as germicides.

Answer: Cationic detergent

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following cleansing agents contains cationic detergent?
questions.solution:
Cationic detergents are quaternary ammonium salts of amines with acetates, chlorides, or bromides as anions. The cationic part possesses a long hydrocarbon chain and a positive charge on the nitrogen atom.

Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide is a popular cationic detergent and is widely used in hair conditioners.

Anionic detergents are commonly used in household detergents and toothpaste.

Non-ionic detergents are used in liquid dishwashing detergents.

Answer: Hair conditioner

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the term used for drugs that reduce or relieve pain without causing loss of consciousness.
questions.solution:
Analgesics are neurological active drugs that reduce or abolish pain without causing impairment of consciousness, mental confusion, incoordination or paralysis or some other disturbances of nervous system.

Antipyretics are chemical substances which reduce body temperature during high fever.

Antibiotics are chemical substances produced wholly or partly by chemical synthesis, which in low concentrations inhibit the growth or destroy microorganisms by intervening in their metabolic processes.

Antimicrobials tend to destroy/prevent development or inhibit the pathogenic action of microbes such as bacteria, fungi, virus or other parasites selectively.

Answer: Analgesic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the use of Formalin from the followings.
options: Preservation of biological and anatomical specimens
questions.solution:
Formalin is a $40\%$ aqueous solution of formaldehyde.

It is widely used for the preservation of biological and anatomical specimens because it prevents decay and tissue degradation by cross-linking proteins.

Answer: Preservation of biological and anatomical specimens

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the use of antipyretic drugs.
questions.solution:
Antipyretic drugs are chemical substances which are used to lower the body temperature in high fever.

Common examples of antipyretic drugs include paracetamol and aspirin.

Drugs used to kill microorganisms are called antimicrobials or antibiotics.

Drugs used to relieve pain are called analgesics.

Drugs used to prevent pregnancy are called antifertility drugs.

Answer: To reduce fever.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the result when soap is used in hard water?
questions.solution:
Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium ions ($Ca^{2+}$ and $Mg^{2+}$).

When soap (which is typically a sodium or potassium salt of a long-chain fatty acid, such as sodium stearate) is added to hard water, these ions react with the soap molecules.

The sodium or potassium ions are replaced by calcium and magnesium ions, leading to the formation of insoluble calcium and magnesium salts of the fatty acids.

For example:
$2C_{17}H_{35}COONa + Ca^{2+} \rightarrow (C_{17}H_{35}COO)_2Ca \downarrow + 2Na^+$

These insoluble precipitates separate out from the water and are commonly known as scum.

Answer: Scum

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statement about enzyme is correct ?
options: They alter the equilibrium constant of reactions
They increase the activation energy of reactions
They are specific in their action
They are consumed in the reaction
questions.solution:
Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up the rate of biochemical reactions without being consumed in the process.

They do not alter the equilibrium constant of a reaction; they only help attain equilibrium faster.

They work by lowering the activation energy of the reaction, not increasing it.

Enzymes are highly specific in their action, meaning each enzyme typically catalyzes only one specific reaction or acts on a specific substrate.

Thus, the statement that they are specific in their action is correct.

Answer: They are specific in their action

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of drug the aspirin is?
questions.solution:
Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is a non-narcotic analgesic. It is widely used to relieve minor aches and pains, and also has antipyretic (fever-reducing) and anti-inflammatory properties.

Therefore, aspirin is classified as an analgesic.

Answer: Analgesic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a medicinal compound having amide linkage.
questions.solution:
Analysis of medicinal compounds with amide linkages:

Aspirin ($\mathrm{CH_3COOC_6 H_4 COOH}$) contains ester and carboxylic acid functional groups without amide functionality.

Methylsalicylate ($\mathrm{HOC_6 H_4 COOCH_3}$) features ester and phenolic hydroxyl groups, lacking an amide linkage.

Curcumin contains diketone and phenolic groups in its diarylheptanoid structure but no amide group.

Paracetamol ($\mathrm{HOC_6 H_4 NHCOCH_3}$), chemically N-(4-hydroxyphenyl)acetamide, contains the characteristic amide linkage ($-\mathrm{NHCO}^-$).

Only paracetamol possesses an amide functional group among the given compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is useful to extract analgesic and antimicrobial compounds?
questions.solution:
Analysis of medicinal plant properties: The identification focuses on plants containing compounds with both analgesic and antimicrobial effects.

Turmeric (A) contains curcumin, which demonstrates significant anti-inflammatory analgesic properties and antimicrobial activity against various pathogens.

Cinnamon (B) contains cinnamaldehyde, exhibiting strong antimicrobial effects and anti-inflammatory properties that contribute to analgesic applications.

Citrus fruit (C) primarily provides vitamin C and antioxidants, lacking the specific potent analgesic and antimicrobial compounds found in medicinal spices.

Clove (D) contains eugenol, a well-established analgesic compound particularly effective in dental applications, with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity.

The plants providing both analgesic and antimicrobial compounds are A, B, and D.

$\boxed{\text{A, B, D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify source of Eugenol from following.
questions.solution:
Eugenol is a phenylpropanoid compound prominently found in clove oil, constituting approximately $70\%$ to $90\%$ of its composition.

Among the options:

Clove is the primary commercial source of eugenol.

Indian gooseberry is noted for vitamin C content, not eugenol.

Wintergreen oil consists mainly of methyl salicylate.

Citrus fruits contain terpenes such as limonene.

Clove is therefore the correct source.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following metal nanoparticle is used for coating the filter material that acts as effective bacterial disinfectant?
questions.solution:
The metal nanoparticle used for coating filter material that acts as an effective bacterial disinfectant is silver.

Silver nanoparticles exhibit potent broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity through membrane disruption, metabolic interference, and reactive oxygen species generation. While nickel, gold, and copper nanoparticles show some antimicrobial properties, silver nanoparticles demonstrate superior efficacy and are the standard choice for bacterial disinfection in filtration applications.

The final result is $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following medicinal properties is exhibited by curcumin?
questions.solution:
Curcumin, a bioactive compound derived from turmeric, exhibits several well-documented medicinal properties:

It demonstrates analgesic effects by reducing pain, antiseptic action through inhibiting microbial growth, antioxidant capacity for neutralizing free radicals, and broad antimicrobial activity against bacteria, viruses, and fungi.

All listed properties—A, B, C, and D—are valid medicinal characteristics of curcumin.

$\boxed{A, B, C, D}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is formula of mustard gas?
questions.solution:
Mustard gas, systematically named bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide, has the molecular structure $\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{Cl}$.

Among the options, $\mathrm{COCl}_2$ corresponds to phosgene, $\mathrm{CCl}_3 \mathrm{NO}_2$ is chloropicrin, and $\mathrm{CCl}_2 \mathrm{F}_2$ is dichlorodifluoromethane—none match mustard gas.

The correct representation is therefore option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the source of gallic acid from following
questions.solution:
Gallic acid is a phenolic compound occurring naturally in certain plant species. Among the options:

Clove contains gallic acid alongside eugenol and other phenolics.

Wintergreen primarily contains methyl salicylate rather than gallic acid.

Citrus fruits are characterized by citric acid and ascorbic acid content, not gallic acid.

Indian gooseberry is particularly rich in gallic acid and hydrolyzable tannins.

The correct sources are therefore clove and Indian gooseberry.

$\boxed{A, D}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify an antiseptic compound from following.
questions.solution:
Antiseptics are chemical substances applied to living tissues to kill or inhibit microbial growth, preventing infection. Assessing the options:

Salvarsan is an arsenic-based chemotherapeutic agent for syphilis treatment, not an antiseptic. Thymol exhibits antiseptic and antifungal properties, commonly used in mouthwashes and topical applications. Sulphanilamide and chloramphenicol are systemic antibacterial antibiotics rather than antiseptics.

Given these pharmacological classifications, thymol qualifies as the antiseptic compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify false statement regarding aspirin.
options: It is obtained from salicylic acid.
It has fewer side effects than salicylic acid.
It has stomach irritating side effects.
questions.solution:
Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) contains an ester linkage ($\text{-OCOCH}_3$) rather than an amide group, making statement A incorrect.

Statement B is valid as aspirin is synthesized through acetylation of salicylic acid using acetic anhydride.

Statement C holds since aspirin was developed specifically to reduce the gastric irritation associated with salicylic acid.

Statement D is correct due to aspirin's inhibition of cyclooxygenase enzymes, which leads to stomach irritation.

The false statement is therefore $\boxed{A}$.

1. Morphology of nanomaterial
- FTIR does not provide information about morphology (shape, structure) of nanomaterials. Techniques like SEM or TEM are used for this. This is incorrect.
2. Absorption of functional group
- FTIR identifies functional groups by detecting characteristic absorption bands in the infrared region, such as those for $-\mathrm{OH},-\mathrm{CH},-\mathrm{NH},-\mathrm{CO}$, etc. This is correct.
3. Geometry of particles
- FTIR does not give information about particle geometry (e.g., spherical or cubic shapes). This is incorrect.
4. Particle size
- FTIR cannot determine particle size. Techniques like DLS (Dynamic Light Scattering) or electron microscopy are used for this. This is incorrect.

questions.q: Which element from following has positive electron gain enthalpy?
questions.solution:
Electron gain enthalpy is the enthalpy change when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom.

Halogens such as Chlorine, Bromine, and Iodine have a strong tendency to accept an electron to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, resulting in highly negative electron gain enthalpies.

Noble gases like Xenon have a completely filled and stable valence shell ($ns^2 np^6$). Adding an electron requires energy to place it in a higher energy principal quantum shell, overcoming interelectronic repulsions. Thus, Xenon has a positive electron gain enthalpy.

Answer: Xenon

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Identify increasing order of acidity for following diprotic acids in aqueous solutions.
questions.solution:
The given compounds are hydrides of Group 16 elements.

As we move down the group from Sulphur (S) to Tellurium (Te), the atomic size of the central atom increases.

This leads to an increase in the H-E bond length (where E is S, Se, Te) and a corresponding decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy.

Consequently, the H-E bond becomes weaker, making the release of an $\text{H}^{+}$ ion easier.

Therefore, the acidic strength increases down the group.

The increasing order of acidity is $\text{H}_2\text{S} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Se} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Te}$.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{S} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Se} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Te}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: What happens to the size of atoms in p-block elements when we move from left to right in the same period?
questions.solution:
As we move from left to right across a period, the atomic number increases, meaning the number of protons in the nucleus increases.

The additional electrons are added to the same principal shell, so the shielding effect remains almost constant.

This results in an increase in the effective nuclear charge ($Z_{eff}$), which pulls the valence electrons closer to the nucleus.

Consequently, the atomic size decreases from left to right in the same period.

Answer: Size decreases

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which group elements have the smallest atomic radii in their respective periods?
questions.solution:
In a given period, the atomic radius decreases from left to right as the effective nuclear charge increases.

This trend continues up to group 17 (halogens).

For group 18 (noble gases), the atomic radius is expressed as van der Waals radius since they do not form covalent bonds under normal conditions.

Since van der Waals radii are always larger than covalent radii, group 18 elements have larger radii than group 17 elements.

Thus, group 17 elements possess the smallest atomic radii in their respective periods.

Answer: group 17

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is most acidic in nature?
questions.solution:
The given compounds are hydrides of Group 16 elements.

As we move down the group from oxygen to tellurium, the atomic size of the central atom increases.

Due to the increase in atomic size, the bond length of the $\text{H-E}$ bond (where $\text{E}$ is $\text{O}$, $\text{S}$, $\text{Se}$, $\text{Te}$) increases, which leads to a decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy.

A lower bond dissociation enthalpy means the $\text{H-E}$ bond can be broken more easily to release an $\text{H}^+$ ion.

Therefore, the acidic character increases down the group.

The order of acidic strength is $\text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{H}_2\text{S} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Se} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Te}$.

Thus, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ is the most acidic compound among the given options.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following hydrides of Group $16$ elements has highest reducing property?
questions.solution:
The reducing property of Group $16$ hydrides depends on the ease with which they can release hydrogen atoms.

As we move down the group from oxygen to tellurium, the atomic size of the central atom increases.

This leads to an increase in the $E-\text{H}$ bond length ($E = \text{O, S, Se, Te}$) and a corresponding decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy.

Due to the lowest bond dissociation enthalpy among the given options, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ releases hydrogen most easily.

Therefore, the reducing property increases in the order: $\text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{H}_2\text{S} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Se} \lt \text{H}_2\text{Te}$.

Hence, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ has the highest reducing property.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which is the correct increasing order of atomic radii of $\mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{K}, \mathrm{Mg}, \mathrm{Rb}$ ?
questions.solution:
Atomic radius is determined by the number of electron shells and effective nuclear charge.

Periodic trends: Atomic radius decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge while electron shells remain constant. Atomic radius increases down a group as additional electron shells are added, outweighing the shielding effect of inner electrons.

The relative positions are: $\mathrm{Na}$ (Group 1, Period 3), $\mathrm{K}$ (Group 1, Period 4), $\mathrm{Mg}$ (Group 2, Period 3), and $\mathrm{Rb}$ (Group 1, Period 5).

Within Period 3, $\mathrm{Mg}$ lies to the right of $\mathrm{Na}$, giving $\mathrm{Mg} \lt \mathrm{Na}$.
Down Group 1, atomic radius increases: $\mathrm{Na} \lt \mathrm{K} \lt \mathrm{Rb}$.

Combining these inequalities yields the correct order: $\mathrm{Mg} \lt \mathrm{Na} \lt \mathrm{K} \lt \mathrm{Rb}$.

Only option B matches this ordering, making it the correct choice.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.q: Which from following is a CORRECT decreasing order of ionisation enthalpy for different elements?
questions.solution:
The ionisation enthalpy decreases down the group due to increase in the atomic size.
Therefore, ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Ne}$ is more than that of Ar.
Across a period ionisation enthalpy increases with increase of atomic number.
Therefore, ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{S}, \mathrm{Cl}$ and $\mathrm{Ar}$ is in the order: $\mathrm{S} \lt  \mathrm{Cl} \lt  \mathrm{Ar}$.
Hence, the correct decreasing order of ionisation enthalpy for the given elements is:
$\mathrm{Ne} \gt \mathrm{Ar} \gt \mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{S}$

questions.q: Which block element from following are known as transition elements?
questions.solution: Transition elements (also known as transition metals) are elements that have partially filled $d$ orbitals. IUPAC defines transition elements as an element having a $\mathrm{d}$ subshell that is partially filled with electrons, or an element that has the ability to form stable cations with an incompletely filled d orbital. In general, any element which corresponds to the d-block of the modern periodic table (which consists of groups 3-12) is considered to be a transition element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following coordinate complexes is heteroleptic?
questions.solution:
A homoleptic complex has only one type of ligand attached to the central metal atom or ion.

A heteroleptic complex has more than one type of ligand attached to the central metal atom or ion.

Pentacarbonyliron(0) is $[Fe(CO)_5]$, which has only $CO$ ligands (homoleptic).

Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is $[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]$, which has two different types of ligands, $NH_3$ and $NO_2^{-}$ (heteroleptic).

Tetraamminecopper(II) ion is $[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$, which has only $NH_3$ ligands (homoleptic).

Tetracyanonickelate(II) ion is $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$, which has only $CN^{-}$ ligands (homoleptic).

Thus, Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) is the heteroleptic complex.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following complex is neutral?
questions.solution:
A neutral complex is a coordination compound that does not have an overall electrical charge and does not dissociate into ions in solution.

$\text{K}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]$ is an ionic complex that dissociates into $3\text{K}^+$ and $[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]^{3-}$ ions.

$[\text{Zn(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ is a cationic complex with a $+2$ charge.

$[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ is a cationic complex with a $+2$ charge.

$[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$ has no overall charge and no counter ions, making it a neutral complex.

Answer: $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the coordination number of central metal ion in $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$ complex ?
questions.solution:
The given complex is $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$.

The ligand 'en' stands for ethylenediamine, which is a bidentate ligand. This means each 'en' molecule coordinates to the central metal ion through two donor nitrogen atoms.

Since there are three 'en' ligands attached to the central cobalt ion, the total number of coordinate bonds formed is $3 \times 2 = 6$.

Therefore, the coordination number of the central metal ion is $6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the formula of Bis(ethylenediamine)dithiocyanatoplatinum(IV)ion from following.
questions.solution:
The central metal ion is Platinum in the $+4$ oxidation state, denoted as $\text{Pt}^{4+}$.

The ligands are:
Bis(ethylenediamine) \rightarrow two ethylenediamine (en) molecules. Since 'en' is a neutral ligand, its charge contribution is $0$.
dithiocyanato \rightarrow two thiocyanato ($\text{SCN}^{-}$) ions. Each $\text{SCN}^{-}$ has a charge of $-1$, so their total charge contribution is $-2$.

The net charge on the complex ion is calculated as:
Net charge = Charge of Pt + Charge of $2(\text{en})$ + Charge of $2(\text{SCN}^{-})$
Net charge = $+4 + 0 + 2(-1) = +2$

Writing the formula by placing the central metal atom followed by the ligands in alphabetical order inside the coordination sphere, we get:
$[\text{Pt(en)}_2(\text{SCN})_2]^{2+}$

Answer: $[\text{Pt(en)}_2(\text{SCN})_2]^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following complexes is an example of $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ type distereoisomers ?
questions.solution:
The general formula $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ represents an octahedral complex with one central metal atom $\text{M}$, four identical ligands $\text{A}$, and two different ligands $\text{B}$ and $\text{C}$.

Analyzing the given options:

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)(\text{H}_2\text{O})\,\text{Cl}_2]$ is of the type $\text{MA}_2\text{BC}$ (where $\text{A} = \text{Cl}$, $\text{B} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{C} = \text{H}_2\text{O}$).

$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{ClBr}]^{2+}$ is of the type $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$, $\text{C} = \text{Br}$).

$\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\,\text{Cl}_2$ is of the type $\text{MA}_2\text{B}_2$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$).

$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is of the type $\text{MA}_4\text{B}_2$ (where $\text{A} = \text{NH}_3$, $\text{B} = \text{Cl}$).

Thus, $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4\,\text{ClBr}]^{2+}$ is the example of $\text{MA}_4\text{BC}$ type complex, which exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms), and these geometrical isomers are diastereoisomers.

questions.q: Which from following coordinate complexes contains neutral ligand ?
questions.solution:
Pentacarbonyliron (0) has the formula $[Fe(CO)_5]$. The ligand present is carbonyl (CO), which is a neutral molecule.

Hexacyanoferrate (II) ion has the formula $[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}$. The ligand is cyanide ($CN^-$), which is an anionic ligand.

Trioxalatocobaltate (III) ion has the formula $[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}$. The ligand is oxalate ($C_2O_4^{2-}$), which is an anionic ligand.

Sodium hexanitrocobaltate (III) has the formula $Na_3[Co(NO_2)_6]$. The ligand is nitro ($NO_2^-$), which is an anionic ligand.

Therefore, only pentacarbonyliron (0) contains a neutral ligand.

Answer: Pentacarbonyliron (0)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of cobalt in $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ ?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of cobalt be $x$.

Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is a neutral ligand, so its charge is $0$.

The sum of the oxidation states of all atoms in the complex ion is equal to the net charge on the ion.

$x + 6(0) = +3$

$x = +3$

The oxidation state of cobalt in $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of hybridization is found in $[\text{Ni}(\text{Cl})_4]^{2-}$?
questions.solution:
The given complex is $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$.

Let the oxidation state of Ni be $x$.

$x + 4(-1) = -2 \Rightarrow x = +2$

The electronic configuration of neutral Ni is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of Ni$^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$.

Cl$^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so it does not cause the pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals of Ni$^{2+}$.

To accommodate the four electron pairs donated by the four Cl$^{-}$ ligands, the Ni$^{2+}$ ion undergoes hybridization using one $4s$ and three $4p$ empty orbitals.

Therefore, the hybridization involved is $sp^3$, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry.

Answer: $sp^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct increasing order of ligand field strength ?
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the ligands are arranged in the increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) or ligand field strength as follows:

$I^{-} \lt Br^{-} \lt SCN^{-} \lt Cl^{-} \lt S^{2-} \lt F^{-} \lt OH^{-} \lt C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^{-} \lt EDTA^{4-} \lt NH_3 \lt en \lt CN^{-} \lt CO$

From the given options, the correct increasing order of ligand field strength is:

$C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt EDTA \lt en$

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{EDTA} \lt \text{en}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is EAN for metal ion in $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ ?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of iron (Fe) is $26$.

Let the oxidation state of Fe in $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ be $x$.

$x + 6(-1) = -3$

$x = +3$

The formula for Effective Atomic Number (EAN) is:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{Oxidation state} + 2 \times (\text{Coordination number})$

$\text{EAN} = 26 - 3 + 2 \times 6$

$\text{EAN} = 23 + 12 = 35$

Answer: $35$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find EAN of Fe in $\text{Fe(CO)}_5$
questions.solution:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) is calculated using the formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{Oxidation State} + 2 \times \text{Coordination Number}$

For $\text{Fe(CO)}_5$:

Atomic number of Fe ($Z$) = $26$

Oxidation state of Fe = $0$ (since CO is a neutral ligand)

Coordination number = $5$

$\text{EAN} = 26 - 0 + 2 \times 5$

$\text{EAN} = 26 + 10 = 36$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a ligand with highest field strength among the following.
questions.solution:
According to the spectrochemical series, the arrangement of ligands in the increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) values is:

$I^- \lt Br^- \lt SCN^- \lt Cl^- \lt S^{2-} \lt F^- \lt OH^- \lt C_2O_4^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^- \lt edta^{4-} \lt NH_3 \lt en \lt CN^- \lt CO$

From the given options, the order of field strength is $S^{2-} \lt H_2O \lt NCS^- \lt NH_3$.

Thus, $\text{NH}_3$ has the highest field strength.

Answer: $\text{NH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a ligand with lowest field strength among the following.
questions.solution:
The field strength of ligands is determined by the spectrochemical series, which arranges ligands in order of increasing field strength.

The spectrochemical series is given as:
$\text{I}^- \lt \text{Br}^- \lt \text{SCN}^- \lt \text{Cl}^- \lt \text{S}^{2-} \lt \text{F}^- \lt \text{OH}^- \lt \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{NCS}^- \lt \text{edta}^{4-} \lt \text{NH}_3 \lt \text{en} \lt \text{CN}^- \lt \text{CO}$

Comparing the given ligands based on the series, the order of field strength is:
$\text{Br}^- \lt \text{OH}^- \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{en}$

Therefore, $\text{Br}^-$ has the lowest field strength among the given options.

Answer: $\text{Br}^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the EAN of metal ion in $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ ?
questions.solution:
The effective atomic number (EAN) is calculated using the formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{O.S.} + 2 \times \text{C.N.}$

For the complex $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$:
Atomic number of copper ($Z$) = $29$
Oxidation state of copper ($\text{O.S.}$) = $+2$
Coordination number ($\text{C.N.}$) = $4$

Substituting the values:

$\text{EAN} = 29 - 2 + 2 \times 4$

$\text{EAN} = 27 + 8 = 35$

Answer: $35$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the ionization isomer of $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}(\text{NO}_2)]\,\text{Cl}$ from the following.
questions.solution:
Ionization isomerism occurs when a ligand inside the coordination sphere is exchanged with an anion outside the coordination sphere (counter ion), resulting in a complex that yields different ions in solution.

In the given complex $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}(\text{NO}_2)]\,\text{Cl}$, the counter ion is $\text{Cl}^-$ and the ligands are $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{Cl}^-$, and $\text{NO}_2^-$.

By exchanging the $\text{NO}_2^-$ ligand inside the coordination sphere with the $\text{Cl}^-$ counter ion outside, we get the ionization isomer $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}_2]\,(\text{NO}_2)$.

The original complex yields $\text{Cl}^-$ ions in aqueous solution, whereas its ionization isomer yields $\text{NO}_2^-$ ions.

Answer: $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}_2]\,(\text{NO}_2)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify oxidation state of cobalt ion in the complex, $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]\text{SO}_4$ .
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of cobalt be $x$.

The given coordination compound dissociates into a complex cation $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Br}]^{2+}$ and a sulfate anion $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$.

The overall charge on the complex cation is $+2$.

Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is a neutral ligand with an oxidation state of $0$, and bromide ($\text{Br}^-$) has an oxidation state of $-1$.

Summing the oxidation states of the central metal atom and the ligands:

$x + 5(0) + (-1) = +2$

$x - 1 = +2$

$x = +3$

The oxidation state of cobalt in the complex is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the number of unpaired electrons present and geometry respectively of $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ complex.
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of Co in $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is $+3$.

The electronic configuration of Co is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of Co$^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.

Since $\text{NH}_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for Co$^{3+}$, pairing of electrons takes place in the $3d$ subshell.

All $6$ electrons pair up in the inner $d$-orbitals, leaving two $3d$ orbitals empty.

The number of unpaired electrons is $0$.

The complex undergoes $d^2sp^3$ hybridization, resulting in an octahedral geometry.

Answer: 0, octahedral

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ligands splits d orbitals to maximum level?
questions.solution:
The splitting of d orbitals depends on the strength of the ligand, which is given by the spectrochemical series.

The order of ligand strength for the given options is $\text{Cl}^- \lt \text{H}_2\text{O} \lt \text{NH}_3 \lt \text{CN}^-$.

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is the strongest field ligand among the given options, it causes the maximum crystal field splitting of the d orbitals.

Answer: $\text{CN}^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the complex having the highest number of unpaired electrons from following.
questions.solution: In $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$, Co is in $+3$ oxidation state with $3d^6$ configuration. Since NH_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for Co$^{3+}$, pairing of electrons takes place resulting in $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ configuration. Number of unpaired electrons $= 0$. \\  \\ In $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, Co is in $+3$ oxidation state with $3d^6$ configuration. F$^-$ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs. The configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$. Number of unpaired electrons $= 4$. \\  \\ In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in $+2$ oxidation state with $3d^8$ configuration. Cl$^-$ is a weak field ligand, forming a tetrahedral complex with $e^4 t_2^4$ configuration. Number of unpaired electrons $= 2$. \\  \\ In $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$, Ni is in $+2$ oxidation state with $3d^8$ configuration. CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, forming a square planar complex where all electrons are paired. Number of unpaired electrons $= 0$. \\  \\ Thus, $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ has the highest number of unpaired electrons. \\  \\ Answer: $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the coordination complex, Potassium hexacyanoferrate(II), the central atom/ion acts as,
questions.solution:
The coordination complex is Potassium hexacyanoferrate(II), which is $K_4[Fe(CN)_6]$.

The central metal ion is $Fe^{2+}$ and the ligands are $CN^{-}$ ions.

In the formation of a coordination complex, the central metal ion accepts electron pairs from the ligands to form coordinate covalent bonds.

According to the Lewis acid-base theory, an electron pair acceptor is a Lewis acid.

Therefore, the central atom/ion acts as a Lewis acid.

Answer: Lewis acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The sum of coordination number and oxidation number of M in $[\text{M(en)}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4]\text{Cl}$ is
questions.solution:
In the given complex $[\text{M(en)}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4]\text{Cl}$, the ligands present inside the coordination sphere are ethylenediamine (en) and oxalate ($\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$).

Both ethylenediamine and oxalate are bidentate ligands.
Coordination number of M = $2 \times 2$ (from en) + $1 \times 2$ (from oxalate) = $4 + 2 = 6$.

To find the oxidation number of M, let its oxidation state be $x$.
The charge on ethylenediamine is $0$, the charge on oxalate is $-2$, and the charge on the chloride ion outside the coordination sphere is $-1$.
Equating the sum of oxidation states to the overall charge of the neutral compound:
$x + 2(0) + 1(-2) + 1(-1) = 0$
$x - 3 = 0$
$x = +3$

The oxidation number of M is $3$.

Sum of coordination number and oxidation number = $6 + 3 = 9$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$ ?
options: It is $sp^3 d^2$ hybridised and tetrahedral.
It is $d^2 sp^3$ hybridised and octahedral.
It is $dsp^2$ hybridised and square planar
It is $sp^3 d^2$ hybridised and octahedral.
questions.solution:
The given complex is $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$.

Let the oxidation state of Mn be $x$.

$x + 6(-1) = -3 \Rightarrow x = +3$

The electronic configuration of Mn is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$.

Since $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals against Hund's rule. The four electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals, leaving two $e_g$ orbitals empty.

These two empty $3d$ orbitals, along with one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals, undergo $d^2sp^3$ hybridization.

The geometry corresponding to $d^2sp^3$ hybridization is octahedral.

Answer: It is $d^2 sp^3$ hybridised and octahedral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following comparisons is correct for $\Delta_0$ of the following complexes?
I- $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$
II- $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$
III- $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$
IV- $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3+}$
questions.solution:
The crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_0$) depends on several factors, including the oxidation state of the central metal ion and the nature of the ligands.

1. Oxidation state of the metal ion: For the same metal and ligand, $\Delta_0$ increases with an increase in the oxidation state of the central metal ion. This is because a higher charge on the metal ion draws the ligands closer, leading to greater repulsion and a larger splitting of the d-orbitals.
In complex I, Co is in the $+2$ oxidation state: $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$.
In complex II, Co is in the $+3$ oxidation state: $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$.
Therefore, $\Delta_0$ of II > I, which means $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$ is a correct comparison.

2. Nature of the ligand: Strong field ligands cause a larger splitting than weak field ligands. $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, whereas $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand.
Thus, $\Delta_0$ of $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3+}$ (IV) is significantly greater than that of $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ (II) and $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ (III). The comparison $\text{IV} \lt \text{II}$ is incorrect.

3. The comparison $\text{II} \lt \text{I}$ is incorrect based on the oxidation state rule.

Thus, the most appropriate and direct standard comparison is $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$.

Answer: $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of color is observed when a compound absorbs red coloured light?
questions.solution:
When a compound absorbs a specific color of light from the visible spectrum, the color it exhibits (observed color) is the complementary color of the absorbed light.

According to the complementary color wheel, the complementary color of red is blue-green (or cyan). For example, hydrated copper(II) complexes absorb red light and appear blue.

Since blue-green is not explicitly given in the options, blue is the most appropriate and closest choice.

Answer: Blue

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following sets of ligands does NOT contain ambident ligand in it?
questions.solution:
An ambidentate ligand is a ligand that has more than one type of donor atom and can bind to the central metal ion through any of these different donor atoms.

Examples of ambidentate ligands include $\text{NO}_2^-$ (which can bind through N or O) and $\text{NCS}^-$ (which can bind through N or S).

Checking the given options:
Option 1 contains $\text{NO}_2^-$ and $\text{NCS}^-$, both of which are ambidentate ligands.
Option 2 contains $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ (binds only through O), ethylene diamine (binds only through N), and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (binds only through O). None of these are ambidentate ligands.
Option 3 contains $\text{NO}_2^-$, which is an ambidentate ligand.
Option 4 contains $\text{NCS}^-$, which is an ambidentate ligand.

Therefore, the set containing $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$, ethylene diamine, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ does not contain any ambidentate ligand.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an ambident ligand ?
questions.solution:
An ambident ligand is a monodentate ligand that contains more than one coordinating atom and can bind to the central metal ion through different atoms.

Ethylene diamine is a bidentate ligand coordinating through two nitrogen atoms.

$\text{Cl}^-$ is a monodentate ligand coordinating only through the chlorine atom.

EDTA is a hexadentate ligand coordinating through two nitrogen and four oxygen atoms.

$\text{SCN}^-$ (thiocyanate ion) can coordinate to the central metal ion either through the sulfur atom (thiocyanato) or through the nitrogen atom (isothiocyanato). Therefore, it is an ambident ligand.

Answer: SCN

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a complex compound, central metal ion is
questions.solution:
In a complex compound, the central metal ion accepts one or more electron pairs from the surrounding ligands to form coordinate covalent bonds.

According to the Lewis theory of acids and bases, an electron pair acceptor is defined as a Lewis acid, while an electron pair donor is defined as a Lewis base.

Therefore, the central metal ion acts as a Lewis acid.

Answer: Lewis acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the hybridization in central metal of $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$ complex.
questions.solution:
In $[Fe(CO)_5]$, the central metal atom is $Fe$ and its oxidation state is $0$.

The ground state electronic configuration of $Fe$ is $[Ar] 3d^6 4s^2$.

$CO$ is a strong field ligand, which causes the pairing of electrons.

The two $4s$ electrons shift to the $3d$ subshell and pair up, resulting in a $3d^8$ configuration. Four $3d$ orbitals are completely filled and one $3d$ orbital is left empty.

To accommodate the five electron pairs from the five $CO$ ligands, one $3d$, one $4s$, and three $4p$ orbitals hybridize.

Therefore, the hybridization is $dsp^3$.

questions.q: Which from following complexes contains anionic ligand?
questions.solution:
To identify the complex containing an anionic ligand, examine the charge characteristics of each ligand in the coordination sphere.
In the tetraamminecopper(II) ion $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}_3)4]^{2+}$, the ammine ligand $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is neutral.
The pentaammineaquacobalt(III) iodide complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)5(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})]^{3+}$ contains neutral ammine and aqua ligands $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.
In tetracyanonickelate(II) ion $[\mathrm{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$, the cyano ligand $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ carries a $-1$ charge, confirming its anionic character.
Pentacarbonyliron(0) $[\mathrm{Fe(CO)}_{5}]$ features the neutral carbonyl ligand $\mathrm{CO}$.
The tetracyanonickelate(II) ion is the only complex with an anionic ligand.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following complexes does NOT obey EAN rule?
questions.solution:
Effective Atomic Number analysis determines which complex violates the noble gas electron count rule.

The EAN equals the sum of metal valence electrons and ligand-donated electrons, aiming for Kr (36), Xe (54), or Rn (86). For monodentate ligands: $\text{EAN} = Z_{\text{metal}} - \text{oxidation state} + 2 \times \text{number of ligands}$.

For $\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6^{3+}$: Co atomic number 27, oxidation state +3 gives 24 valence electrons; 6 $\mathrm{NH}_3$ donate 12 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 24 + 12 = 36$, satisfying the rule.

For $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CO})_6$: Cr atomic number 24, oxidation state 0 gives 24 valence electrons; 6 CO donate 12 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 24 + 12 = 36$, satisfying the rule.

For $\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4^{2+}$: Zn atomic number 30, oxidation state +2 gives 28 valence electrons; 4 $\mathrm{NH}_3$ donate 8 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 28 + 8 = 36$, satisfying the rule.

For $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4^{2+}$: Cu atomic number 29, oxidation state +2 gives 27 valence electrons; 4 $\mathrm{NH}_3$ donate 8 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 27 + 8 = 35 \neq 36$, violating the rule.

The complex that does not obey the EAN rule is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the EAN of Fe in $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3-}$ ?
questions.solution:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) of Fe in $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}$ is determined using the formula:

$\mathrm{EAN} = Z - \mathrm{OS} + 2 \times \mathrm{CN}$
where $Z$ is the atomic number, $\mathrm{OS}$ is the oxidation state, and $\mathrm{CN}$ is the coordination number.

For iron, $Z = 26$. The oxidation state $x$ satisfies $x + 6 \times (-1) = -3$, yielding $x = +3$. The complex contains six cyanide ligands, so $\mathrm{CN} = 6$.

Substituting these values: $\mathrm{EAN} = 26 - 3 + 2 \times 6 = 35$.

Final answer: $\boxed{35}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the total number of moles of donor atoms present in one mole $\mathrm{K}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]$ complex.
questions.solution:
The complex $\mathrm{K}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]$ contains the coordination ion $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{4-}$ with iron as the central metal atom coordinated by six cyanide ligands.

Cyanide is monodentate with carbon serving as the donor atom, contributing one donor site per ligand.

Since there are six ligands, each providing one donor atom, one mole of the complex contains exactly six moles of donor atoms.

$\boxed{6}$

Ligand field strength is determined by the spectrochemical series: $\mathrm{I}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Br}^{-} \lt \mathrm{S}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{SCN}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \lt \mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-} \lt \mathrm{F}^{-} \lt \mathrm{OH}^{-} \lt \mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{NCS}^{-} \lt \mathrm{EDTA}^{4-} \lt \mathrm{NH}_{3} \lt \mathrm{en} \lt \mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-} \lt \mathrm{CN}^{-} \lt \mathrm{CO}$

Among the options, $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is a strong field ligand, $\mathrm{NC}^{-}$ is a very strong field ligand (similar to $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$), $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, and $\mathrm{CO}$ is the strongest ligand in the series. The weakest is $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

In contrast, triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) and pentaammineaquacobalt(III) iodide involve neutral or cationic cobalt complexes, lacking the -ate suffix.

Only sodium hexanitrocobaltate(III) contains a complex anion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the EAN of Zn in $\left[\mathrm{Zn}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\right]^{2+}$ ?
questions.solution:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) is calculated as $\text{EAN} = Z - s + 2n$, where $Z$ is the atomic number, $s$ is the oxidation state, and $n$ is the coordination number.

For the complex ion $\left[\mathrm{Zn}\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}$, zinc has atomic number $Z = 30$.

Ammonia is a neutral ligand, and the complex has a $+2$ charge, giving zinc an oxidation state of $s = +2$.

With four ammonia ligands, the coordination number is $n = 4$.

Substituting into the formula:
$\text{EAN} = 30 - 2 + (2 \times 4) = 28 + 8 = 36$

The Effective Atomic Number of zinc in this complex is therefore $\boxed{36}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct increasing order of field strength of ligands form following.
questions.solution:
The spectrochemical series ranks ligands by crystal field splitting strength $\Delta$. The general increasing order for common ligands is:

$\mathrm{I}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Br}^{-} \lt \mathrm{S}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{SCN}^{-} \text{ (S-bonded)} \lt \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \lt \mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-} \lt \mathrm{F}^{-} \lt \mathrm{OH}^{-} \lt \mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{NCS}^{-} \text{ (N-bonded)} \lt \mathrm{EDTA}^{4-} \lt \mathrm{NH}_{3} \lt \mathrm{en} \lt \mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-} \lt \mathrm{PPh}_{3} \lt \mathrm{CN}^{-} \lt \mathrm{CO}$

Among the given ligands, $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is the weakest due to its large size and strong $\pi$-donation, while $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ is the strongest owing to oxygen's high electronegativity and effective $\sigma$-donation. Chloride $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ is stronger than iodide but weaker than hydroxide. Sulfide $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$, with its higher charge, typically exhibits intermediate strength.

Comparing the options:

A) $\mathrm{Cl}^{-} \lt \mathrm{I}^{-} \lt \mathrm{S}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{OH}^{-}$ is invalid since $\mathrm{I}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$.
B) $\mathrm{I}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \lt \mathrm{S}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{OH}^{-}$ correctly starts with the weakest and ends with the strongest ligand.
C) $\mathrm{OH}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \lt \mathrm{I}^{-} \lt \mathrm{S}^{2-}$ incorrectly positions $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ as weakest.
D) $\mathrm{S}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{OH}^{-} \lt \mathrm{I}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ is invalid due to multiple misorderings.

The only valid increasing order is B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of unpaired electrons in $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ complex?
questions.solution:
The cobalt ion in $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ has an oxidation state of +3, giving it the configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^6$.

Ammonia is a strong field ligand that causes significant crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes. This favors electron pairing in the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals before occupying $e_g$ orbitals.

All six electrons pair completely in the three $t_{2g}$ orbitals: $\uparrow\downarrow \uparrow\downarrow \uparrow\downarrow$

There are zero unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is EAN of Co in $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ ?
questions.solution:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) for cobalt in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is calculated using the standard formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{Oxidation State} + 2 \times (\text{Number of Ligands} \times \text{Denticity})$

Cobalt has atomic number $Z = 27$. In this complex, with six neutral $\mathrm{NH}_3$ ligands and an overall +3 charge, cobalt's oxidation state is +3.

Each $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is monodentate, donating one electron pair, contributing $6 \times 2 = 12$ electrons.
Substituting values: $\text{EAN} = 27 - 3 + 12 = 36$.

The Effective Atomic Number is $\boxed{36}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a lowest field strength ligand from following.
questions.solution:
The spectrochemical series establishes ligand strength through crystal field splitting magnitude $\Delta$.

Standard ordering of increasing strength: $\mathrm{I}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Br}^{-} \lt \mathrm{S}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{SCN}^{-} \lt \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \lt \mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-} \lt \mathrm{F}^{-} \lt \mathrm{OH}^{-} \lt \mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} \lt \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{NCS}^{-} \lt \mathrm{EDTA}^{4-} \lt \mathrm{NH}_{3} \lt \mathrm{en} \lt \mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-} \lt \mathrm{CN}^{-} \lt \mathrm{CO}$.

Among the options, $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ initiates the series with minimal splitting, $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ exhibits moderate strength, while $\mathrm{en}$ and $\mathrm{CO}$ represent progressively stronger field ligands due to $\pi$-acceptor capability and chelation.

$\mathrm{I}^{-}$ yields the weakest crystal field.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following ligands has highest field strength?
questions.solution:
The field strength of ligands follows the spectrochemical series, which ranks ligands by their ability to induce crystal field splitting ($\Delta$). Among the given ligands, carbonyl ($\mathrm{CO}$) is a strong-field ligand positioned near the high-splitting end of the series.

The approximate order for these ligands is $\mathrm{OH}^{-} \lt \mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} \approx \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{CO}$.

Since CO produces the largest crystal field splitting, it has the highest field strength.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is EAN of metal ion in hexacyanoferrate (II) ion?
questions.solution:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) for the metal ion in $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$ is determined through systematic analysis of its electronic configuration.

The central metal ion is iron with atomic number $Z = 26$. The oxidation state calculation yields $x + 6 \times (-1) = -4$, resulting in $x = +2$ for $\text{Fe}^{2+}$.

The number of electrons in $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $26 - 2 = 24$. Each cyanide ligand donates 2 electrons, with 6 ligands contributing $6 \times 2 = 12$ electrons.

EAN $= 24 + 12 = 36$

Therefore, the Effective Atomic Number is $\boxed{36}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the coordination number of central metal ion if it forms octahedral complex?

The coordination number represents the count of ligand donor atoms bonded directly to the central metal ion.

In an octahedral complex, the metal ion is surrounded by six ligand donor atoms positioned at the vertices of an octahedron.

$\therefore$ The coordination number is $6$.

Option B is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry

Neutral ligand identification

A neutral ligand donates an electron pair without carrying net charge. Among the options:

Carbonyl ($\mathrm{CO}$) is neutral, as in $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ or $\mathrm{Fe(CO)_5}$.
Sulphato ($\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$), oxalato ($\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}}$), and bromo ($\mathrm{Br-}$) are anionic.

Only carbonyl qualifies as neutral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of hybridisation is present in square planar geometry of complex $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$
questions.solution:
Oxidation state of nickel: With CN- ligands (charge -1) and overall charge -2, $x + 4(-1) = -2$ yields $x = +2$, so Ni2+ is present.

Electron configuration: Ni atom is [Ar] 4s2 3d8, so Ni2+ is [Ar] 3d8.

Effect of ligand field: Cyanide is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of electrons in d-orbitals.

The d8 configuration with pairing renders one 3d orbital empty. Hybridization involves this empty d orbital, the empty 4s orbital, and two empty 4p orbitals, forming $sp^2d$ hybridization.

This hybridization is consistent with the square planar geometry of the complex. The answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of moles of silver chloride precipitated when excess silver nitrate is treated with one mole of pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride?
questions.solution:
Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) chloride features a $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ center coordinated to five neutral $\mathrm{NH_3}$ ligands and one $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$ ligand, giving the complex ion $[\mathrm{Co(NH_3)5CO3}]^+$ with charge $+3 + 0 - 2 = +1$.

Silver nitrate test for ionic chloride: Each formula unit contains one $\mathrm{Cl-}$ ion, producing one mole of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ precipitate per mole of compound.

$E = \frac{\text{mass of AgCl}}{\text{molar mass of AgCl}} = \frac{2.87\,\text{g}}{143.32\,\text{g/mol}} = 0.02\,\text{mol}$

Since one mole of compound yields one mole of $\mathrm{AgCl}$, the moles of silver chloride precipitated are $\mathbf{0.02\,\text{mol}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following cations forms least stable complex with same ligand?
questions.solution:
Complex stability depends on cation charge, ionic radius, and electronic configuration. All given cations ($\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$) share a +2 charge, so differentiation arises from size and crystal field effects.

Ionic radii for high-spin, octahedral ions are approximately $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$: 73 pm, $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$: 74.5 pm, $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$: 78 pm, $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$: 95 pm. Larger radii correlate with lower charge density and weaker ligand attraction.

Electronic configurations yield crystal field stabilization energies: $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ($d^6$), $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ ($d^7$), and $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ ($d^9$) all benefit from CFSE, but $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$) gains no stabilization.

The Irving-Williams series orders stability as $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Fe}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Co}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Ni}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Cu}^{2+} \gt \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$, yet $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$ lies outside this trend due to its filled $d$-shell.

Combining larger size and absence of CFSE, $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$ forms the least stable complex.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following cations will form most stable complex with same ligand?
questions.solution:
The stability of coordination complexes formed by divalent transition metal ions follows the Irving-Williams series: $Mn^{2+} \lt Fe^{2+} \lt Co^{2+} \lt Ni^{2+} \lt Cu^{2+} \gt Zn^{2+}$. This trend results from decreasing ionic radii and increasing effective nuclear charge across the period, enhanced by crystal field stabilization effects.

Among the given ions, $Cu^{2+}$ exhibits the highest stability due to maximum crystal field stabilization energy among first-row transition metals and Jahn-Teller distortion effects.

Final Answer: $\boxed{A}$

questions.q: Identify the correct decreasing order of stability of complexes formed by divalent metal ions with same ligand.
questions.solution:
Stability in the Irving-Williams series: For first-row transition metal divalent ions, complex stability follows $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Fe}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Co}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Ni}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Cu}^{2+} \gt \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$, so $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} \gt \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$.

Comparison of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$: Both have zero crystal field stabilization energy, but $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ has a smaller ionic radius (83 pm) than $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$ (95 pm), resulting in higher charge density and stronger ligand interactions. Complexes of type $\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{BC}$ feature a central metal atom (M) with two identical monodentate ligands (A) and two different monodentate ligands (B and C).

Option A: $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2\mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$ uses bidentate ethylenediamine ligands, making it type $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA})_2\mathrm{B}_2$, not $\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{BC}$.

Option B: $\left[\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})\mathrm{Cl}_2\right]$ is square planar. Assigning $\mathrm{Cl}$ as A, $\mathrm{NH}_3$ as B, and $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ as C gives the exact $\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{BC}$ formulation. This geometry produces cis-trans diastereoisomers due to the relative positions of B and C when the two A ligands are either adjacent or opposite.

Option C: $\mathrm{Pt}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$ is type $\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{B}_2$, lacking a distinct third ligand.

Option D: $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$ is octahedral and type $\mathrm{MA}_4\mathrm{B}_2$.

Only option B satisfies the $\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{BC}$ criteria and exhibits diastereoisomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is effective atomic number of cobalt in $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ if $\operatorname{Co}(Z=27) ?$
questions.solution:
The total number of electrons present with a central metal atom or ion in a coordination complex plus the electrons donated by the ligands is known as Effective Atomic Number (EAN).
The formula to calculate the EAN is as follows.
Effective atomic number $=\mathrm{Z}-\mathrm{O} . \mathrm{N}+2 \mathrm{C} . \mathrm{N}\mathrm{Z}=$ Atomic number
O.N= Oxidation number
C. $\mathrm{N}=$ Coordination number

\begin{aligned}
& {\left[\mathrm{C}_0\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{3+} \quad \mathrm{C}_0^{3+}} \\
& \mathrm{Z}=27 . \mathrm{O} \cdot \mathrm{N} .=3 . \quad \text { C.N. }=6 \\
& \mathrm{EAN}=27-3+2 \times 6=36
\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify neutral complex from following.
questions.solution:
Identifying a neutral complex requires calculating the total charge of each coordination entity. The overall charge is the sum of the central metal's oxidation state and the charges from all ligands.

For tetracyanonickelate(II) ion, the nickel center is Ni2+ and four CN– ligands contribute –4, yielding a –2 charge: $+2 + 4 \times (-1) = -2$, an anion.

Sodium hexafluoroaluminate(III) contains the complex ion [AlF6]3–, as aluminum is +3 and six F– ligands contribute –6: $+3 + 6 \times (-1) = -3$, an anion.

Triamminetrinitrocobalt(III) has cobalt at +3, three neutral NH3 ligands, and three NO2– ligands contributing –3: $+3 + 3 \times 0 + 3 \times (-1) = 0$, a neutral complex.

Tetraamminecopper(II) ion features Cu2+ and four neutral NH3 ligands: $+2 + 4 \times 0 = +2$, a cation.

$\boxed{C}$ is the neutral complex.
