questions.q: In the electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride with inert electrodes the products obtained at anode and cathode respectively are
questions.solution:
In the electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride with inert electrodes, the products obtained at anode and cathode respectively are Cl2 and H2.
The solution contains four ions Na+,Cl-,H+,OH.
Following reaction takes place:
At cathode
Na+aq+e-→Nas;                              ENa+/Na-=-2.71V2H2Ol+2e-→H2g+2O-Haq;                                        EH2O/H2o=-0.83V
At anode
2Cl-aq→Cl2g+2e-;ECl-/Cl2o=-1.36V2H2O2l→Og+4H+aq+4e-;                                                                  EH2O/O2o=-1.23 V
EH2O/H2o>ENa+/Nao. is formed at cathode.
Whereas EH2O/O2o>ECl-/Cl2o. So, formed at anode.

questions.q: The molar conductivities at infinite dilution for sodium acetate, HCI and NaCI are 91 S <math><mi>c</mi><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> <math><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><msup><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>425.9</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi>S</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi>c</mi><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><msup><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mn>126.4</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi>S</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi>c</mi><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>m</mi><mi>o</mi><msup><mrow><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> respectively. The molar conductivity of acetic acid at infinite dilution is
questions.solution:
Key Idea kohlrausch law of independent migration of ions can be used to calculate Δmo for weak electrolyte such as acetic acid.
Given, Δm(NaAC)o=91 S cm2mol-1
Δm(HCI)o=425.9 S cm2mol-1
Δm(NaCl)o=126.4 S cm2mol-1
Using Kohlrausch law, to find the molar conductivity of acetic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a green alternative for dry cleaning solvents?
questions.solution:
Tetrachloroethene (perchloroethylene) was traditionally used as a solvent for dry cleaning. However, it contaminates groundwater and is a suspected carcinogen.

To minimize environmental pollution and health hazards, green chemistry principles have led to the replacement of halogenated solvents with liquefied or supercritical $\text{CO}_2$ along with a suitable detergent.

Using supercritical $\text{CO}_2$ is a greener alternative as it is non-toxic, non-flammable, and does not contaminate groundwater.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following gases causes the depletion of ozone layer in upper atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere is depleted by substances like chlorofluorocarbons and nitrogen oxides. Nitric oxide (NO) is a significant ozone-depleting agent that reacts with ozone ($\mathrm{O}_3$) in a catalytic cycle: $\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{NO}_2 + \mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{NO}_2 + \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O}_2$.

$\mathrm{O}_3 + \mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{O}_2$

NO acts as a catalyst, regenerating after each cycle to destroy multiple ozone molecules. Although other nitrogen oxides can contribute, NO is the most direct and potent among the options. The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find principle of green chemistry to show protection of selective group is not advantageous.
questions.solution:
Reducing derivative generation is a core principle of green chemistry that disfavors protection of selective groups. Protection introduces additional synthetic steps through derivatization, requiring supplementary reagents and generating avoidable waste without contributing to molecular complexity.

Evaluating the principles:

The use of protecting groups constitutes unnecessary derivatization, directly contravening the principle to minimize such steps. This approach increases material consumption, energy expenditure, and waste production without synthetic necessity.

While renewable feedstocks, catalytic processes, and degradable design represent valuable green chemistry objectives, they do not specifically address the inefficiencies inherent in protection/deprotection sequences.

Thus, protection of selective groups is disadvantageous under the principle of derivative reduction.

questions.solution:
Reduce derivatives is the principle that advocates avoiding protection and deprotection of selective groups. This principle minimizes unnecessary derivatization steps, which often require additional reagents and generate waste.

The alternatives do not address this concept: use of renewable feed stock concerns raw material sustainability, design for energy efficiency focuses on energy minimization, and designing safer chemicals emphasizes toxicity reduction.

The correct choice is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is effectively used instead of DDT?
questions.solution:
BHC (Benzene Hexachloride), also known as Lindane, is an organochlorine insecticide that serves as an effective alternative to DDT. While BHC shares similar environmental concerns due to its persistence, it belongs to the same chemical class and was widely adopted for pest control purposes.

The other compounds lack insecticidal properties: $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ is a solvent and anesthetic, $\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$ is a solvent, and picric acid functions as an explosive and antiseptic.

The correct alternative is therefore $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is used as Green solvent?
questions.solution:
Green solvents are environmentally benign substances that minimize ecological impact and health hazards by being non-toxic, non-flammable, and recyclable or biodegradable.

Among the options, only supercritical $\mathrm{CO}_2$ qualifies as a green solvent. It is non-toxic, non-flammable, inexpensive, and widely available. Its properties are tunable with temperature and pressure adjustments, making it versatile for applications like extraction and reactions. It leaves no toxic residue and separates easily from products via depressurization.

In contrast: $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ (chloroform) is toxic and carcinogenic; $\mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2$ (dichloromethane) is volatile and harmful; $\mathrm{CCl}_4$ (carbon tetrachloride) is highly toxic and ozone-depleting. These chlorinated solvents do not meet green criteria.

The green solvent is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following principal of green chemistry suggests use of chemicals made from plant based sources?
questions.solution:
Use of renewable feed stocks is the green chemistry principle advocating for raw materials derived from replenishable sources like plants, rather than depletable resources.

This directly contrasts with options describing process minimization, degradation design, or derivative reduction, which address efficiency and waste management rather than material origin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following gases causes depletion in ozone layer?
questions.solution:
The ozone layer in the stratosphere protects Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation. Depletion occurs primarily through catalytic reactions with certain chemical species.

Helium is inert and non-reactive with ozone. Carbon dioxide contributes to global warming but does not deplete ozone. Hydrogen gas shows no known ozone-depleting properties.

Nitric oxide participates in a catalytic cycle:
$NO + O_3 \rightarrow NO_2 + O_2$
$NO_2 + O \rightarrow NO + O_2$

The net reaction is $O_3 + O \rightarrow 2O_2$, with nitric oxide acting as a catalyst to destroy ozone molecules.

Nitric oxide is therefore the ozone-depleting species.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which solvent from following is used in order to avoid creation of waste and pollution of air?
questions.solution:
This question addresses green chemistry principles, seeking a solvent that minimizes waste and air pollution. The environmental impact of each option is evaluated:

Option A ($\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{3}$) appears to contain a typographical error; if intended as $\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ (dichloromethane), it is a volatile organic compound contributing to air pollution and toxicity.

Option B ($\mathrm{CHCl}_{3}$, chloroform) is toxic, carcinogenic, and environmentally harmful, exacerbating pollution.

Option C ($\mathrm{CCl}_{4}$, carbon tetrachloride) is highly toxic, ozone-depleting, and a significant pollutant, with restricted use due to its adverse effects.

Option D ($\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, water) is non-toxic, non-flammable, abundant, and environmentally benign, aligning with waste reduction and pollution prevention goals.

The solvent that avoids waste and air pollution is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is one of the product of ozonolysis at ozone layer in atmosphere?
questions.solution:
Ozone (

$O_3$

) in the atmosphere undergoes ozonolysis with unsaturated hydrocarbons, cleaving carbon-carbon double bonds to form carbonyl compounds. The reaction proceeds through an unstable ozonide intermediate that decomposes to aldehydes or ketones depending on substituents.

The general ozonolysis reaction is:
$R_1R_2C=CR_3R_4 + O_3 \rightarrow R_1R_2C=O + R_3R_4C=O$

When R is hydrogen, aldehydes form; with alkyl groups, ketones result. Among the options, aldehydes are direct products of ozonolysis, while alcohols, acids, and esters are not.

The product is therefore $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following series contains only electrophiles?
questions.solution:
Electrophiles are electron-deficient species that can accept an electron pair. They are either positively charged or neutral molecules with an incomplete octet or highly polar bonds.

In the first series, $\text{R-OH}$ and $\text{NH}_3$ have lone pairs on oxygen and nitrogen respectively, making them nucleophiles.

In the second series, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{R}_2\text{N}^-$ have lone pairs and a negative charge respectively, making them nucleophiles.

In the third series, $\text{BF}_3$ is an electron-deficient Lewis acid with an incomplete octet. $\text{SO}_3$ has a highly electron-deficient sulfur atom due to three electronegative oxygen atoms. $\text{NO}^+$ is a positively charged ion. All three are electrophiles.

In the fourth series, $\text{R-NH}_2$ has a lone pair on nitrogen, making it a nucleophile.

Answer: $\text{BF}_3, \text{SO}_3, \text{NO}^+$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecule has Chiral Carbon?
questions.solution:
A chiral carbon atom is one that is bonded to four different atoms or groups.

Let us examine each option:
In the first molecule, the central carbon is bonded to two identical hydrogen (H) atoms. Thus, it is achiral.
In the second molecule, the central carbon is bonded to four different groups: H, CH_3$, OH, and I. Thus, it is a chiral carbon. \\ In the third molecule, the central carbon is bonded to two identical methyl (CH_3$) groups. Thus, it is achiral.
In the fourth molecule, the central carbon is bonded to two identical ethyl (C_2$H_5$) groups. Thus, it is achiral.

Therefore, only the second molecule contains a chiral carbon.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of the following compound is,
questions.solution:
The parent ring in the given structure is cyclohexane.

The substituents attached to the ring are one methoxy group ($-OCH_3$) and two ethyl groups ($-CH_2CH_3$).

According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the ring must be numbered to give the lowest possible set of locants for the substituents.

If we start numbering from the carbon with the two ethyl groups, the locant set is $1, 1, 4$.

If we start numbering from the carbon with the methoxy group, the locant set is $1, 4, 4$.

Comparing the two sets, $(1, 1, 4)$ is lower than $(1, 4, 4)$ at the first point of difference. Therefore, the carbon with the two ethyl groups is designated as position $1$, and the carbon with the methoxy group is position $4$.

When writing the name, substituents are listed in alphabetical order. 'Ethyl' comes before 'methoxy' (multiplying prefixes like 'di' are ignored for alphabetization).

Thus, the correct IUPAC name is 1,1-diethyl-4-methoxycyclohexane.

Answer: 1, 1 - diethyl - 4 - methoxycyclohexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of the following compound ?
questions.solution:
The principal functional group in the given compound is the amine ($-NH_2$) group.

The longest continuous carbon chain containing the carbon attached to the amine group and the double bond has 5 carbon atoms, making the parent chain a pentene.

According to IUPAC rules, the chain is numbered to give the principal functional group the lowest possible locant, as the amine group has higher priority than the alkene double bond.

Numbering from right to left places the amine group at position 2 and the double bond at position 3.

Numbering from left to right would place the double bond at position 2 and the amine group at position 4, which is incorrect because the principal functional group must receive the lower number.

Therefore, the correct IUPAC name is Pent-3-en-2-amine.

Answer: Pent-3-en-2-amine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is tertiary benzylic alcohol?
questions.solution:
A benzylic alcohol has the $-OH$ group attached to a carbon atom that is directly bonded to a benzene ring (benzylic carbon).

For the alcohol to be tertiary ($3^{\circ}$), the benzylic carbon must be bonded to three other carbon atoms (one from the benzene ring and two other alkyl groups).

Let us analyze the given options:
Option (326143): The structure is benzyl alcohol ($Ph-CH_2-OH$). The benzylic carbon is bonded to only one carbon atom (from the benzene ring). It is a primary ($1^{\circ}$) benzylic alcohol.

Option (326144): The structure is 1-phenylpropan-1-ol ($Ph-CH(OH)-CH_2-CH_3$). The benzylic carbon is bonded to two carbon atoms (one from the benzene ring and one from the ethyl group). It is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) benzylic alcohol.

Option (326145): The structure is 1-phenylethan-1-ol ($Ph-CH(OH)-CH_3$). The benzylic carbon is bonded to two carbon atoms (one from the benzene ring and one from the methyl group). It is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) benzylic alcohol.

Option (326146): The structure is 2-phenylpropan-2-ol ($Ph-C(CH_3)_2-OH$). The benzylic carbon is bonded to three carbon atoms (one from the benzene ring and two from the methyl groups). It is a tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) benzylic alcohol.

Answer:

Carboxylic acids > Sulfonic acids > Esters > Acid halides > Amides > Nitriles > Aldehydes > Ketones > Alcohols > Amines > Alkenes > Alkynes.

Comparing the given functional groups, the correct priority order is:

$-\text{CONH}_2 \gt -\text{CHO} \gt -\text{OH} \gt -\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-$

Answer: $-\text{CONH}_2 \gt -\text{CHO} \gt -\text{OH} \gt -\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of following compound?
questions.solution:
The principal functional group in the given compound is the carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$). Therefore, the parent chain is taken as benzoic acid.

Numbering of the benzene ring starts from the carbon atom attached to the $-COOH$ group as position 1. To give the lowest possible number to the substituent, the carbon attached to the methyl group ($-CH_3$) is numbered as 2.

Thus, there is a methyl group at the 2-position of the benzoic acid ring. The IUPAC name of the compound is 2-Methylbenzoic acid. (Note: o-Toluic acid is its common name).

Answer: 2-Methylbenzoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the number of structural isomers possible for hexane ?
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of hexane is $C_6H_{14}$.

The possible structural isomers are:

1. $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$ (n-hexane)

2. $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$ (2-methylpentane)

3. $CH_3-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$ (3-methylpentane)

4. $CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH_2-CH_3$ (2,2-dimethylbutane)

5. $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$ (2,3-dimethylbutane)

Thus, there are five structural isomers possible for hexane.

Answer: Five

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a phenol ?
questions.solution:
A phenol is a compound in which a hydroxyl group ($-OH$) is directly attached to an $sp^2$ hybridized carbon atom of an aromatic ring.

In the first option, the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the benzene ring (o-nitrophenol), so it is a phenol.

In the second option, the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the naphthalene ring (2-naphthol), so it is considered a phenolic compound.

In the third option, the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the benzene ring (o-bromophenol), so it is a phenol.

In the fourth option, the $-OH$ group is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom of a side chain ($-CH_2OH$), not directly to the aromatic ring. This compound is benzyl alcohol, which is an aromatic alcohol but not a phenol.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following structures represents 1,3 butadiene ?
questions.solution:
The IUPAC name 1,3-butadiene corresponds to a four-carbon chain with two double bonds located at the 1st and 3rd carbon atoms.

The chemical formula is $CH_2=CH-CH=CH_2$.

Let us analyze the given bond-line structures:
1. The first structure has a five-carbon chain with one double bond at the second position, representing pent-2-ene.
2. The second structure has a four-carbon chain with double bonds at the first and third positions, representing 1,3-butadiene.
3. The third structure has a four-carbon chain with a triple bond at the first position, representing but-1-yne.
4. The fourth structure has a three-carbon chain with a triple bond, representing propyne.

Therefore, the second structure correctly represents 1,3-butadiene.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: IUPAC name of glycerol is -
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of glycerol is $CH_2(OH)-CH(OH)-CH_2(OH)$.

The principal functional group is the hydroxyl group ($-OH$), which is indicated by the suffix 'ol'.

The longest carbon chain containing the $-OH$ groups has 3 carbon atoms, so the parent alkane is propane.

Numbering the carbon chain from either end gives the positions of the $-OH$ groups as 1, 2, and 3.

Since there are three hydroxyl groups, the multiplier 'tri' is used.

Combining these parts, the IUPAC name of glycerol is propane-1,2,3-triol.

Answer: Propane - 1,2,3-triol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is allylic halide ?
questions.solution:
Allylic halides are compounds in which the halogen atom is bonded to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond ($C=C$).

In $\text{CH}_2 = \text{CH} - \text{CH}_2 - \text{X}$, the halogen atom $\text{X}$ is attached to the $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom which is directly attached to the $C=C$ double bond. Thus, it is an allylic halide.

$\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{X}$ is a primary alkyl halide.

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2 - \text{X}$ is a benzylic halide.

$\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH} = \text{CH} - \text{X}$ is a vinylic halide.

Answer: $\text{CH}_2 = \text{CH} - \text{CH}_2 - \text{X}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of the following compound ?
questions.solution:
To find the IUPAC name of the given compound, we follow these steps:

1. Identify the principal functional group: The molecule contains a hydroxyl group ($-OH$) and a double bond. The hydroxyl group has higher priority, so it is the principal functional group and must be given the lowest possible locant.

2. Determine the longest carbon chain: The longest continuous carbon chain that contains both the $-OH$ group and the double bond must be selected.
Tracing from the rightmost ethyl group to the leftmost ethyl group gives a chain of 9 carbon atoms. Thus, the parent alkane is nonane.

3. Number the chain: We number the chain to give the principal functional group ($-OH$) the lowest possible number.
Numbering from right to left:
C1, C2: Ethyl group on the right ($-CH_2-CH_3$)
C3: Carbon with a methyl substituent
C4: Carbon with the $-OH$ group
C5, C6: Carbons of the double bond
C7: Carbon with a methyl substituent
C8, C9: Ethyl group on the left ($-CH_2-CH_3$)
In this numbering, the $-OH$ group is at position 4.
If we numbered from left to right, the $-OH$ group would be at position 6. Therefore, the right-to-left numbering is correct.

4. Identify substituents and their positions:
- A methyl group at C-3.
- A methyl group at C-7.
- A double bond starting at C-5.
- The hydroxyl group at C-4.

5. Assemble the name:
Combining these parts, we get: 3,7-dimethyl + non + 5-en + 4-ol \rightarrow 3,7-dimethylnon-5-en-4-ol.

Answer: 3,7-Dimethylnon-5-en-4-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is an aromatic aldehyde ?
questions.solution:
An aromatic aldehyde is a compound in which the aldehyde group ($\text{-CHO}$) is directly attached to an aromatic ring.

Let us evaluate the given options:
1. In the first structure (3-phenylpropanal), the $\text{-CHO}$ group is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon of an aliphatic chain, not directly to the benzene ring.
2. In the second structure (cinnamaldehyde), the $\text{-CHO}$ group is attached to an $sp^2$ hybridized carbon of an alkene chain.
3. In the third structure (cyclohexanecarbaldehyde), the $\text{-CHO}$ group is attached to a cyclohexane ring, which is non-aromatic.
4. In the fourth structure (2-methylbenzaldehyde or $o$-tolualdehyde), the $\text{-CHO}$ group is directly attached to the aromatic benzene ring.

Therefore, 2-methylbenzaldehyde is the only aromatic aldehyde among the given choices.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following aldehydes contains two $-\text{CHO}$ groups in a molecule?
questions.solution:
Acrolein is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$, which contains one $-\text{CHO}$ group.

o-Tolualdehyde is $o-\text{CH}_3-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CHO}$, which contains one $-\text{CHO}$ group.

Phthaldehyde is benzene-1,2-dicarbaldehyde, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{CHO})_2$, which contains two $-\text{CHO}$ groups.

Butyraldehyde is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$, which contains one $-\text{CHO}$ group.

Therefore, phthaldehyde contains two $-\text{CHO}$ groups.

Answer: Phthaldehyde

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a primary benzylic alcohol?
questions.solution:
A benzylic alcohol contains an -OH group attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom directly bonded to an aromatic ring.

A primary alcohol has the -OH group attached to a primary carbon atom (a carbon bonded to only one other carbon).

In $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, the -OH group is attached to a $\text{CH}_2$ group which is directly bonded to the benzene ring. Thus, it is a primary benzylic alcohol.

In $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3$, the -OH group is attached to a secondary carbon, making it a secondary benzylic alcohol.

$\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3$ is a secondary allylic alcohol.

$\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is a primary allylic alcohol.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the aldehyde from following so that the aldehydic group is NOT attached with any $sp^3$ hybrid 'c' atom.
questions.solution:
Methanal is $H-CHO$. The aldehydic group ($-CHO$) is attached to a hydrogen atom, not to any carbon atom. Therefore, it is not attached to any $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Ethanal is $CH_3-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a methyl group, which contains an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

2-Methylpropanal is $(CH_3)_2CH-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a $CH$ group, which is an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Propanal is $CH_3-CH_2-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a $CH_2$ group, which is an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Thus, methanal is the only aldehyde among the given options where the aldehydic group is not attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of chiral carbon atoms in 2-chlorobutane?
questions.solution:
The structure of 2-chlorobutane is $CH_{3}-CH(Cl)-CH_{2}-CH_{3}$.

A chiral carbon atom is one that is bonded to four different atoms or groups.

In 2-chlorobutane, the second carbon atom (C2) is bonded to four different groups: a hydrogen atom ($-H$), a chlorine atom ($-Cl$), a methyl group ($-CH_{3}$), and an ethyl group ($-CH_{2}CH_{3}$).

Therefore, C2 is a chiral carbon.

The other carbon atoms (C1, C3, and C4) are bonded to at least two identical hydrogen atoms, so they are not chiral.

Thus, there is only $1$ chiral carbon atom in 2-chlorobutane.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds does NOT contain double bond in it ?
questions.solution:
Tetrahydrofuran is a fully saturated five-membered cyclic ether with the chemical formula $C_4H_8O$. It does not contain any double bonds.

4H-Pyran is a six-membered non-aromatic heterocyclic compound containing one oxygen atom and two double bonds.

Pyrrole is a five-membered aromatic heterocyclic compound containing one nitrogen atom and two double bonds.

Thiophene is a five-membered aromatic heterocyclic compound containing one sulfur atom and two double bonds.

Therefore, tetrahydrofuran is the only compound among the given options that does not contain a double bond.

Answer: Tetrahydrofuran

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds is NOT optically active?
questions.solution:
The optical activity of a compound depends on the presence of a chiral carbon atom, which is bonded to four different groups.

In 3-bromohexane, the C3 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, an ethyl group, and a propyl group. Since all four groups are different, it is chiral and optically active.

In 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a bromine atom, an ethyl group, and two identical methyl groups. Since two groups are the same, it does not have a chiral center and is optically inactive.

In 2-bromopentane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, a methyl group, and a propyl group. It is chiral and optically active.

In 2-bromo-3-methylbutane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, a methyl group, and an isopropyl group. It is chiral and optically active.

Thus, 2-bromo-2-methylbutane is not optically active.

Answer: 2 - Bromo - 2 - methylbutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the of number of chiral carbon atoms present in 2-Bromo-3,4,5-trimethylhexane ?
questions.solution:
The structure of 2-Bromo-3,4,5-trimethylhexane is:

$CH_3 - CH(Br) - CH(CH_3) - CH(CH_3) - CH(CH_3) - CH_3$

Let us examine each carbon atom in the principal chain for chirality (a chiral carbon must be attached to four different groups):

C1: Attached to three identical hydrogen atoms \Rightarrow Achiral.

C2: Attached to $-H$, $-Br$, $-CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different \Rightarrow Chiral.

C3: Attached to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH(Br)CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different \Rightarrow Chiral.

C4: Attached to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH(CH_3)CH(Br)CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different \Rightarrow Chiral.

C5: Attached to $-H$, a methyl group ($-CH_3$), C6 (which is also a $-CH_3$ group), and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(Br)CH_3$. Since it is attached to two identical methyl groups, it is \Rightarrow Achiral.

C6: Attached to three identical hydrogen atoms \Rightarrow Achiral.

The chiral carbon atoms are C2, C3, and C4. Therefore, there are 3 chiral carbon atoms in the molecule.

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of second higher homologue of formic acid?
questions.solution:
Formic acid is the first member of the carboxylic acid homologous series with the IUPAC name methanoic acid ($HCOOH$).

The first higher homologue is obtained by adding one $-CH_2-$ group, which gives ethanoic acid ($CH_3COOH$).

The second higher homologue is obtained by adding another $-CH_2-$ group, which gives propanoic acid ($CH_3CH_2COOH$).

Answer: Propanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many chiral carbon atoms are present in 2-Iodo-3, 4, 5-trimethylhexane ?
questions.solution:
The structure of 2-iodo-3,4,5-trimethylhexane is $CH_3-CH(I)-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$.

Let us examine each carbon atom in the principal chain for chirality by checking if it is bonded to four different groups:

$C_1$: Bonded to three identical hydrogen atoms, hence achiral.

$C_2$: Bonded to $-H$, $-I$, $-CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different, making $C_2$ a chiral center.

$C_3$: Bonded to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH(I)CH_3$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)_2$. All four groups are different, making $C_3$ a chiral center.

$C_4$: Bonded to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH(CH_3)_2$, and $-CH(CH_3)CH(I)CH_3$. All four groups are different, making $C_4$ a chiral center.

$C_5$: Bonded to $-H$, $-CH_3$, $-CH_3$ (from $C_6$), and $-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(I)CH_3$. Since it is bonded to two identical methyl groups, $C_5$ is achiral.

$C_6$: Bonded to three identical hydrogen atoms, hence achiral.

The methyl substituents on $C_3$, $C_4$, and $C_5$ are also bonded to three identical hydrogen atoms and are achiral.

Thus, there are exactly $3$ chiral carbon atoms ($C_2$, $C_3$, and $C_4$).

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the name of second lower homologue of $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{COOH}$ ?
questions.solution:
The given compound is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{COOH}$, which contains 4 carbon atoms and is named butanoic acid.

Homologues in a series differ by a successive $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit.

The first lower homologue has one less $-\text{CH}_2-$ unit, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (propanoic acid).

The second lower homologue has two less $-\text{CH}_2-$ units, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ (ethanoic acid).

Answer: Ethanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following elements is NOT present in mustard gas?
questions.solution:
The chemical name of mustard gas is bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide.

Its chemical structure is $\text{Cl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{S}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ and its molecular formula is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{Cl}_2\text{S}$.

The elements present in mustard gas are Carbon ($\text{C}$), Hydrogen ($\text{H}$), Chlorine ($\text{Cl}$), and Sulphur ($\text{S}$).

Nitrogen ($\text{N}$) is not present in mustard gas.

Answer: $\text{N}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of following compound?
questions.solution:
The given compound contains a seven-membered carbon ring with a principal functional group, an alcohol (-OH). Thus, the parent name is cycloheptanol.

The carbon atom attached to the -OH group is numbered as C1.

The substituents on the ring are an ethyl group and a methyl group.

Numbering the ring to assign the lowest possible locants to the substituents yields two possibilities: clockwise gives positions 3 for ethyl and 6 for methyl, while counter-clockwise gives positions 3 for methyl and 6 for ethyl.

When the set of locants is the same in both directions, alphabetical order is considered. Since 'ethyl' comes before 'methyl' alphabetically, the ethyl group is assigned the lower number (3).

Therefore, the correct numbering places the ethyl group at C3 and the methyl group at C6.

The complete IUPAC name is 3-Ethyl-6-methylcycloheptanol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following statements is NOT true about homologous series?
options: Each member of a series has same functional group.
Each member has same type of carbon skeleton.
Each member differs by ethylene group from next member.
All members of series possess similar chemical properties.
questions.solution:
A homologous series is a series of organic compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties, and the same general formula.

Successive members of a homologous series differ from each other by a methylene group ($-CH_2-$) and a molecular mass of $14\text{ u}$.

The statement that each member differs by an ethylene group is incorrect, as they differ by a methylene group.

Answer: Each member differs by ethylene group from next member.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is haloalkyne?
questions.solution:
A haloalkyne (or alkynyl halide) is a compound in which a halogen atom is directly bonded to an $sp$-hybridized carbon atom of the carbon-carbon triple bond.

In chloroethyne ($Cl-C \equiv CH$), the chlorine atom is directly attached to the $sp$-hybridized carbon atom. Therefore, it is a haloalkyne.

In 3-chloropropyne ($HC \equiv C-CH_2-Cl$), 1-chloropent-2-yne ($CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv C-CH_2-Cl$), and 4-chloropent-2-yne ($CH_3-CH(Cl)-C \equiv C-CH_3$), the chlorine atom is attached to an $sp^3$-hybridized carbon atom.

Answer: Chloroethyne

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following has the highest nucleophilicity ?
questions.solution:
The given species $\text{CH}_3^-$, $\text{NH}_2^-$, $\text{OH}^-$, and $\text{F}^-$ have donor atoms belonging to the same period (Period 2) of the periodic table.

Across a period from left to right, the electronegativity of the atoms increases in the order $\text{C} \lt \text{N} \lt \text{O} \lt \text{F}$.

A more electronegative atom holds its lone pair of electrons more tightly, making it less available for donation to an electrophile. Therefore, nucleophilicity decreases as electronegativity increases.

The order of nucleophilicity is $\text{CH}_3^- \gt \text{NH}_2^- \gt \text{OH}^- \gt \text{F}^-$.

Thus, $\text{CH}_3^-$ has the highest nucleophilicity.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the number of hyperconjugation structures in the isopropyl carbocation.
questions.solution:
The structure of the isopropyl carbocation is $(CH_3)_2CH^+$.

The carbon atom bearing the positive charge is attached to two methyl groups.

The number of $\alpha$-hydrogens is the total number of hydrogen atoms attached to the $\alpha$-carbons.

Here, there are two $\alpha$-carbons, each having $3$ hydrogen atoms. Thus, the total number of $\alpha$-hydrogens is $3 + 3 = 6$.

The number of hyperconjugation structures is equal to the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens.

Therefore, the number of hyperconjugation structures is $6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of following reactions, the oxidative rancidity is?
questions.solution:
Oxidative rancidity is the process of autoxidation of lipids (fats and oils) exposed to oxygen, resulting in unpleasant odors and flavors.

This autoxidation proceeds via a free radical chain reaction mechanism.

The mechanism involves three main steps: initiation (formation of lipid free radicals), propagation (reaction of lipid radicals with oxygen to form peroxyl radicals, which abstract hydrogen from other lipid molecules), and termination (combination of radicals to form stable, non-radical products).

Therefore, oxidative rancidity is a free radical chain reaction.

Answer: free radical chain reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an aromatic alcohol?
questions.solution:
Aromatic alcohols are compounds in which the hydroxyl ($-OH$) group is attached to a carbon atom of an aliphatic side chain, rather than directly to the aromatic ring.

If the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the aromatic ring, the compound is classified as a phenol.

In compounds (I) and (IV), the $-OH$ group is directly attached to the benzene ring. Hence, they are phenols.

In compounds (II) and (III), the $-OH$ group is attached to a $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom of the side chain. Hence, they are aromatic alcohols.

Answer: II and III Only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List IList II
(A). Inductive effect(I). Delocalization of $\pi$ electrons
(B). Hyper-conjugation(II). Displacement of $\pi$ electrons
(C). Resonance effect(III). Delocalization of $\sigma$ electrons
(IV). Displacement of $\sigma$ electrons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Inductive effect involves the permanent displacement of $\sigma$ electrons along a saturated carbon chain due to differences in electronegativity. Thus, (A) matches with (IV).

Hyper-conjugation involves the delocalization of $\sigma$ electrons (typically from a C-H bond) into an adjacent empty p-orbital or $\pi$ system. Thus, (B) matches with (III).

Resonance effect involves the delocalization of $\pi$ electrons or lone pairs across a conjugated system. Thus, (C) matches with (I).

The correct matching is (A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (I).

Answer: $(A) - (IV), (B) - (III), (C) - (I)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of the compound $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH=CHCOOH}$ ?
questions.solution:
The principal functional group is the carboxylic acid ($-\text{COOH}$), so numbering starts from the carbon atom of the $-\text{COOH}$ group.

The longest carbon chain containing the principal functional group has $6$ carbon atoms, so the root word is 'hex'.

There are two double bonds located at C2 and C4, so the primary suffix is '2,4-diene'.

The secondary suffix for the carboxylic acid is 'oic acid'.

Combining these parts, the IUPAC name of the compound is Hexa-2,4-dienoic acid.

Answer: Hexa-2,4-dienoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name for a molecule that has two amino groups in opposing (para) locations around a benzene ring?
questions.solution:
The molecule consists of a benzene ring with two amino ($-NH_2$) groups attached at opposite positions.

According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the parent hydrocarbon is benzene.

The two amino groups are indicated by the suffix "diamine".

The positions of the amino groups are numbered to give them the lowest possible locants. Since they are at opposite positions (para), the locants are $1$ and $4$.

Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is benzene-1,4-diamine.

Answer: Benzene-1,4-diamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following, the most stable carbocation is
questions.solution:
The stability of carbocations increases with the increase in the number of alkyl groups attached to the positively charged carbon atom. This is due to the +I (inductive) effect and hyperconjugation.

The order of stability of alkyl carbocations is $3^{\circ} \gt 2^{\circ} \gt 1^{\circ} \gt \text{methyl}$.

Among the given options, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$ is a tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) carbocation, which has nine $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms, leading to maximum hyperconjugation structures. Hence, it is the most stable carbocation.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following is correct decreasing order of acidic strength for the compounds listed below?
I: p-chlorophenol, II: p-Cresol, III: p-nitrophenol, IV: p-methoxyphenol.
questions.solution:
Acidic strength of phenols is directly proportional to the stability of the phenoxide ion formed after losing a proton.

Electron-withdrawing groups stabilize the phenoxide ion through $-I$ and $-R$ effects, thereby increasing the acidic strength. Electron-donating groups destabilize the phenoxide ion through $+I$, $+H$, and $+R$ effects, thereby decreasing the acidic strength.

In p-nitrophenol (III), the $-NO_2$ group exerts strong $-R$ and $-I$ effects, making it the most acidic.

In p-chlorophenol (I), the $-Cl$ group exerts a $-I$ effect which dominates over its $+R$ effect, making it more acidic than phenol but less acidic than p-nitrophenol.

In p-cresol (II), the $-CH_3$ group exerts $+I$ and hyperconjugation ($+H$) effects, decreasing the acidic strength compared to phenol.

In p-methoxyphenol (IV), the $-OCH_3$ group exerts a strong $+R$ effect which dominates over its $-I$ effect, making it the least acidic.

Thus, the decreasing order of acidic strength is III > I > II > IV.

Answer: III > I > II > IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital formed by overlap of p-orbitals must contain,
questions.solution:
According to H\u00fcckel's rule, a cyclic, planar, and completely conjugated system is highly stable and aromatic if it contains $(4n + 2)\pi$-electrons, where $n$ is an integer ($0, 1, 2, \dots$).

These $\pi$-electrons reside in the cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital formed by the continuous lateral overlap of unhybridized p-orbitals of the atoms in the ring.

Thus, the cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital must contain $(4n + 2)$ p electrons for the system to exhibit aromatic stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are TRUE?
(I) Inductive effect operates through the sigma bond
(II) Resonance effect operates through the pi bond
(III) Inductive effects operate through the pi bond
(IV) Resonance effect operates through the sigma bond
questions.solution:
Inductive effect involves the displacement of $\sigma$-electrons along a saturated carbon chain. Thus, it operates through $\sigma$-bonds.

Resonance effect involves the delocalization of $\pi$-electrons or lone pairs of electrons. Thus, it operates through $\pi$-bonds.

Therefore, statements (I) and (II) are true.

Answer: (I) and (II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the false statement regarding chirality from the following.
options: $SN^1$ reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
A recemic mixture shows zero dipole rotation
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images of each other
The product obtained by $SN^2$ reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
questions.solution:
Enantiomers are defined as stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other. Therefore, the statement that enantiomers are superimposable mirror images is false.

In an $S_N1$ reaction, the formation of a planar carbocation intermediate allows the nucleophile to attack from either face with equal probability, generally yielding a 1:1 mixture of enantiomers (a racemic mixture).

A racemic mixture contains equal amounts of dextrorotatory and levorotatory enantiomers, resulting in zero net optical rotation.

In an $S_N2$ reaction at a chiral center, the nucleophile attacks from the side opposite to the leaving group, leading to a complete inversion of configuration.

Answer: Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images of each other

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the difference in terms of molar masses of second and fourth members of homologous series?
questions.solution:
Successive members of a homologous series differ by a $-CH_2-$ group.

The molar mass of a $-CH_2-$ group is $12 + 2 \times 1 = 14 \text{ g/mol}$.

The difference between the second and fourth members of a homologous series corresponds to two $-CH_2-$ groups.

Difference in molar mass $= 2 \times 14 = 28 \text{ g/mol}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of isomerism is exhibited by neopentane?
questions.solution:
Neopentane ($C_5H_{12}$) is an isomer of pentane.

The isomers of pentane are n-pentane, isopentane, and neopentane.

These compounds have the same molecular formula but differ in the arrangement of their carbon skeleton (straight chain versus branched chain).

Therefore, neopentane exhibits chain isomerism.

Answer: chain

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of moles of ' C ' and ' H ' atoms respectively present in n mole molecule represented by following structure ?
questions.solution:
The molecular structure of styrene consists of a benzene ring bonded to a vinyl group.

A benzene ring attached as a substituent contributes 6 carbon atoms and 5 hydrogen atoms, while the vinyl group $\mathrm{-CH=CH_2}$ contributes 2 carbon atoms and 3 hydrogen atoms.

Total carbon atoms: $6 + 2 = 8$

Total hydrogen atoms: $5 + 3 = 8$

The molecular formula is $\mathrm{C8H8}$.

For $n$ moles of styrene molecules, the number of moles of carbon atoms is $8 \times n = 8n$, and the number of moles of hydrogen atoms is $8 \times n = 8n$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is trihydric phenol?
questions.solution:
Phenols are classified by the number of hydroxyl groups bonded to the benzene ring: monohydric (one $\mathrm{-OH}$), dihydric (two $\mathrm{-OH}$), or trihydric (three $\mathrm{-OH}$).

Catechol (benzene-1,2-diol), resorcinol (benzene-1,3-diol), and quinol (benzene-1,4-diol) are all dihydric phenols.

Pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol and contains three hydroxyl groups.

Thus, pyrogallol is the only trihydric phenol among the options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the difference of molar masses expressed in gram of two neighbouring members of a homologous series?
questions.solution:
A homologous series consists of compounds with the same functional group, where each successive member differs by a $\text{CH}_2$ group.

The molar mass of $\text{CH}_2$ is calculated as $12 \text{ g/mol} + 2 \times 1 \text{ g/mol} = 14 \text{ g/mol}$.

The difference in molar masses is 14 g/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to carbinol system tert butyl alcohol is named as,
questions.solution:
In the carbinol system, alcohols are named as derivatives of methanol by replacing hydrogen atoms on the methyl group with substituents.

Tert-butyl alcohol has the formula $(CH_3)_3C\text{--}OH$, where the carbinol carbon is bonded to three methyl groups. This corresponds to trimethyl carbinol.

The alternatives correspond to different structures: methyl carbinol ($CH_3CH_2OH$), ethyl carbinol ($CH_3CH_2CH_2OH$), and propyl carbinol ($CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2OH$).

The correct carbinol system name is therefore trimethyl carbinol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Select from the following a correct IUPAC name of pyrogallol.
questions.solution:
Pyrogallol is the common name for 1,2,3-trihydroxybenzene. In IUPAC nomenclature, the parent structure is benzene, with hydroxyl groups located at positions 1, 2, and 3.

Evaluating the options: A corresponds to resorcinol, B to hydroquinone, C correctly identifies pyrogallol as benzene-1,2,3-triol, and D corresponds to phloroglucinol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The common name of Benzene - 1,2 - diol is
questions.solution:
Benzene-1,2-diol features two hydroxyl groups at adjacent positions on the aromatic ring, corresponding to the common name catechol.

For comparison, benzene-1,3-diol is known as resorcinol, benzene-1,4-diol is quinol (or hydroquinone), and benzene-1,2,3-triol is pyrogallol.

The correct answer is A. Catechol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the common name of Benzene-1,3-diol?
questions.solution:
The common name for Benzene-1,3-diol is resorcinol, corresponding to isomer position 1,3.

Benzene-1,2-diol is catechol, while benzene-1,4-diol is hydroquinone or quinol. Pyrogallol is the trihydroxybenzene 1,2,3-isomer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the difference in molar mass of Undecane and Dodecane?
questions.solution:
Alkanes follow the general formula $C_nH_{2n+2}$.
For undecane ($n=11$): $C_{11}H_{24}$
For dodecane ($n=12$): $C_{12}H_{26}$

Using atomic masses $C \approx 12.01 \text{ g/mol}$ and $H \approx 1.008 \text{ g/mol}$:
Undecane molar mass: $11 \times 12.01 + 24 \times 1.008 = 156.302 \text{ g/mol}$
Dodecane molar mass: $12 \times 12.01 + 26 \times 1.008 = 170.328 \text{ g/mol}$

The difference is $170.328 - 156.302 = 14.026 \text{ g/mol}$, which rounds to $14 \text{ g/mol}$.

Equivalently, consecutive alkanes differ by a $CH_2$ group with molar mass $12.01 + 2 \times 1.008 = 14.026 \text{ g/mol}$.

Correct option: D $14 \text{ g/mol}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds does NOT contain nitrogen in it?
questions.solution:
Thiophene has the formula $C_4H_4S$ and contains sulfur but no nitrogen. All other options contain nitrogen: pyridine ($C_5H_5N$), pyrrole ($C_4H_5N$), and piperidine ($C_5H_{11}N$) are nitrogenous heterocycles.

The compound that does not contain nitrogen is thiophene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is an optically inactive compound?
questions.solution:
Optical inactivity arises in achiral molecules. A compound lacking chiral centers or possessing a plane of symmetry is achiral and thus optically inactive.

For 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, the carbon at position 2 is bonded to $-\text{Cl}$, $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_3$, and $-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, with two identical methyl groups making it non-chiral. No other chiral centers exist, and the molecule lacks a plane of symmetry, confirming achirality.

In contrast, 3-chlorohexane has one chiral center at $C3$ with groups $- \text{H}$, $- \text{Cl}$, $- \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and $- \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, all distinct. 2-chloropentane and 2-chloro-3-methylbutane each possess a chiral center at $C2$, bonded to distinct groups, ensuring chirality and optical activity.

Only 2-chloro-2-methylbutane is achiral and optically inactive.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of following compound?
questions.solution:
Identifying the IUPAC name requires analyzing the structure: a cyclobutane ring with substituents including a methoxy group and two methyl groups.

Numbering begins at the carbon bearing the methoxy group to maintain the lowest possible locants. The adjacent carbon, with two methyl groups, is assigned position 2.

The correct name is $\text{1-methoxy-2,2-dimethylcyclobutane}$, matching option C. Option A and B incorrectly identify the parent as butane rather than cyclobutane, and option D uses non-optimal numbering for the methoxy group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds does NOT contain oxygen as heteroatom?
questions.solution:
Identification of compounds without oxygen heteroatoms: Among the given options, pyrrole contains nitrogen as the sole heteroatom and lacks oxygen entirely.

Furan features an oxygen heteroatom in its five-membered aromatic ring structure $C_4H_4O$.

Tetrahydrofuran contains oxygen in its saturated five-membered ring $C_4H_8O$.

4H-Pyran incorporates oxygen in its six-membered ring structure $C_5H_6O$.

Pyrrole $C_4H_5N$ contains nitrogen as its heteroatom without oxygen participation.

Since pyrrole is the only compound devoid of oxygen, the correct choice is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many chiral carbon atoms are present in 2-chloro-3,4,5-trimethylhexane?
questions.solution:
Identifying chiral carbon atoms in 2-chloro-3,4,5-trimethylhexane

The compound has structure: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(Cl)-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3}$

Chiral centers require carbon bonded to four distinct groups. Terminal methyl carbons (C1 and C6) have three identical hydrogens and are not chiral.

Carbons C2, C3, C4, and C5 each have four different substituents:
C2: H, Cl, CH_3, and $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH_3}$
C3: H, CH_3, $\mathrm{-CH(Cl)CH_3}$, and $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH_3}$
C4: H, CH_3, $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH(Cl)CH_3}$, and $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH_3}$
C5: H, $CH_3$, $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)CH(CH_3)CH(Cl)CH_3}$, and $CH_3$

All four internal carbons satisfy the chirality condition.

Final answer: $\boxed{4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is structural formula of mesityl oxide?
questions.solution:
The compound mesityl oxide is systematically named 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one, indicating a five-carbon chain with a ketone at position 2, a double bond at position 3, and a methyl substituent at position 4.

The correct structural formula must correspond to $\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH=C(CH_3)-CH_3}$, which is 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one under standard numbering.

Option A, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CH-CH=CH-CO-CH_3}$, is 5-methylhex-3-en-2-one.
Option B, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{C=CH-CO-CH_3}$, expands to $\mathrm{CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CO-CH_3}$ and corresponds to 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one.
Option C, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{C-CH=CH-CO-CH_3}$, is 5,5-dimethylhex-3-en-2-one.
Option D, $(\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{CH-CH=CH-CO-CH(CH_3)_2}$, is 2,6-dimethylhept-3-en-4-one.

Only option B matches the structure of mesityl oxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is a pair of functional isomers?
questions.solution:
Functional isomers are compounds sharing the same molecular formula but differing in their functional groups. Option B satisfies this criterion as the two compounds are both $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ but contain alcohol and ether groups respectively.

Butan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) is an alcohol, while 1-methoxypropane ($\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) is an ether.

The remaining options involve pairs that are isomers but share the same functional group, such as alcohols (A) or ethers (C and D), making them positional or chain isomers rather than functional isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkenes does NOT exhibit cis-trans isomerism ?
questions.solution:
Cis-trans isomerism requires that each carbon of the double bond be bonded to two distinct groups. But-1-ene, with structure $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$, has both hydrogens attached to the first carbon and thus fails this condition.
But-2-ene, 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene, and pent-2-ene all meet the requirement with different substituents on each olefinic carbon, so only but-1-ene lacks geometric isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a non benzenoid aromatic compound?
questions.solution:
Non-benzenoid aromatic compounds satisfy Hückel's rule while lacking a benzene ring structure.

Aniline contains a benzene ring, making it benzenoid aromatic.

Naphthalene consists of fused benzene rings, classifying it as benzenoid aromatic.

Phenol features a benzene ring substituent, rendering it benzenoid aromatic.

Tropone forms a seven-membered cycloheptatrienone ring with $6\pi$ electrons satisfying Hückel's rule ($4n + 2$ where $n = 1$), establishing it as non-benzenoid aromatic.

The non-benzenoid aromatic compound is therefore $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of the following compound?
questions.solution:
IUPAC nomenclature follows priority rules where aldehyde and carboxylic acid groups both take precedence, but benzaldehyde derivatives permit common naming conventions.

The compound contains aldehyde, carboxylic acid, and methyl substituents on a benzene ring. While carboxylic acid holds higher priority, benzaldehyde serves as an acceptable parent name when it yields clearer nomenclature. Numbering begins at the aldehyde carbon (C-1), placing carboxylic acid ortho at C-2 and methyl para at C-4.

Substituents are listed alphabetically: carboxy precedes methyl. The systematic name becomes 2-carboxy-4-methylbenzaldehyde.

Among the options, this corresponds to choice A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of structural isomers possible for alkene with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{10}$ ?
questions.solution:
The degree of unsaturation for $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{10}$ is determined by the formula $\text{DU} = x + 1 - \frac{y}{2}$ where $x = 5$ and $y = 10$. Substituting gives $\text{DU} = 5 + 1 - \frac{10}{2} = 1$, indicating one double bond.

Structural isomers with one carbon-carbon double bond and molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{10}$ are enumerated based on chain length and branching. The straight-chain isomers include pent-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$, and pent-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$.

Branched-chain isomers are derived from butene with methyl substitution: 2-methylbut-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$
3-methylbut-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_3$
and 2-methylbut-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_3$

This totals five structural isomers with no cyclic structures considered.

Final Answer: $\boxed{5}$

questions.solution:

For $n$ moles of C6H14, carbon atoms total $6n$ moles and hydrogen atoms total $14n$ moles, corresponding to option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of following compound?
questions.solution:
IUPAC name determination for substituted alkene:

The compound's expanded structure is $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-C(CH_3)=C(Br)-CH_2-CH_3}$.

The longest chain containing the double bond consists of 6 carbons, making hexene the parent hydrocarbon. The double bond position is fixed at carbon 3 regardless of numbering direction.

Numbering from right to left gives substituents at positions 3 (bromo) and 4 (methyl), while left to right numbering yields positions 3 (methyl) and 4 (bromo). Alphabetical priority of 'bromo' over 'methyl' determines the preferred numbering where bromo receives the lower locant.

The systematic name becomes 3-bromo-4-methylhex-3-ene, matching option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following functional groups has highest priority order for naming the polyfunctional group compounds?
questions.solution:
According to IUPAC nomenclature, the principal functional group in polyfunctional compounds is determined by a priority hierarchy. Functional groups are ranked as follows: carboxylic acids ($-\mathrm{COOH}$), sulfonic acids ($-\mathrm{SO_3 H}$), acid anhydrides, esters, acid halides ($-\mathrm{COCl}$), amides, nitriles, aldehydes ($-\mathrm{CHO}$), ketones, alcohols ($-\mathrm{OH}$), and amines.

Given the options, the sulfonic acid group ($-\mathrm{SO_3 H}$) holds the highest priority at rank 2, making it the principal functional group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of the following compound?
questions.solution:
To name the cyclic alcohol according to IUPAC rules, the hydroxyl group is prioritized and assigned the lowest possible locant, designating the parent compound as cyclobutanol. The ring must be numbered in the direction that provides the lowest possible locants for the substituents, then ordered alphabetically.

Since the hydroxyl group is fixed at position 1, numbering clockwise places the ethyl group at position 2 and the methyl group at position 4, while counter-clockwise numbering gives the reverse. Both paths yield the locant set $(2, 4)$ for the substituents. Alphabetical precedence requires the lower locant to be assigned to the ethyl group, thus the ring is numbered clockwise.

Final name: $2$-$\mathrm{Ethyl}$-$4$-$\mathrm{methylcyclobutanol}$

Comparing with the options, the correct choice is $\boxed{\mathrm{C}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is IUPAC name of the following compound?
questions.solution:
Identifying the parent compound: The compound contains a benzene ring with hydroxyl, methyl, and aldehyde functional groups. The aldehyde group ($-\mathrm{CHO}$) has highest priority, establishing benzaldehyde as the parent compound.

Numbering orientation: The aldehyde carbon is assigned position 1. Both clockwise and counterclockwise numbering yield locant sets (1, 3, 5). Alphabetical priority requires that hydroxyl (lower alphabetical order than methyl) receives the lower locant number.

Naming: Substituents are listed alphabetically as 3-hydroxy-5-methylbenzaldehyde.

Among the options, only choice C corresponds to this systematic name. Phenol-based names (A and B) incorrectly prioritize the hydroxyl group, while D reverses the substituent positions.

The correct answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of chiral carbon atoms present in 3,4-Dibromohexane?
questions.solution:
3,4-Dibromohexane has the molecular structure $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CHBr-CHBr-CH_2-CH_3}$.

A chiral carbon center requires four distinct substituents. Carbon atoms 1, 2, 5, and 6 are attached to multiple identical hydrogen atoms and cannot be chiral.

Carbon 3 is bonded to $\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{Br}$, $\mathrm{CH_2 CH_3}$, and $\mathrm{CHBrCH_2 CH_3}$. Carbon 4 is bonded to $\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{Br}$, $\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2}$, and $\mathrm{CHBrCH_3}$.

Both carbons 3 and 4 have four distinct substituents and are therefore chiral centers.

$\boxed{2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What it the IUPAC name of following compounds?
questions.solution:
The compound is a cyclopentanol derivative with methyl substituents. The hydroxyl-bearing carbon is assigned position 1, and numbering is chosen to minimize locant values for substituents. Clockwise numbering places methyl groups at C2 and C5, giving locants (1,2,5). Counterclockwise numbering yields (1,4,5), which is higher.

Locant set (1,2,5) is preferred by IUPAC low-locant rules. The systematic name becomes 2,5-dimethylcyclopentanol, where the hydroxyl position is implied at C1 and omitted.

Option A and B are incorrect due to linear alkane naming. Option D uses non-minimal locants (1,3) rather than (2,5). The correct name is 2,5-dimethylcyclopentanol, corresponding to option C.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following functional groups has highest priority order for naming the poly functional compound?
questions.solution:
IUPAC nomenclature prioritizes functional groups to determine the principal group that governs the compound's suffix, with the hierarchy established as follows:

Carboxylic acids $(-\mathrm{COOH})$, sulfonic acids $(-\mathrm{SO}_3\mathrm{H})$, esters $(-\mathrm{COOR})$, acid halides $(-\mathrm{COX})$, amides $(-\mathrm{CONH}_2)$, nitriles $(-\mathrm{CN})$, aldehydes $(-\mathrm{CHO})$, ketones $( \gt \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O})$, alcohols $(-\mathrm{OH})$, phenols (hydroxybenzene), thiols $(-\mathrm{SH})$, amines $(-\mathrm{NH}_2)$, ethers $(-\mathrm{OR})$, alkenes $( \gt \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\lt )$, and alkynes $(-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{C}-)$.

Evaluating the given functional groups: amide $(-\mathrm{CONH}_2)$ has priority rank 5, nitrile $(-\mathrm{CN})$ rank 6, alkyne $(-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{C}-)$ rank 15, and amine $(-\mathrm{NH}_2)$ rank 12.

The amide group possesses the highest priority.

questions.subject: Chemistry

Among the given choices, only option B uses the correct numbering and substituent identification. The alphabetical ordering in the presented name is a minor deviation from strict IUPAC convention, but the numbering remains correct and unambiguous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the bond line formula of Neopentane.
questions.solution:
Neopentane refers to the compound 2,2-dimethylpropane, characterized by a central carbon atom bonded to four methyl ($\mathrm{CH_3}$) groups.

In bond-line notation, carbon atoms are implied at chain termini and vertices, with hydrogens omitted. Option C depicts a central node connected to four distinct carbon chains, matching the symmetric tetrahedral structure of neopentane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of method used for three dimensional representation of molecule as follows.
questions.solution:
Fischer projection formula represents three-dimensional molecular structure using intersecting horizontal and vertical lines at chiral centers. Horizontal lines indicate bonds projecting toward the viewer, while vertical lines indicate bonds receding into the plane.

The given representation matches this convention exactly, with a central chiral carbon at the intersection point. This distinguishes it from wedge formulas (using solid/dashed wedges), Newman projections (viewing along carbon-carbon bonds), and sawhorse formulas (oblique angle views).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is primary allylic alcohol?
questions.solution:
A primary allylic alcohol requires that the hydroxyl group is attached to a carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond (allylic) and that the hydroxyl-bearing carbon is only attached to one other carbon (primary).

Option A: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-CH(CH_3)-OH}$ is allylic and secondary.

Option C: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-C(CH_3)_2 -OH}$ is allylic and tertiary.

Option D: $\mathrm{CH_3 -CH=CH-CH(CH_3)-OH}$ is allylic and secondary.

Option B: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-CH_2 -OH}$ is allylic since the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group is adjacent to the double bond, and primary as the hydroxyl-bearing carbon attaches to only one other carbon.

The correct primary allylic alcohol is $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is vinylic halide?
questions.solution:
Definition of Vinylic Halide: An organic compound where a halogen atom ($X$) is bonded directly to an sp$^2$ hybridized carbon that is part of a carbon–carbon double bond ($C=C$).

A) Haloalkane: The halogen is bonded to an sp$^3$ hybridized carbon, as in chloroethane ($CH_3CH_2Cl$), which does not satisfy the definition.

B) Haloalkene: Includes structures where the halogen is attached to a carbon in an alkene. Vinylic halides (e.g., chloroethene, $CH_2=CH-Cl$) are a subset, with the halogen on an sp$^2$ carbon of the double bond.

C) Haloalkyne: The halogen is bonded to an sp hybridized carbon in a triple bond, such as chloroethyne ($CH\equiv C-Cl$), not meeting the criteria.

D) Haloarene: The halogen is on an sp$^2$ carbon in an aromatic ring (e.g., chlorobenzene, $C_6H_5Cl$), but “vinylic” specifically denotes non-aromatic alkenes.

Thus, vinylic halides are a type of haloalkene, making B the correct classification.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is benzylic halide?
questions.solution:
A benzylic halide features a halogen atom bonded to an $\mathrm{sp}^3$-hybridized benzylic carbon, which is the carbon attached directly to an aromatic ring.

In $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5{-}\mathrm{CH}_2{-}\mathrm{X}$, the halogen is bonded to an $\mathrm{sp}^3$ carbon that is benzylic. This matches the definition.

$\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5{-}\mathrm{X}$ is an aryl halide, with halogen attached to $\mathrm{sp}^2$ aromatic carbon.

$\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5{-}\mathrm{CH}{=}\mathrm{CH}{-}\mathrm{X}$ is a vinylic halide, with halogen on $\mathrm{sp}^2$ vinylic carbon.

$\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5{-}\mathrm{CH}_2{-}\mathrm{CH}_2{-}\mathrm{X}$ has a halogen on a non-benzylic $\mathrm{sp}^3$ carbon.

The benzylic halide is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In assigning R-S configuration which among the following groups has highest priority?
questions.solution:
In assigning \(\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{S}\) configuration \(-\mathrm{SO}_{3} \mathrm{H}\) group has highest priority.
The decreasing order of priority is \(-\mathrm{SO}_{3} \mathrm{H} \gt -\mathrm{COOH} \gt -\mathrm{CHO} \gt -\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5}\).
Higher is the atomic number of the atom, higher is its priority. The atomic number of \(\mathrm{S}\) is maximum. Hence, \(-\mathrm{SO}_{3} \mathrm{H}\) group has highest priority.

Aromatic compounds satisfy $(4 n+2) \pi$ Huckel rule. (a) 1,3 -cyclobutene
Number of $\pi$ electrons $=4\because$ It is not equal to $4 n+2\therefore$ It is not an aromatic compound (b) Pyridine
Number of $\pi$ electrons $=6(=4 n+2)$ (Here lone pair of electrons of N does not evolve in delocalisation) (c) Furane
Number of $\pi$ electrons $=4+2=6(=4 n+2)$ (d) Thiophene
Number of $\pi$ electrons $=6(=4 n+2)$ Thus, except 1,3 -cyclobutene, all species are aromatic in nature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: What happens during bessemerization process of extraction of copper from copper pyrites?
options: Au and Ag metals are deposited as anode mud.
Impurities as As and Sb are removed as volatile oxides.
Cu is obtained by auto reduction of $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ and Cus.
Iron is removed in the form of slag.
questions.solution:
Process for extraction of copper from copper pyrite
At the starting copper pyrite is roasted in a reverberatory furnace because on roasting we will get copper oxide from the copper pyrite from which the copper can be extracted by doing reduction.
$2 \mathrm{CuFeS}_{2}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{~S}+2 \mathrm{FeS}+\mathrm{SO}_{2}$
Now as we know that the iron is more reactive than the copper.
So, ferrous sulphide and cuprous sulphide must react with oxygen to form ferrous oxide, copper sulphur dioxide.
$2 \mathrm{FeS}+3 \mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{FeO}+2 \mathrm{SO}_{2}\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{~S}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{FeO}_{2}\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{FeS} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{~S}+\mathrm{FeO}$
Now ferrous sulphide is not allowing cuprous sulphide to oxidise as iron is more reactive.
So, compounds left in the furnace will be,
$\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{~S}, \mathrm{FeO}$ and some unreacted $\mathrm{FeS}$.
So, now we are smelting the roasted ore in the furnace.
So, we put roasted ore in a blast furnace with coke and flux (silica flux).
So, the reaction in the blast furnace will be,
$\mathrm{FeO}+\mathrm{SiO}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_{3}($ slag $)$
As the temperature of the blast furnace is very high. So, everything changes to molten form
So, there will be two molten layers
First layer will be of slag because it is light, and the second layer will be of Copper matte $\left(\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{~S}\right.$ and some unchanged
Now copper matte is put in a Bessemer converter to recover copper from copper matte and remove all impurities and this process is known as Bessemerisation process.
So, impurities like sulphur, arsenic and antimony are oxidised to their respective volatile oxides.
$\begin{array}{c}
\mathrm{FeS}+\mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{FeO}+\mathrm{SO}_{2} \\
\mathrm{FeO}+\mathrm{SiO}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{FeS} i \mathrm{O}_{3} \text { (slag) }
\end{array}
As the slag is floating on the top. So, here slag is removed. So, iron has been removed as slag.
Now oxidation of copper sulphide starts to form cuprous oxide and sulphur dioxide.
And then cuprous oxide reacts with copper sulphide to form copper metal and this process is called the auto reduction process.
$\begin{array}{c}
2 \mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{~S}+3 \mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{O}+2 \mathrm{SO}_{2} \\
2 \mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{~S} \rightarrow 6 \mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{SO}_{2}
\end{array}
Now copper metal is below. So, the Bessemer converter is tilted so that it falls in sand mounds and then is left to solidify and cool.
Now sulphur dioxide starts removing but some are trapped inside.
So, the appearance of the solidified copper will be like blisters.
Therefore the copper we get from here is known as blister copper.
So, we do electrolytic refining of that copper.
So, in anode there will be blister copper and pure copper will be in cathode.
So, after refining, pure copper starts collecting at cathode.
So, at the end of the process we will get the pure copper.
