questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In Finkelstein reaction, which one of the following reagents is used?
questions.solution:
The Finkelstein reaction is a halogen exchange reaction used for the synthesis of alkyl iodides from alkyl chlorides or alkyl bromides.

The reaction involves treating an alkyl chloride or bromide with sodium iodide (NaI) in dry acetone.

$R-X + NaI \xrightarrow{\text{dry acetone}} R-I + NaX \downarrow$

where $X = Cl, Br$.

Sodium iodide is soluble in dry acetone, whereas sodium chloride and sodium bromide are insoluble and precipitate out. This precipitation drives the forward reaction according to Le Chatelier's principle.

Answer: NaI in dry acetone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the major product formed when 2-bromopentane reacts with alcoholic KOH?
questions.solution:
Reaction of 2-bromopentane with alcoholic KOH undergoes dehydrohalogenation (E2 elimination).

$CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3 \xrightarrow{alc. KOH, \Delta} CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-CH_3 + CH_2=CH-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$

According to Zaitsev's rule, the more substituted alkene is formed as the major product.

Pent-2-ene is a disubstituted alkene, whereas pent-1-ene is a monosubstituted alkene.

Thus, pent-2-ene is the major product.

Answer: Pent-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent is used to convert Alkyl halide into Alkyl nitrite ?
questions.solution:
Potassium nitrite ($KNO_2$) is an ionic compound and provides nitrite ions ($NO_2^-$) in the solution. The nitrite ion is an ambidentate nucleophile with two donor sites: oxygen and nitrogen.

Since the $K-O$ bond is ionic, the negative charge on the oxygen atom is available for nucleophilic attack on the alkyl halide. This results in the formation of an alkyl nitrite ($R-O-N=O$) as the major product.

In contrast, silver nitrite ($AgNO_2$) has a covalent $Ag-O$ bond, making the lone pair on the nitrogen atom act as the nucleophile, which leads to the formation of a nitroalkane ($R-NO_2$).

Therefore, potassium nitrite is used to convert an alkyl halide into an alkyl nitrite.

Answer: Potassium nitrite

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is NOT a feature of $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism ?
options: Involves simultaneous bond breaking and bond forming
questions.solution:
The $S_N2$ mechanism is a single-step concerted reaction where bond breaking and bond forming occur simultaneously.

It involves the backside attack of the nucleophile on the substrate, leading to the inversion of configuration.

The reaction proceeds via a transition state and does not involve the formation of any intermediate.

The formation of a planar carbocation intermediate is a characteristic feature of the $S_N1$ mechanism, not the $S_N2$ mechanism.

Answer: Formation of planar carbocation intermediate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product 'B' in the following reaction sequence.
questions.solution:
The given reaction sequence involves the formation of a Grignard reagent followed by its reaction with an alcohol.

The reactant 2-chlorobutane reacts with magnesium (Mg) in the presence of dry ether to form a Grignard reagent, sec-butylmagnesium chloride (A).
$CH_3-CH_2-CH(Cl)-CH_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Mg, Dry ether}} CH_3-CH_2-CH(MgCl)-CH_3$

Grignard reagents are strong bases and react vigorously with compounds containing acidic hydrogen atoms, such as alcohols, water, and amines, to form alkanes. Ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$) provides an acidic proton.
The sec-butylmagnesium chloride abstracts a proton from ethanol to form butane (B) and an alkoxide salt.
$CH_3-CH_2-CH(MgCl)-CH_3 + C_2H_5OH \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3 + Mg(OC_2H_5)Cl$

Therefore, the final product 'B' is butane, which corresponds to the skeletal structure shown in the second option.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the product B in following reaction.
$\text{CH}_3\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{KCN}}} \text{A} \xrightarrow[\large{\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}}]{\large{\text{Na}}} \text{B}$
questions.solution:
The reaction of methyl bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$) with potassium cyanide ($\text{KCN}$) is a nucleophilic substitution reaction which yields ethanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$) as the major product A.

$\text{CH}_3\text{Br} + \text{KCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CN} + \text{KBr}$

The reduction of ethanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$) with sodium and ethanol ($\text{Na} / \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) is known as the Mendius reduction. It reduces the nitrile group to a primary amine, yielding ethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$) as product B.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} + 4[\text{H}] \xrightarrow{\text{Na} / \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$

Answer: Ethanamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following compounds is not obtained when methyl bromide is treated with ethyl bromide in presence of sodium metal in dry ether?
questions.solution:
The reaction of methyl bromide and ethyl bromide with sodium metal in dry ether is an example of the Wurtz reaction.

The alkyl free radicals formed during the reaction are methyl radical ($CH_3^{\bullet}$) and ethyl radical ($C_2H_5^{\bullet}$).

These radicals can undergo self-coupling as well as cross-coupling to give a mixture of alkanes:

$CH_3^{\bullet} + CH_3^{\bullet} \rightarrow CH_3-CH_3$ (Ethane)

$C_2H_5^{\bullet} + C_2H_5^{\bullet} \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$ (n-Butane)

$CH_3^{\bullet} + C_2H_5^{\bullet} \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH_3$ (Propane)

2-methyl propane cannot be formed by the coupling of methyl and ethyl radicals. Therefore, 2-methyl propane is not obtained in this reaction.

Answer: 2-methyl propane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following $n$ mole compound is obtained when $2n$ moles of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ treated of with $2n$ mole sodium atom in dry ether?
questions.solution:
The reaction of an aryl halide with sodium in the presence of dry ether to form a diaryl compound is known as the Fittig reaction.

The chemical equation for the reaction is:

$2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5 + 2\text{NaCl}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $2$ moles of chlorobenzene react with $2$ moles of sodium to produce $1$ mole of biphenyl.

Therefore, $2n$ moles of chlorobenzene reacting with $2n$ moles of sodium will produce $n$ moles of biphenyl.

Answer: Biphenyl

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify reagent B in following reaction.
$\text{R}-\text{X} \xrightarrow{\ \large{\text{B}}\ } \text{Nitroalkane}$
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alkyl halide with silver nitrite ($\text{AgNO}_2$) yields a nitroalkane as the major product.

$\text{AgNO}_2$ is predominantly covalent in nature. The bond between silver and oxygen ($\text{Ag}-\text{O}$) is covalent, which leaves the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom available for nucleophilic attack.

Therefore, the nucleophilic attack on the alkyl halide occurs through the nitrogen atom, resulting in the formation of a nitroalkane ($\text{R}-\text{NO}_2$).

In contrast, potassium nitrite ($\text{KNO}_2$) is an ionic compound and provides nitrite ions ($\text{NO}_2^-$) in which oxygen is the nucleophilic center, leading to the formation of alkyl nitrites ($\text{R}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$).

Thus, reagent B is $\text{Ag}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$.

Answer: $\text{Ag} - \text{O} - \text{N} = \text{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify substrate 'S' in the following reaction.
$\text{S} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{Na / dry ether}}}$ 3, 4 - diethyl - 3, 4 - dimethyl hexane
questions.solution:
The given reaction is a Wurtz reaction, which involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules in the presence of sodium and dry ether to form a symmetrical alkane.

The structure of the product, 3,4-diethyl-3,4-dimethylhexane, is:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)-C(CH}_3\text{)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$

Since the Wurtz reaction produces a symmetrical alkane by the dimerization of alkyl radicals, we can determine the structure of the reactant by cleaving the central carbon-carbon bond of the product.

Cleaving the bond between C3 and C4 yields two identical radicals:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-C}^{\bullet}\text{(CH}_3\text{)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3)$

The corresponding alkyl halide substrate 'S' is formed by attaching a halogen (e.g., chlorine) to the radical carbon:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-C(Cl)(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3$

The longest carbon chain has 5 carbon atoms. Numbering the chain from either side gives the same locants, with a chloro group and a methyl group at the 3rd carbon.

Thus, the IUPAC name of the substrate 'S' is 3-chloro-3-methylpentane.

Answer: 3 - chloro - 3 - methylpentane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of aryl halide with sodium metal in dry ether to give biphenyl is known as
questions.solution:
The reaction of an aryl halide with sodium metal in the presence of dry ether to form biphenyl is known as the Fittig reaction.

$2\text{Ar-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar-Ar} + 2\text{NaX}$

The Wurtz reaction involves two alkyl halides to form an alkane, while the Wurtz-Fittig reaction involves one alkyl halide and one aryl halide to form an alkylarene. The Swarts reaction is used for the synthesis of alkyl fluorides.

Answer: Fittig reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when 2- Chloro - 2 - methylbutane is reacted with sodium metal in presence of dry ether?
questions.solution:
The given reactant is 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, which has the structure $CH_3-C(Cl)(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$.

When reacted with sodium metal in the presence of dry ether, it undergoes the Wurtz reaction.

The reaction proceeds via the formation of an alkyl free radical. The cleavage of the $C-Cl$ bond yields the radical $CH_3-C^{\bullet}(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$.

Two such radicals dimerize to form the final alkane product:

$2 CH_3-C(Cl)(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3 + 2 Na \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-C(CH_3)_2-C(CH_3)_2-CH_2-CH_3 + 2 NaCl$

The longest continuous carbon chain in the product contains 6 carbon atoms, making the parent chain a hexane. Numbering the chain from either end gives substituents at the 3rd and 4th positions.

There are four methyl groups attached to the main chain, two at C-3 and two at C-4. Thus, the IUPAC name of the product is $3,3,4,4-$tetramethylhexane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when 2-chlorobutane is heated with aqueous solution of potassium hydroxide.
questions.solution:
When an alkyl halide is treated with an aqueous solution of potassium hydroxide (KOH), it undergoes a nucleophilic substitution reaction. The hydroxide ion ($OH^-$) acts as a nucleophile and replaces the halogen atom.

For 2-chlorobutane, the reaction proceeds as follows:

$CH_3-CH(Cl)-CH_2-CH_3 + KOH(aq) \xrightarrow{\Delta} CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_2-CH_3 + KCl$

The chlorine atom at the second carbon is substituted by a hydroxyl group, resulting in the formation of Butan-2-ol.

Answer: Butan - 2 - ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is allylic halide?
questions.solution:
An allylic halide is a compound in which the halogen atom is bonded to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom that is adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond ($C=C$).

In $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{X}$, the halogen is attached to an $sp^3$ carbon of an alkane chain, making it an alkyl halide.

In $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5 - \text{CH}_2 - \text{X}$, the halogen is attached to an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to a benzene ring, making it a benzylic halide.

In $\text{CH}_2 = \text{CH} - \text{CH}_2 - \text{X}$, the halogen is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom which is directly bonded to a carbon-carbon double bond. This is an allylic halide.

In $\text{CH}_3 - \text{CH} = \text{CH} - \text{X}$, the halogen is attached directly to an $sp^2$ hybridized carbon of a double bond, making it a vinylic halide.

Answer: $\text{CH}_2 = \text{CH} - \text{CH}_2 - \text{X}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is used for the preparation of alkyl fluorides from alkyl chlorides?
questions.solution:
Swarts reaction is the standard method used for the preparation of alkyl fluorides from alkyl chlorides or bromides.

In this reaction, heating an alkyl chloride or bromide in the presence of a metallic fluoride such as $AgF$, $Hg_2F_2$, $CoF_3$, or $SbF_3$ yields the corresponding alkyl fluoride.

$R-Cl + AgF \rightarrow R-F + AgCl$

Finkelstein reaction is used for the preparation of alkyl iodides.

Sandmeyer's reaction is used for the preparation of aryl halides from diazonium salts.

Fittig reaction is used for the preparation of diaryls from aryl halides.

Answer: Swartz reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the product P obtained in following reaction?
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{AgCN}_{(alc)} \rightarrow \text{P}$
questions.solution:
$\text{AgCN}$ is predominantly a covalent compound. The bond between $\text{Ag}$ and $\text{C}$ is covalent, which leaves the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom available for nucleophilic attack.

When an alkyl halide such as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ reacts with alcoholic $\text{AgCN}$, the nucleophilic attack occurs through the nitrogen atom rather than the carbon atom.

This results in the formation of an alkyl isocyanide as the major product.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{AgCN}_{(alc)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC} + \text{AgBr}$

The product P is ethyl isocyanide, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent used for replacement of $-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ from benzene diazonium chloride by iodine.
questions.solution:
Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with aqueous potassium iodide (KI) upon warming to form iodobenzene.

The reaction is given by:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{KI} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{I} + \text{N}_2 + \text{KCl}$

Therefore, the reagent used for the replacement of the diazonium group by iodine is KI.

Answer: KI

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl halides undergoes $\text{SN}^1$ reaction most readily?
questions.solution:
The rate of an $\text{SN}^1$ reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation formed and the leaving group ability of the halide ion.

Since the alkyl group is the same in all the given options, the carbocation formed is the tert-butyl carbocation, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$, in each case.

The rate of reaction will therefore depend on the leaving group ability of the halide ion. A better leaving group leads to a faster reaction.

The leaving group ability increases as the size of the halogen atom increases and the carbon-halogen bond strength decreases. The order of bond dissociation energy is $\text{C-F} \gt \text{C-Cl} \gt \text{C-Br} \gt \text{C-I}$.

Thus, the iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) is the best leaving group among the halides.

Therefore, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I}$ undergoes the $\text{SN}^1$ reaction most readily.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-I}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl halides is hydrolyzed most rapidly by the $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism ?
questions.solution:
The rate of an $\text{SN}^2$ reaction is inversely proportional to the steric hindrance around the carbon atom bearing the leaving group.

The order of reactivity of alkyl halides towards $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism is:
Methyl halide $ \gt 1^{\circ}$ alkyl halide $ \gt 2^{\circ}$ alkyl halide $ \gt 3^{\circ}$ alkyl halide.

Among the given options:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-Br}$ is a methyl halide.
$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-Br}$ is a $1^{\circ}$ alkyl halide.
$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-Br}$ is a $2^{\circ}$ alkyl halide.
$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-Br}$ is a $3^{\circ}$ alkyl halide.

Since $\text{CH}_3\text{-Br}$ has the least steric hindrance, it is hydrolyzed most rapidly by the $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{-Br}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Method of preparation of alkyl halide
$2\text{R-Br} + \text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{R-F} + \text{Hg}_2\text{Br}_2$
This reaction is known as
questions.solution:
The synthesis of alkyl fluorides is best accomplished by heating an alkyl chloride or bromide in the presence of a metallic fluoride such as $\text{AgF}$, $\text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2$, $\text{CoF}_2$, or $\text{SbF}_3$.

The given reaction involves the conversion of an alkyl bromide to an alkyl fluoride using mercurous fluoride ($\text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2$).

$2\text{R-Br} + \text{Hg}_2\text{F}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{R-F} + \text{Hg}_2\text{Br}_2$

This halogen exchange reaction for the preparation of alkyl fluorides is known as the Swarts reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In benzylic halides, the halogen atom is bonded to
questions.solution:
In benzylic halides, the halogen atom is bonded to an alkyl carbon atom that is directly attached to an aromatic ring (benzene ring).

The general structure of a benzylic halide is $\text{Ar-CH}_2\text{-X}$.

The benzylic carbon atom forms four single ($\sigma$) bonds: one with the aromatic ring, two with hydrogen atoms, and one with the halogen atom.

Since it forms four $\sigma$ bonds and zero $\pi$ bonds, the hybridization of the benzylic carbon atom is $\text{sp}^3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct feature of the $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism?
options: The $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism proceeds mainly with racemization.
The $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism includes a transition state with penta coordinating carbon.
The $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism involves formation of planar carbocation intermediate in the first step.
The $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism involves formation of carbocation with $\text{SP}^2$ hybridized carbon.
questions.solution:
The $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism is a concerted, single-step process where the nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbon from the side opposite to the leaving group.

During this process, a transition state is formed in which the central carbon atom is partially bonded to five groups (the incoming nucleophile, the leaving group, and three other substituents), making it penta-coordinated.

There is no carbocation intermediate formed in the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism, which rules out the formation of a planar $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbocation.

The reaction proceeds with complete inversion of configuration (Walden inversion), not racemization.

Answer: The $\text{SN}^2$ mechanism includes a transition state with penta coordinating carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is used as solvent for Grignard reagent?
questions.solution:
Grignard reagents ($RMgX$) are highly reactive compounds that act as strong bases and nucleophiles.

Solvents with acidic protons, such as alcohols and phenols, react with Grignard reagents to form alkanes, thereby destroying the reagent.

Similarly, solvents with electrophilic carbonyl groups, such as ketones, undergo nucleophilic addition with Grignard reagents.

Ether is an aprotic solvent that does not react with Grignard reagents.

Furthermore, the lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom of ether coordinate with the electron-deficient magnesium atom, stabilizing the reagent.

Therefore, ether is the suitable solvent for Grignard reagents.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the general molecular formula of alkyl halides?
questions.solution:
Alkanes have the general molecular formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$.

Alkyl halides are formed by replacing one hydrogen atom of an alkane with a halogen atom ($\text{X}$).

Removing one hydrogen atom from an alkane gives an alkyl group with the general formula $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+1}$.

Attaching a halogen atom to the alkyl group gives the general molecular formula of alkyl halides as $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+1}\text{X}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+1}\text{X}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following halogen derivative forms a poisonous phosgene, when come in contact with air and light?
questions.solution:
Chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) is slowly oxidized by oxygen in the presence of light to form a highly poisonous gas, carbonyl chloride, which is commonly known as phosgene.

The chemical reaction is given by:

$2\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\text{COCl}_2 + 2\text{HCl}$

Therefore, $\text{CHCl}_3$ forms poisonous phosgene when it comes in contact with air and light.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following favors $\text{SN}^1$ reaction?
options: Bulky alkyl groups on the carbon atom attached to halogen atom
Small alkyl groups on the carbon atom attached to halogen atom
questions.solution:
The $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reaction proceeds via the formation of a carbocation intermediate in its rate-determining step.

Bulky alkyl groups on the carbon atom attached to the halogen atom (such as in tertiary alkyl halides) stabilize the resulting carbocation through the $+I$ inductive effect and hyperconjugation. Additionally, the steric crowding in the initial tetrahedral substrate is relieved when it forms a planar carbocation, which provides a driving force for the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism.

In contrast, a strong nucleophile and small alkyl groups favor the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism, while non-polar solvents do not favor the ionization step required for $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$.

Answer: Bulky alkyl groups on the carbon atom attached to halogen atom

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the importance of Sandmeyer's reaction?
options: To obtain Ar-X by replacing diazo group of $\text{AR-N}_2^+\text{-X}^-$ using $\text{CuCl}$ / $\text{HCl}$
To obtain R-F from R-Cl using AgF
To obtain $\text{R-CH}_2\text{-R}$ from R-CO-R using Zn-Hg / HCl
questions.solution:
Sandmeyer's reaction is a chemical reaction used to synthesize aryl halides from aryl diazonium salts. It involves the replacement of the diazonium group ($-\text{N}_2^+$) in $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{X}^-$ by a halogen atom (such as Cl or Br) or a cyanide group using copper(I) salts like $\text{CuCl}/\text{HCl}$, $\text{CuBr}/\text{HBr}$, or $\text{CuCN}/\text{KCN}$.

The reaction to obtain R-I from R-Cl is known as the Finkelstein reaction.

The reaction to obtain R-F from R-Cl using AgF is known as the Swarts reaction.

The reaction to obtain $\text{R-CH}_2\text{-R}$ from R-CO-R using Zn-Hg / HCl is known as the Clemmensen reduction.

Therefore, Sandmeyer's reaction is used to obtain Ar-X by replacing the diazo group of $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{X}^-$ using $\text{CuCl}$ / $\text{HCl}$.

Answer: To obtain Ar-X by replacing diazo group of $\text{AR-N}_2^+\text{-X}^-$ using $\text{CuCl}$ / $\text{HCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is obtained when Bromoethane is reacted with silver acetate?
questions.solution:
The reaction between bromoethane and silver acetate is a nucleophilic substitution reaction.

The acetate ion ($CH_3COO^-$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbon of bromoethane ($CH_3CH_2Br$), displacing the bromide ion.

The chemical equation for the reaction is:
$CH_3CH_2Br + CH_3COOAg \rightarrow CH_3COOCH_2CH_3 + AgBr \downarrow$

The product formed is $CH_3COOCH_2CH_3$, which is ethyl acetate.

Answer: ethyl acetate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the major product of dehydrohalogenation of $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(Br)-CH}_3$.
questions.solution:
Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(Br)-CH}_3$) involves the removal of a hydrogen atom from a $\beta$-carbon and the bromine atom from the $\alpha$-carbon.

There are two $\beta$-carbons in 2-bromobutane, leading to two possible alkene products:
1. Removal of hydrogen from C1 yields 1-butene ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH=CH}_2$).
2. Removal of hydrogen from C3 yields 2-butene ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_3$).

According to Zaitsev's rule, the major product in a dehydrohalogenation reaction is the more substituted alkene, as it is thermodynamically more stable.

2-butene is a disubstituted alkene, whereas 1-butene is a monosubstituted alkene.

Thus, 2-butene ($\text{H}_3\text{C-CH=CH-CH}_3$) is the major product.

Answer: $\text{H}_3\text{C-CH=CH-CH}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is formed when chloroform is exposed to air and light?
questions.solution:
Chloroform ($CHCl_3$) undergoes slow oxidation in the presence of air and light to form a highly poisonous gas called phosgene ($COCl_2$).

The chemical equation for this reaction is:

$2CHCl_3 + O_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2COCl_2 + 2HCl$

Thus, phosgene is the compound formed.

Answer: Phosgene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product 'B' in the below mentioned reaction is-
questions.solution:
The given reactant is 2-bromopropane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$).

When 2-bromopropane is treated with alcoholic KOH and heated, it undergoes dehydrohalogenation ($\beta$-elimination) to form propene (A).
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Alc. KOH, } \Delta} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$

Next, propene (A) reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxide. This is an electrophilic addition reaction that follows Markovnikov's rule. The negative part of the addendum ($\text{Br}^-$) attaches to the carbon atom of the double bond that has fewer hydrogen atoms.
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{\text{Peroxide absent}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_3$

Thus, the major product 'B' is 2-bromopropane.

Answer: 2-Bromopropane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Wurtz reaction is NOT possible with
questions.solution:
Wurtz reaction is used for the preparation of higher alkanes from alkyl halides using sodium metal in dry ether.

Primary and secondary alkyl halides readily undergo Wurtz reaction to form alkanes.

Tertiary alkyl halides, due to high steric hindrance, undergo dehydrohalogenation (elimination) rather than coupling when treated with sodium in dry ether, resulting in the formation of alkenes instead of alkanes.

Among the given options, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$ is a tertiary alkyl halide, so it does not undergo Wurtz reaction.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following factors proceeds more rapidly, unimolecular nucleophilic substitution reaction?
questions.solution:
Unimolecular nucleophilic substitution ($S_{N}1$) reactions proceed via the formation of a carbocation intermediate in the rate-determining step.

Polar protic solvents have high dielectric constants and are capable of hydrogen bonding. They stabilize both the carbocation intermediate and the leaving group anion through solvation. This stabilization lowers the activation energy required for the cleavage of the carbon-halogen bond, thereby increasing the rate of the $S_{N}1$ reaction.

The strength of the nucleophile does not affect the rate of an $S_{N}1$ reaction because the nucleophile is not involved in the rate-determining step. Aprotic solvents generally favor $S_{N}2$ reactions.

Answer: Polar protic solvent

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify ' $A$ ' in the following reaction.
$\text { A }+ \text { Acetyl chloride } \xrightarrow[\mathrm{AlCl}_3]{\text { anhydrous }} 1 \text { - chloroacetophenone }+4 \text {-chloroacetophenone }$
questions.solution:
The given Friedel-Crafts acylation reaction produces both 1-chloroacetophenone (ortho-substituted isomer) and 4-chloroacetophenone, indicating chlorobenzene as the aromatic substrate, with chlorine directing electrophilic substitution to ortho and para positions.

From acetyl chloride $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COCl}$ and anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$, the acyl group attaches to positions activated by chlorine. Benzene yields only acetophenone, toluene gives methylacetophenones, and phenol produces hydroxyacetophenones, all inconsistent with the chloro-substituted products.

Chlorobenzene undergoes acylation at ortho and para positions, forming 2-chloroacetophenone and 4-chloroacetophenone, matching the observed outcome.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is obtained as major product when excess of methane is treated with limited chlorine in presence of UV light?
questions.solution:
The reaction between methane and chlorine under UV light proceeds through free radical substitution mechanisms.

The primary reaction yields chloromethane: $\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV light}} \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{HCl}$.

While subsequent chlorination is possible: $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 + \text{HCl}$, $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CHCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$, $\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CCl}_4 + \text{HCl}$,
an excess of methane with limited chlorine favors monochlorination.
The high concentration of methane increases the probability of chlorine radicals reacting with $\text{CH}_4$ rather than chlorinated derivatives.

Chloromethane is therefore the major product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reagents is used in the preparation of nitroalkane from haloalkane?
questions.solution:
Haloalkanes undergo nucleophilic substitution with nitrite ions ($\text{NO}_2^-$), which are ambident nucleophiles capable of attacking through either oxygen or nitrogen atoms.

Alkali metal nitrites like KNO_2$ and NaNO_2$ are predominantly ionic, with oxygen's higher electronegativity making it the preferred nucleophilic site, yielding alkyl nitrites: R–X + KNO_2\rightarrow$ R–O–N=O + KX.

Silver nitrite (AgNO_2$) is covalent, with the Ag–O bond reducing oxygen's nucleophilicity and favoring nitrogen attack, producing nitroalkanes: R–X + AgNO_2\rightarrow$ R–NO_2$ + AgX.

To prepare nitroalkanes from haloalkanes, silver nitrite is the preferred reagent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the order of reactivity of alkyl halides with ammonia?
questions.solution:
Reactivity of alkyl halides with ammonia depends on nucleophilic substitution mechanisms, where ammonia acts as a nucleophile. The key factor is the leaving group ability of the halide ion.

Leaving group ability is inversely related to basicity. Comparing halides: iodine is the weakest base and thus the best leaving group, followed by bromine and then chlorine. This gives the order I- > Br- > Cl- for leaving group quality.

Consequently, alkyl halide reactivity follows: $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl}$.

Evaluating the options:
A) $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I}$ (Incorrect)
B) $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl}$ (Incorrect)
C) $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl}$ (Correct)
D) $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I} \gt \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B}$ (Incorrect)

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is haloarene?
questions.solution:
Haloarenes are characterized by a halogen atom directly bonded to an aromatic ring carbon. In A ($C_6H_5CH_2X$), the halogen is benzylic, not aromatic. B and C feature halogens attached to non-aromatic cycloalkene and cycloalkane rings, respectively.

Only D ($C_6H_5X$) has the halogen bonded directly to the benzene ring, satisfying the haloarene definition.

Answer: D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is benzylic halide?
questions.solution: No Solution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Select the correct decreasing order of boiling points of compounds from the following.
questions.solution:
Intermolecular forces dictate boiling points, with London dispersion forces dominating as molecular mass increases due to stronger temporary dipoles. All compounds are polar, exhibiting dipole-dipole interactions, but mass is the primary factor here.

Molecular masses are calculated as:

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl} = 50.5$ g/mol, $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Br} = 95$ g/mol, $\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}_2 = 174$ g/mol, $\mathrm{CHBr}_3 = 253$ g/mol

Boiling point increases with molecular mass, so the decreasing order is:

$\mathrm{CHBr}_3 \gt \mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br}_2 \gt \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Br} \gt \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl}$

Option D matches this sequence.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a fittig reaction?
questions.solution:
The Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides with sodium in dry ether to form a biaryl compound:

$2 \text{Ar-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar-Ar} + 2\text{NaX}$

Option A: $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{CH}_3+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ involves an aryl halide and an alkyl halide, characteristic of the Wurtz–Fittig reaction.

Option B: $2 \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ uses only alkyl halides, indicating the Wurtz reaction.

Option C: $2 \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_3+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ also uses alkyl halides and is another Wurtz reaction.

Option D: $2 \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Br}+2 \mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5-\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5+2 \mathrm{NaBr}$ couples two aryl halides to form biphenyl, matching the definition of the Fittig reaction.

The Fittig reaction is represented by option D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product when chlorobenzene is heated with nitrating mixture.
questions.solution:
Nitration of chlorobenzene proceeds via electrophilic aromatic substitution with the nitronium ion $\mathrm{NO_2+}$.

The chloro substituent exhibits both inductive electron-withdrawing and mesomeric electron-donating effects, rendering it ortho-para directing while deactivating the ring. Attack occurs at both ortho and para positions relative to chlorine.

This yields two isomeric products: 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene and 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene.

The para isomer predominates due to reduced steric hindrance compared to the ortho position.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds does not exhibit optical isomerism?
questions.solution:
Optical isomerism requires chirality, typically from a chiral carbon bonded to four distinct groups.

3-Iodohexane has a chiral carbon at position 3 bonded to -H, -I, -CH2CH3, and -CH2CH2CH3, so it exhibits optical isomerism.

2-Iodopentane has a chiral carbon at position 2 bonded to -H, -I, -CH3, and -CH2CH2CH3, so it exhibits optical isomerism.

2-Iodo-2-methylbutane has a carbon at position 2 bonded to -I, -CH3, another -CH3, and -CH2CH3. With two identical methyl groups, it is not chiral and does not exhibit optical isomerism.

2-Iodo-3-methylbutane has a chiral carbon at position 2 bonded to -H, -I, -CH3, and -CH(CH3)2, so it exhibits optical isomerism.

Thus, the compound that does not exhibit optical isomerism is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product formed when 2-Bromobutane is heated with aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide.
questions.solution:
2-Bromobutane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3}$) is a secondary alkyl halide reacting with sodium hydroxide, a strong nucleophile and base, in aqueous solution under heating. The polar protic solvent facilitates solvation and favors nucleophilic substitution.

Hydroxide ion attacks the electrophilic carbon, displacing bromide via $\mathrm{S_N2}$: $\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3 + OH- \rightarrow CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH_3 + Br^-}$, yielding butan-2-ol.

Concurrently, elimination may occur via $\mathrm{E2}$, abstracting a $\beta$-hydrogen to form either but-1-ene or but-2-ene: $\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3 + OH- \rightarrow CH_3CH=CHCH_3 + H_2 O + Br^-}$ or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3 + OH- \rightarrow CH_2=CHCH_2CH_3 + H_2 O + Br^-}$. Zaitsev's rule predicts but-2-ene as the major elimination product.

In aqueous solvent, $\mathrm{S_N2}$ dominates over $\mathrm{E2}$ due to solvation effects that stabilize the substitution transition state. Butan-2-ol is thus the major product.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT obtained when mixture of methyl bromide and ethyl bromide is treated with sodium metal in presence of dry ether?
questions.solution:
Wurtz reaction of alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether yields alkanes via self-coupling and cross-coupling. For methyl bromide ($\mathrm{CH_3Br}$) and ethyl bromide ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2 Br}$), the products arise from three distinct pathways.

Self-coupling of methyl bromide: $2\mathrm{CH_3Br} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH_3CH_3} + 2\mathrm{NaBr}$, yielding ethane.

Self-coupling of ethyl bromide: $2\mathrm{CH_3CH_2 Br} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3} + 2\mathrm{NaBr}$, yielding butane.

Cross-coupling: $\mathrm{CH_3Br} + \mathrm{CH_3CH_2 Br} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_3} + 2\mathrm{NaBr}$, yielding propane.

The alkanes obtained are ethane, propane, and butane. Pentane is not formed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate percentage atom economy when 46 g ethanol is obtained from 64.5 g chloroethane and $56 \mathrm{~g~} \mathrm{KOH} (\mathrm{aq})$
questions.solution:
The reaction proceeds by nucleophilic substitution:

$\mathrm{C_2H_5Cl} + \mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + \mathrm{KCl}$

Percentage atom economy evaluates the mass efficiency of the desired product formation:

$\text{Percentage Atom Economy} = \frac{\text{Mass of desired product}}{\text{Total mass of all reactants}} \times 100\%$

Given $64.5\text{ g}$ chloroethane and $56\text{ g}$ potassium hydroxide produce $46\text{ g}$ ethanol, the total reactant mass sums to $120.5\text{ g}$. The atom economy becomes:

$\frac{46}{120.5} \times 100\% \approx 38.17\%$

This result could be confirmed by computing the total product mass: $46\text{ g ethanol} + 74.5\text{ g KCl} = 120.5\text{ g}$, yielding an identical fraction. The correct answer is B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is likely to undergo racemization during alkaline hydrolysis by $\mathrm{SN}^1$ mechanism?
questions.solution:
Racemization occurs during alkaline hydrolysis via $\mathrm{SN}^1$ mechanism when a chiral center forms a planar carbocation intermediate, allowing nucleophilic attack from either face with equal probability.

A) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{CH}_3$ contains a non-chiral carbon bonded to two identical methyl groups.

B) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has a chiral carbon bonded to $\mathrm{CH}_3$, $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5$, $\mathrm{H}$, and $\mathrm{Cl}$. Alkaline hydrolysis proceeds through a secondary carbocation intermediate, resulting in racemization.

C) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Cl})-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$ features a non-chiral carbon with two identical ethyl groups.

D) $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{Cl}$ contains a primary non-chiral carbon and is unlikely to proceed via $\mathrm{SN}^1$ mechanism.

The only compound satisfying both chirality and $\mathrm{SN}^1$ pathway requirements is B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify ' $A$ ' in the following reaction.
$\underset{\text { (excess) }}{\mathrm{A}}$ + $\underset{\text { (excess) }}{\mathrm{Acetyl \ chloride}}\xrightarrow[\mathrm{AlCl}_3]{\text { Anhydrous }} 1$-Chloroacetophenone + 4-chloroacetophenone
questions.solution:
Friedel-Crafts acylation of aromatic compound A with acetyl chloride yields both ortho- and para-chloroacetophenone products, indicating the presence of a chlorine substituent originating from A.

The acetyl group directs substitution to positions ortho and para relative to existing substituents. Since both chloroacetophenone isomers are formed, A must contain a chlorine atom attached to the aromatic ring that acts as an ortho-para director.

Among the options, only chlorobenzene satisfies these conditions: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + \text{CH}_3\text{COCl} \xrightarrow[\text{AlCl}_3]{\text{Anhydrous}} \text{ortho-ClC}_6\text{H}_4\text{COCH}_3 + \text{para-ClC}_6\text{H}_4\text{COCH}_3$.

Benzene would yield simple acetophenone without chlorine, while toluene and phenol would produce methyl- and hydroxy-substituted acetophenones respectively, inconsistent with the observed products.

The correct starting material is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds has difficulty in breaking of C-X bond?
questions.solution:
The nucleophilic aromatic substitution mechanism requires electron-withdrawing groups to stabilize the intermediate Meisenheimer complex via resonance. o-Nitrochlorobenzene and p-nitrochlorobenzene position their nitro groups optimally for resonance stabilization of the negative charge at the reaction site.

2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene features three nitro groups providing exceptional resonance stabilization, making its C-Cl bond easiest to cleave.

m-Nitrochlorobenzene cannot provide resonance stabilization to the intermediate since the meta-position nitro group operates primarily through inductive effects. This results in the least stabilized intermediate and therefore the most difficult C-Cl bond cleavage.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of aryl halide with sodium metal in dry ether to give biphenyl is known as
questions.solution:
The reaction of aryl halides with sodium metal in dry ether to form biphenyl constitutes the Fittig reaction. This transformation produces biaryl compounds through the general reaction $\mathrm{Ar-X + 2Na + X-Ar \rightarrow Ar-Ar + 2NaX}$.

The Swartz reaction employs metallic fluorides to synthesize alkyl fluorides and does not involve aryl halides or biphenyl formation. The Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides to form alkanes: $\mathrm{R-X + 2Na + X-R \rightarrow R-R + 2NaX}$.

Although the Wurtz-Fittig reaction involves aryl halides, it requires an alkyl halide co-reactant and produces alkylarenes rather than biaryls.

Since the transformation specifically couples two aryl halide molecules to form a biaryl compound, it corresponds exclusively to the Fittig reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has highest reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution reaction involving cleavage of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond?
questions.solution:
Electron-withdrawing groups at ortho and para positions enhance nucleophilic aromatic substitution by stabilizing the Meisenheimer complex through resonance.

Chlorobenzene lacks electron-withdrawing groups and shows minimal reactivity.

p-Nitrochlorobenzene has one nitro group at the para position, providing moderate stabilization.

2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene features nitro groups at ortho and para positions, offering greater stabilization.

2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene possesses three nitro groups at ortho and para positions, delivering maximum stabilization and thus the highest reactivity.

The reactivity order is chlorobenzene $\ll$ p-nitrochlorobenzene < 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene < 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following statements is true for haloalkyne?
options: Halogen atom is bonded to 'sp' hybridised carbon atom.
Halogen atom is bonded to ' $s p^{2 \text { ' }}$ hybridised carbon atom of aliphatic chain.
Halogen atom is bonded to ' $s p^{3 \text { ' }}$ hybridised carbon atom next to a carbon-carbon double bond.
Halogen atom is bonded to ' $\mathrm{sp}^{2 '}$ hybridised carbon atom of aromatic ring.
questions.solution:
Haloalkynes are characterized by containing both a halogen atom and a carbon–carbon triple bond.

Carbon atoms in triple bonds are $sp$ hybridized. Therefore, a halogen attached directly to such a carbon satisfies the definition of a haloalkyne, as in chloroethyne, HC≡CCl.

In contrast, option B describes a vinyl halide, option C an allylic halide, and option D an aryl halide. None feature the $sp$-hybridized carbon indicative of a triple bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is NOT Alliylic halide?
questions.solution:
An allylic halide requires the halogen to attach to an sp$^3$ carbon directly adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond.

In compound A, $\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{X}$, the halogen is bonded to a carbon that is sp$^3$ and adjacent to the double bond, so it is allylic.

In compound B, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{X}$, the halogen is attached to an sp$^3$ carbon adjacent to the double bond, so it is allylic.

In compound C, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{X}$, the halogen is connected to an sp$^3$ carbon directly adjacent to the double bond, so it is allylic.

In compound D, $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{X}$, the halogen is bonded to an sp$^3$ carbon, but it is separated from the double bond by a methylene group; since it is not directly adjacent, this structure is homoallylic rather than allylic.

The compound that is not an allylic halide is $\boxed{D}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has highest reactivity for SN reactions?
questions.solution:
Reactivity in SN reactions depends on the mechanism pathway: SN1 favors tertiary alkyl halides due to carbocation stability, while SN2 favors primary alkyl halides due to minimal steric hindrance.

n-Butyl iodide (primary) and isobutyl iodide (primary with beta-branching) undergo SN2 readily but are unreactive in SN1 due to unstable primary carbocations. sec-Butyl iodide (secondary) reacts through both mechanisms but with moderate rates.

Tertiary alkyl halides like tert-butyl iodide undergo rapid SN1 reactions, as the tertiary carbocation intermediate is highly stabilized. Steric hindrance prevents SN2 reactivity, but the SN1 pathway dominates under favorable conditions, making tertiary halides the most reactive overall.

The ranking is: tert-butyl iodide > sec-butyl iodide > n-butyl iodide > isobutyl iodide.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of bromobenzene with bromomethane and sodium metal in dry ether to give toluene is
questions.solution:
The reaction involves an aryl halide and an alkyl halide reacting with sodium metal in dry ether to produce an alkylbenzene, which characterizes the Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

The general form is $Ar-X + R-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} Ar-R + 2NaX$.

For bromobenzene and bromomethane, the reaction is $C_6H_5Br + CH_3Br + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} C_6H_5CH_3 + 2NaBr$.

This distinguishes it from the Wurtz reaction (two alkyl halides), the Fittig reaction (two aryl halides), and the Friedel-Crafts reaction (uses Lewis acid catalyst, not sodium metal).

The correct identification is $\boxed{D}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT obtained when a mixture of chloroethane and 1-chloropropane is treated with sodium metal in dry ether?
questions.solution:
The Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides with sodium metal in dry ether to form alkanes. With chloroethane and 1-chloropropane, three products form via self-coupling and cross-coupling.

Let $R_1 = CH_3CH_2$– (ethyl) and $R_2 = CH_3CH_2CH_2$– (propyl). Self-coupling of chloroethane yields butane ($C_4H_{10}$):
$R_1R_1 = CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3$.

Self-coupling of 1-chloropropane yields hexane ($C_6H_{14}$):
$R_2R_2 = CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_3$.

Cross-coupling yields pentane ($C_5H_{12}$):
$R_1R_2 = CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_3$.

Propane ($C_3H_8$) is not formed, as it lacks a coupling pathway. The correct option is A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of reaction that of aryl halide with alkyl halide and sodium metal in dry ether to give substituted aromatic compounds.
questions.solution:
The reaction involves coupling an aryl halide with an alkyl halide using sodium in dry ether to yield an alkyl-aryl product.

The Wurtz-Fittig reaction is defined by $Ar-X + R-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{dry ether} Ar-R + 2NaX$, matching the given transformation.

Other reactions do not fit: the Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides ($R-R'$), the Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides ($Ar-Ar'$), and the Friedel-Crafts reaction uses Lewis acid catalysis rather than sodium metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of arenes are obtained when arene diazonium chloride is treated with fluoroboric acid and then heated further?
questions.solution:
The reaction is the Balz-Schiemann reaction, which synthesizes fluoroarenes from arene diazonium salts.

Arenediazonium fluoroborate forms when arenediazonium chloride $\mathrm{ArN_2^+Cl^-}$ reacts with fluoroboric acid $\mathrm{HBF_4}$:

$\mathrm{ArN_2^+Cl^- + HBF_4 \to ArN_2^+BF_4^- + HCl}$

Thermal decomposition of arenediazonium fluoroborate produces fluoroarene $\mathrm{ArF}$, nitrogen gas, and boron trifluoride:

$\mathrm{ArN_2^+BF_4^- \xrightarrow{heat} ArF + N_2 \uparrow + BF_3}$

The product is a fluoroarene $\mathrm{ArF}$, corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is vinylic halide?
questions.solution: No Solution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following reaction is a Fittig reaction?
questions.solution:
Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides with sodium in dry ether to form diaryls. Analyzing each reaction:

A) $2\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_6 + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ yields an alkane via the Wurtz reaction.

B) $2\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} (\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)_2 + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ produces a diaryl, matching the Fittig reaction.

C) $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\cdot\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5 + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ yields an alkylarene, characteristic of the Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

D) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl} + \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{Cl} + 2\mathrm{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5 + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$ yields an alkane via the Wurtz reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of reaction for aryl halide with alkyl halide and sodium metal in dry ether to give substituted aromatic compounds.
questions.solution:
Wurtz-Fittig reaction occurs when an aryl halide and an alkyl halide react with sodium metal in dry ether, forming an alkyl-substituted aromatic compound: $Ar-X + R-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{Dry\ Ether} Ar-R + 2NaX$.

Other reactions include:

Wurtz reaction: Two alkyl halides yielding a higher alkane: $R-X + R'-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{Dry\ Ether} R-R' + 2NaX$.

Fittig reaction: Two aryl halides forming a biaryl compound: $Ar-X + Ar'-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{Dry\ Ether} Ar-Ar' + 2NaX$.

Finkelstein reaction: Halogen exchange with sodium iodide in acetone: $R-X + NaI \xrightarrow{Acetone} R-I + NaX$ ($X = Cl, Br$).

Since the described reaction involves one aryl and one alkyl halide, it corresponds to the Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of reactivity for reaction involving cleavage of C-X bond in following compounds is
questions.solution:
Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) reactivity in haloarenes depends critically on electron-withdrawing group stabilization of the Meisenheimer complex.

Compound I (1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene) has a single nitro group para to chlorine, providing moderate stabilization.

Compound II (1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene) features two nitro groups (ortho and para), offering enhanced stabilization through combined resonance and inductive effects.

Compound III (1-chloro-2,4,6-trinitrobenzene) possesses three nitro groups (two ortho, one para), yielding maximum stabilization of the anionic intermediate.

The order of reactivity follows the degree of Meisenheimer complex stabilization: $\mathrm{III} \gt \mathrm{II} \gt \mathrm{I}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pair of compounds on heating gives butanenitrile?
questions.solution:
Butanenitrile ($\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 CH_2 CN}$) contains four carbon atoms. Its synthesis from an alkyl halide with three carbons via nucleophilic substitution with cyanide is effective, since the cyanide group contributes one additional carbon. Propanol, butanol, and n-butylchloride are unsuitable: alcohols require prior conversion to alkyl halides, and n-butylchloride would yield a five-carbon nitrile. In contrast, n-propylchloride ($\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 CH_2 Cl}$) reacts with alcoholic KCN under heat to form butanenitrile:

$\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 CH_2 Cl + KCN \rightarrow[alc., heat] CH_3 CH_2 CH_2 CN + KCl}$

Final answer: $\boxed{D}$

questions.q:
Identify the product ' $Z$ ' in the following series of reactions.
Ethanol $\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{SOCl}_2} \mathrm{X} \xrightarrow[\text { Dry ether }]{\mathrm{Mg}} \mathrm{Y} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NH}_3} \mathrm{Z}$
questions.solution: The reaction sequence begins with ethanol treated with thionyl chloride under heat, producing ethyl chloride: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2 OH + SOCl_2 \rightarrow[\Delta] CH_3CH_2Cl + SO_2 + HCl}$, hence X is ethyl chloride ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}$). In dry ether, ethyl chloride reacts with magnesium to form the Grignard reagent ethyl magnesium chloride: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl + Mg \rightarrow[\text{Dry ether}] CH_3CH_2MgCl}$, so Y is $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2MgCl}$. Ethyl magnesium chloride, being a strong base, reacts with ammonia via proton abstraction to yield ethane: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2MgCl + NH_3 \rightarrow CH_3CH_3 + MgClNH_2}$, thus Z is ethane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_3}$). Among the options, ethane corresponds to D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent involved in Sandmeyer reaction.
questions.solution:
The Sandmeyer reaction synthesizes aryl halides or nitriles from aryl diazonium salts by replacing the $\mathrm{-N}_2^+$ group with a halogen or cyano group using copper(I) salts.

CuCN / KCN is a characteristic Sandmeyer reagent, converting aryl diazonium salts to aryl nitriles: $\mathrm{Ar-N}_2^+ \mathrm{X}^- + \mathrm{CuCN} / \mathrm{KCN} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ar-CN} + \mathrm{N}_2 + \mathrm{CuX}$.

In contrast, Cu (powder) / HBr pertains to the Gattermann reaction, H_3$PO_3$ reduces diazonium salts to arenes, and CH_3$CH_2$OH similarly acts as a reducing agent; none are Sandmeyer reagents.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the product ' $X$ ' formed in the following reaction,
Sodium ethoxide + Isopropyl chloride $\longrightarrow X+$ Ethanol + Sodium Chloride
questions.solution:
Sodium ethoxide ($CH_3CH_2ONa$) is a strong base and nucleophile, while isopropyl chloride ($CH_3CHClCH_3$) is a secondary alkyl halide. This combination can lead to either substitution ($S_N2$) or elimination ($E2$) reactions.

In an $E2$ elimination, the ethoxide ion acts as a base, abstracting a $\beta$-hydrogen from the alkyl halide. The products are propene ($CH_2=CHCH_3$), ethanol ($CH_3CH_2OH$), and sodium chloride ($NaCl$). The formation of ethanol is characteristic of $E2$ elimination when ethoxide is the base.

A substitution pathway ($S_N2$) would yield 2-ethoxypropane without forming ethanol, which contradicts the given products. Among the options, only propene aligns with the $E2$ mechanism and observed byproducts.

The product $X$ is propene: $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is NOT benzylic halide ?
questions.solution:
Benzylic halides are defined as compounds where a halogen atom is bonded to an $\mathrm{sp^3}$-hybridized carbon that is directly attached to an aromatic ring.

Evaluating each option:

$\mathbf{A)}$ Bromophenylmethane: $\mathrm{C_6H_5\text{–}CH_2\text{–}Br}$
The bromine is bonded to a methylene carbon directly attached to the phenyl ring, qualifying as a primary benzylic halide.

$\mathbf{B)}$ 1-Bromo-1-phenylpropane: $\mathrm{C_6H_5\text{–}CHBr\text{–}CH_2CH_3}$
The bromine-bearing carbon is directly phenyl-substituted, making it a secondary benzylic halide.

$\mathbf{C)}$ 2-Bromo-2-phenylpropane: $\mathrm{C_6H_5\text{–}CBr(CH_3)\text{–}CH_3}$
The tertiary carbon with bromine is directly bonded to the phenyl ring, a tertiary benzylic halide.

$\mathbf{D)}$ 1-Bromo-2-phenylbutane: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2\text{–}CH(C_6H_5)\text{–}CH_2Br}$
The bromine is attached to a carbon ($\mathrm{CH_2}$) that is one carbon removed from the ring-attached carbon; it is not directly benzylic but rather an alkyl halide.

Only option D lacks a direct attachment between the halogen-bearing carbon and the aromatic ring. Therefore, it is not a benzylic halide.

Final answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is an allylic halide?
questions.solution:
An allylic halide contains a halogen attached to an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond.

Examining the options:

A) 1-Bromopropene ($CH_3-CH=CH-Br$): bromine is attached to an $sp^2$ carbon, making this vinylic.

B) 2-Bromopropene ($CH_2=C(Br)CH_3$): bromine is attached to an $sp^2$ carbon, also vinylic.

C) 3-Bromopropene ($CH_2=CH-CH_2Br$): bromine is attached to an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to the double bond, satisfying the allylic condition.

D) 4-Bromobut-1-ene ($BrCH_2CH_2CH=CH_2$): bromine is attached to an $sp^3$ carbon, but it is not adjacent to the double bond, so it is homoallylic.

The allylic halide is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When tert butyl bromide is heated with silver fluoride the major product obtained is
questions.solution:
Halogen exchange via the Swarts reaction converts tert-butyl bromide to the corresponding fluoride through an $S_N1$ mechanism, favored by the stability of the tertiary carbocation intermediate.

Ionization yields the tertiary carbocation: $(CH_3)_3CBr \rightarrow (CH_3)_3C^+ + Br^-$.

Nucleophilic attack by fluoride ($F^-$ from AgF) gives the product: $(CH_3)_3C^+ + F^- \rightarrow (CH_3)_3CF$.

The systematic name for $(CH_3)_3CF$ is 2-fluoro-2-methylpropane.

Among the options, only 2-fluoro-2-methylpropane corresponds to the tertiary structure formed from tert-butyl bromide.

The product is $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the compound formed by action of chromyl chloride on toluene in presence of $\mathrm{CS}_2$ and hydrolysed further?
questions.solution:
Étard Reaction: Toluene undergoes selective oxidation of its methyl group through the Étard reaction. The process involves treatment with chromyl chloride in carbon disulfide to form an intermediate chromium complex.

$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_3 + 2CrO_2 Cl_2 \rightarrow [CS_2] C_6H_5CH(OCrOHCl_2)_2}$

Subsequent acidic hydrolysis of the complex yields benzaldehyde:

$\mathrm{C_6H_5CH(OCrOHCl_2)_2 \rightarrow[H_3O^+] C_6 H_5 CHO}$

Among the options, only benzaldehyde corresponds to this reaction pathway. Chlorobenzene forms via electrophilic substitution, benzal chloride requires radical halogenation with excess chlorine, and benzoic acid necessitates stronger oxidation conditions.

The product is benzaldehyde, corresponding to option C.

questions.q: Identify the product formed from chlorobenzene on heating with conc. $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ in presence of conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$.
questions.solution:
Nitration of chlorobenzene with concentrated $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4$ proceeds via electrophilic aromatic substitution, where the nitronium ion $\mathrm{NO}_2^+$ acts as the electrophile.

The chlorine substituent exhibits both an electron-withdrawing inductive effect and an electron-donating resonance effect, making it overall deactivating but ortho–para directing. Consequently, substitution occurs at the ortho and para positions, yielding a mixture of 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene and 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene.

Option A is incorrect as it ignores the ortho product, option B is incorrect as it ignores the para product, and option D is incorrect since trinitration requires harsher conditions.

questions.q:
Identify the product ' B ' in the following reaction sequence.
$\text { Alkyl halide } \frac{\mathrm{Mg}}{\text { Dry ether }} \mathrm{A} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NH}_3} \mathrm{~B}$
questions.solution:
Reaction sequence analysis:

Alkyl halide $\mathrm{R-X}$ reacts with magnesium in dry ether to form Grignard reagent $\mathrm{A = R-Mg-X}$.

Grignard reagents are strong bases that react with compounds containing acidic protons. Ammonia $\mathrm{NH_3}$ has acidic hydrogens, producing the corresponding hydrocarbon via proton transfer: $\mathrm{R-Mg-X + H-NH_2 \rightarrow R-H + Mg(X)NH_2}$.

The product $\mathrm{B}$ is therefore a hydrocarbon $\mathrm{R-H}$.

Among the options, the correct answer corresponds to hydrocarbon: $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkenes is most easily formed by dehydrohalogenation of alkyl halides?
questions.solution:
Dehydrohalogenation follows Zaitsev's rule, favoring formation of the most substituted and stable alkene.

Alkene stability increases with substitution: $\mathrm{R}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CR}_2$ (tetrasubstituted) > $\mathrm{R}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CHR}$ (trisubstituted) > $\mathrm{RCH}=\mathrm{CHR}$ (disubstituted) ≈ $\mathrm{R}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}_2$ (disubstituted).

The tetrasubstituted alkene $\mathrm{R}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CR}_2$ possesses maximum hyperconjugative stabilization and will form most readily.

As the size of halogen increases from $F$ to I , $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{X}$ bond length increases and $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{X}$ bond strength decreases. With decrease in bond strength, it becomes easier to break the bond by applying minimum energy.

Increasing molecular weight enhances van der Waals interactions, raising boiling points.

Molecular weights correspond to carbon counts:

$\text{Pentanal (C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O)} \gt \text{Propanal (C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O)} \gt \text{Ethanal (C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O)} \gt \text{Methanal (CH}_2\text{O)}$

Methanal, with the smallest molecular mass and weakest intermolecular forces, exhibits the lowest boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is haloalkyne?
questions.solution:
A haloalkyne is a compound that contains both a halogen $(X)$ and a triple bond (alkyne group, $\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{C}$ ). Let's analyze the given options:
- (A) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-X$ : This is a haloalkene, not a haloalkyne. The structure has a double bond $(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH})$, not a triple bond $(\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{C})$. Therefore, this is not a haloalkyne.
- (B) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{X}$ : This is a haloalkyne. It contains a triple bond ( $\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{C}$ ) between carbon atoms and a halogen $(\mathrm{X})$ attached to a carbon. This matches the definition of a haloalkyne.
- (C) $\mathrm{CH} \equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{X}$ : This is a haloalkyne as it contains a triple bond $(\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{C})$ and a halogen $(\mathrm{X})$ attached to a carbon.
- (D) $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{X}$ : This is also a haloalkyne, containing a triple bond $(\mathrm{C} \equiv \mathrm{C})$ and a halogen $(X)$ attached to a carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the false statement from following about $\mathrm{SN}^1$ reaction mechanism.
options: Intermediate formed during the reaction is a carbocation.
Concentration of nucleophile does not affect the rate of reaction.
Racemization takes place if reaction is carried out at chiral carbon in optically active substance.
questions.solution:
The false statement about SN1 (Substitution Nucleophilic Unimolecular) reaction mechanism is: (D) It is a single-step mechanism.
The SN1 reaction mechanism is a two-step process. In the first step, the leaving group departs, generating a carbocation intermediate. In the second step, the nucleophile attacks the carbocation, leading to the formation of the substitution product.
The correct statement regarding SN1 reaction mechanism is:
(A) Racemization takes place if the reaction is carried out at a chiral carbon in an optically active substance. This is true because the carbocation intermediate formed during the reaction is planar and can be attacked by nucleophiles from either side, resulting in the formation of both enantiomers, leading to racemization.
(B) Intermediate formed during the reaction is a carbocation. This is true as the leaving group departure creates a carbocation intermediate that is stabilized by the surrounding electrondonating groups or the solvent.
(C) Concentration of nucleophile does not affect the rate of the reaction. This is generally true for $\mathrm{SN} 1$ reactions because the rate-determining step is the formation of the carbocation intermediate, which does not involve the nucleophile. The rate is primarily dependent on the stability of the carbocation and the leaving group ability.

questions.solution:
(1) When $\mathrm{C}$ is chiral, then product of $\mathrm{SN}^1$ reaction is racemic mixture, \& the reaction is known as racemization.
In planner carbocation nucleophile attack from both front and back side. In $\mathrm{SN}^1$ reaction both inversion \& retention of configuration takes place. (2) Two step mechanism Thus, option A is incorrect (3) Heterolysis of C $-\mathrm{X}$ bond forms carbocation intermediate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reaction steps is known as propagation step
questions.solution:
In a free radical substitution reaction, the mechanism involves three types of steps:

1. Initiation step: A neutral molecule breaks down to form free radicals.
$\text{Cl-Cl} \rightarrow \text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{Cl}^\bullet$

2. Propagation step: A free radical reacts with a neutral molecule to generate a new free radical and a new neutral molecule. This step keeps the chain reaction going.
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$

3. Termination step: Two free radicals combine to form a neutral molecule, stopping the chain reaction.
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl}$
$\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{CH}_3^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_3$

Therefore, the reaction $\text{CH}_3^\bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-Cl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$ represents the propagation step.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the major product of following reaction.
$\text{Propene} \xrightarrow[\large{\text{Peroxide}}]{\large{\text{HBr}}} \,?$
questions.solution:
The reaction of propene with $HBr$ in the presence of peroxide proceeds via a free radical mechanism, known as the peroxide effect or anti-Markovnikov addition.

The peroxide undergoes homolytic cleavage to form alkoxy radicals, which then abstract a hydrogen atom from $HBr$ to generate a bromine radical ($Br^{\bullet}$).

The bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon atom of the double bond in propene to generate a more stable secondary free radical:

$CH_3-CH=CH_2 + Br^{\bullet} \rightarrow CH_3-\dot{C}H-CH_2Br$

The secondary free radical then abstracts a hydrogen atom from another molecule of $HBr$ to form the final product:

$CH_3-\dot{C}H-CH_2Br + HBr \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Br + Br^{\bullet}$

The major product formed is 1-bromopropane.

Answer: 1 - Bromopropane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following hydrocarbons has stronger London dispersion forces ?
questions.solution:
London dispersion forces increase with an increase in molecular mass and the surface area of the molecule.

Methane ($CH_4$) and ethane ($C_2H_6$) have lower molecular masses compared to n-pentane and neo-pentane ($C_5H_{12}$), resulting in weaker dispersion forces.

Between n-pentane and neo-pentane, n-pentane is a straight-chain alkane, whereas neo-pentane is highly branched and nearly spherical.

The straight-chain structure of n-pentane provides a larger surface area for intermolecular contact compared to the compact structure of neo-pentane.

Therefore, n-pentane has the strongest London dispersion forces among the given hydrocarbons.

Answer: n-pentane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product of the following reaction is
questions.solution:
The given reactant is 3-methylhex-3-ene.

The addition of HI to an alkene is an electrophilic addition reaction that proceeds via the formation of a carbocation intermediate.

First, the electrophile $H^+$ attacks the double bond. This can result in two possible carbocations:
1. Protonation at C-4 yields a tertiary carbocation at C-3.
2. Protonation at C-3 yields a secondary carbocation at C-4.

Since a tertiary carbocation is significantly more stable than a secondary carbocation due to greater hyperconjugation and inductive effects, the reaction proceeds predominantly through the tertiary carbocation at C-3.

Finally, the nucleophile $I^-$ attacks this more stable tertiary carbocation, resulting in the iodine atom attaching to C-3.

The major product formed is 3-iodo-3-methylhexane.

Answer: 3 - iodo - 3 - methylhexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT terminal alkyne ?
questions.solution:
Terminal alkynes have a triple bond at the end of the carbon chain, meaning at least one hydrogen atom is directly attached to a triply bonded carbon atom ($R-C \equiv C-H$).

Ethyne is $H-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

Propyne is $CH_3-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

But-1-yne is $CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv C-H$, which is a terminal alkyne.

But-2-yne is $CH_3-C \equiv C-CH_3$, where the triple bond is between the second and third carbon atoms. It does not have a hydrogen atom attached to the triply bonded carbon atoms. Thus, it is an internal alkyne, not a terminal alkyne.

Answer: But - 2 - yne

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl chlorides on Wurtz reaction gives 2, 2, 5, 5- tetramethylhexane ?
questions.solution:
Wurtz reaction involves the coupling of two alkyl halide molecules in the presence of sodium and dry ether to form a symmetrical alkane.

$2\text{R-Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{R-R} + 2\text{NaCl}$

The given product is 2,2,5,5-tetramethylhexane. Its structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_3$.

Cleaving the molecule symmetrically at the central $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond gives two identical alkyl groups, which are neopentyl groups, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-$.

Therefore, the required alkyl chloride is neopentyl chloride, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$
