questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following nanomaterials has one dimension $\lt  100$ nm?
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified based on the number of dimensions that lie in the nanoscale range ($1$ to $100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include quantum dots and nanoparticles.

One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include nanowires and nanotubes.

Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials have exactly one dimension in the nanoscale. Examples include thin films, graphene, and nanosheets.

Three-dimensional (3D) nanomaterials have no dimensions in the nanoscale but possess nanoscale features.

Since thin films have only one dimension (thickness) less than $100$ nm, they are classified as 2D nanomaterials.

Answer: Thin films

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the term used to describe movement of colloidal particles under applied electric potential without using semipermeable membrane.
questions.solution:
The movement of colloidal particles under the influence of an applied electric potential is called electrophoresis.

When the movement of colloidal particles is prevented by some suitable means (like a semipermeable membrane), it is observed that the dispersion medium begins to move in an electric field. This phenomenon is termed electroosmosis.

Since the question specifies the movement of colloidal particles without using a semipermeable membrane, the correct term is electrophoresis.

Answer: Electrophoresis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following forces is responsible for physisorption ?
questions.solution:
Physisorption, also known as physical adsorption, arises due to weak van der Waals forces between the adsorbate and the adsorbent.

London force of dispersion is a type of van der Waals force and is the primary force responsible for physisorption.

Coulombic and electrostatic forces are strong forces typically associated with ionic interactions or chemisorption, while hydrogen bonding is a specific dipole-dipole interaction not universally responsible for physisorption.

Answer: London force of dispersion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following properties of colloid is used to measure the rate of migration of sol particles?
questions.solution:
Electrophoresis is the phenomenon of movement of colloidal particles under the influence of an applied electric field. By observing this movement, the rate of migration of sol particles can be measured.

Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles.

Brownian motion is the continuous zig-zag motion of colloidal particles.

Electroosmosis is the movement of the dispersion medium under an electric field when the colloidal particles are prevented from moving.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of macromolecular colloid?
questions.solution:
Macromolecular colloids are formed when large molecules (macromolecules) having colloidal dimensions are dispersed in a suitable dispersion medium. Examples include naturally occurring macromolecules such as starch, cellulose, proteins, and enzymes, as well as man-made polymers like polythene, nylon, and polystyrene.

Soaps and detergents are examples of associated colloids (micelles), which are formed by the aggregation of a large number of ions in concentrated solutions.

Sulphur sol, consisting of particles containing a thousand or more $\text{S}_8$ sulphur molecules, is an example of a multimolecular colloid.

Therefore, proteins are an example of a macromolecular colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following anions has greater power for coagulation of positive sol?
questions.solution:
According to the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion is directly proportional to the magnitude of its charge (valency). For the coagulation of a positive sol, an anion is required.

The given anions and their charge magnitudes are:
$\text{Cl}^-$ : $1$
$\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ : $2$
$\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ (given as $\text{PO}_4^{2-}$ in options) : $3$
$[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ : $4$

Since $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ has the highest negative charge, it possesses the maximum coagulating power among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is NOT an example of oil in water emulsion?
questions.solution:
Emulsions are broadly classified into two types based on the dispersed phase and dispersion medium:

1. Oil in water (O/W) emulsion: In this type, oil acts as the dispersed phase and water acts as the dispersion medium. Examples include milk, vanishing cream, and paint.

2. Water in oil (W/O) emulsion: In this type, water acts as the dispersed phase and oil acts as the dispersion medium. Examples include butter, cold cream, and cod liver oil.

Since butter is a water in oil (W/O) emulsion, it is not an example of an oil in water emulsion.

Answer: Butter

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale range (less than $100$ nm). Examples include quantum dots, nanoparticles, and fullerenes.

One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale and one macroscopic dimension. Examples include nanotubes, nanowires, and nanofibers.

Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials have one dimension in the nanoscale and two macroscopic dimensions. Examples include thin films, graphene, and coatings.

Therefore, quantum dots are the nanomaterials having all three dimensions less than $100$ nm.

Answer: Quantum dots

The scattering of light by colloidal particles is known as the Tyndall effect.

Therefore, the Tyndall effect is responsible for the development of colour in colloids.

Answer: Tyndall effect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following exhibits the minimum coagulating power for precipitating of positively charged ferric oxide sol ?
questions.solution:
According to the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion is directly proportional to the magnitude of its charge.

Since the ferric oxide sol is positively charged, the anions of the added electrolyte are responsible for its coagulation.

The anions provided by the given electrolytes are:
$\text{KNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{NO}_3^{-}$ (charge magnitude = $1$)
$\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{SO}_4^{2-}$ (charge magnitude = $2$)
$\text{K}_3\text{PO}_4 \rightarrow \text{PO}_4^{3-}$ (charge magnitude = $3$)
$\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6] \rightarrow [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ (charge magnitude = $4$)

The order of coagulating power is $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-} \gt \text{PO}_4^{3-} \gt \text{SO}_4^{2-} \gt \text{NO}_3^{-}$.

Thus, $\text{KNO}_3$ exhibits the minimum coagulating power.

Answer: $\text{KNO}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the role of catalyst in catalytic reaction ?
options: It decreases the enthalpy of reaction.
It increases the enthalpy of reaction.
It decreases the energy of activation of reaction.
It increases the energy of activation of reaction.
questions.solution:
A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway that has a lower activation energy.

It does not alter the enthalpy, entropy, or Gibbs free energy of the reaction.

Thus, the primary role of a catalyst is to decrease the energy of activation of the reaction.

Answer: It decreases the energy of activation of reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is applicable to thin film?
questions.solution:
Nanostructures are classified based on the number of dimensions that are not confined to the nanoscale range ($\lt 100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional (0D) nanostructures have all three dimensions in the nanoscale (e.g., quantum dots, nanoparticles).

One-dimensional (1D) nanostructures have two dimensions in the nanoscale and one extended dimension (e.g., nanowires, nanotubes).

Two-dimensional (2D) nanostructures have one dimension in the nanoscale (thickness) and two extended dimensions (length and width). A thin film falls under this category as its thickness is in the nanometer range while its other two dimensions are macroscopic.

Three-dimensional (3D) nanostructures have all three dimensions outside the nanoscale (e.g., bulk materials).

Therefore, a thin film is a two-dimensional nanostructure.

Answer: Two dimensional nanostructure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II
List IList II
(A). Brownian Motion(I). Removal of impurities from the colloidal sols using a semipermeable membrane.
(B). Tyndall Effect(II). Movement of colloidal particles under the influence of an electric field.
(C). Electrophoresis(III). Random movement of colloidal particles due to kinetic energy.
(D). Dialysis(IV). Scattering of light by colloidal particles
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Brownian motion is the continuous random zig-zag movement of colloidal particles due to unequal bombardment by the molecules of the dispersion medium. Thus, (A) \rightarrow (III).

Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles, making the path of light visible. Thus, (B) \rightarrow (IV).

Electrophoresis is the movement of colloidal particles towards oppositely charged electrodes under the influence of an applied electric field. Thus, (C) \rightarrow (II).

Dialysis is the process of removing dissolved impurities from a colloidal sol using a semipermeable membrane. Thus, (D) \rightarrow (I).

The correct matching is (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (IV), (C) - (II), (D) - (I)

questions.q: Identify the correct statement regarding lyophilic colloid from the following.
options: It is formed only by special methods.

The word lyophilic means liquid-loving or solvent-loving. Therefore, lyophilic colloids are solvent-loving colloids.

They are reversible in nature because if the dispersion medium is separated from the dispersed phase, the sol can be reconstituted by simply remixing with the dispersion medium.

They can be prepared easily by directly mixing the dispersed phase with the dispersion medium, without requiring any special methods.

Answer: It is solvent loving colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct for the spontaneous adsorption of a gas?
options: $\Delta S$ is negative and, therefore $\Delta H$ should be highly positive
$\Delta S$ is negative and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.
$\Delta S$ is positive and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be negative.
$\Delta S$ is positive and therefore, $\Delta H$ should also be highly positive.
questions.solution:
During the adsorption of a gas, the gas molecules are restricted to the surface of the solid, which decreases their randomness or entropy. Thus, the change in entropy, $\Delta S$, is negative.

For a process to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy, $\Delta G$, must be negative.

According to the Gibbs-Helmholtz equation:
$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

Since $\Delta S$ is negative, the term $-T\Delta S$ becomes positive. For $\Delta G$ to be negative, the enthalpy change, $\Delta H$, must be negative and its magnitude must be large enough to overcome the positive $-T\Delta S$ term.

Therefore, $\Delta S$ is negative and $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.

Answer: $\Delta S$ is negative and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.

questions.q: Identify the gas adsorbed by solid to the largest extent at their respective critical temperature.
questions.solution:
The extent of adsorption of a gas on a solid surface depends on the strength of intermolecular forces. Gases with higher critical temperatures have stronger van der Waals forces of attraction and are more easily liquefiable, leading to a greater extent of adsorption.

The critical temperatures of the given gases are approximately:
$\text{H}_{2} \approx 33 \text{ K}$
$\text{N}_{2} \approx 126 \text{ K}$
$\text{O}_{2} \approx 154 \text{ K}$
$\text{SO}_{2} \approx 430 \text{ K}$

Since $\text{SO}_{2}$ has the highest critical temperature among the given options, it has the strongest intermolecular forces and is adsorbed to the largest extent.

Answer: $\text{SO}_{2(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following assertions about the extent of physisorption is correct?
options: Decreases with increase in surface area
Decreases with increase in the strength of Van der Waals forces
questions.solution:
Physisorption is an exothermic process. According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in temperature shifts the equilibrium in the backward direction, leading to desorption. Thus, the extent of physisorption decreases with an increase in temperature.

Additionally, the extent of physisorption increases with an increase in the surface area of the adsorbent and with an increase in the strength of Van der Waals forces between the adsorbate and adsorbent.

Answer: Decreases with increase in temperature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characterstic of chemisorption?
options: Heat released is in the range of $40-200 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$.
Formation of multimolecular layer of adsorbate.
questions.solution:
Identify which option is not a characteristic of chemisorption:

Chemisorption involves the formation of chemical bonds between adsorbate and adsorbent, making it highly specific—option (A) is characteristic.

The heat released is typically in the range $40-200 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$, aligning with chemical bond energies—option (B) is characteristic.

Chemisorption is unimolecular; strong covalent bonds occupy surface sites, preventing multilayer formation, which is a trait of physisorption—option (C) is not characteristic.

The process is irreversible due to high activation energy for desorption—option (D) is characteristic.

The answer is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify catalyst used in following reaction.
$\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})} \xrightarrow{623 \mathrm{~K}} \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}+\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}$
questions.solution:
Water-Gas Shift Reaction: $\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})} \xrightarrow{623 \mathrm{~K}} \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}+\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}$

The reaction at 623 K represents the high-temperature water-gas shift process, which employs iron oxide-chromium oxide catalysts (iron chromate) to enhance hydrogen production and reduce carbon monoxide.

Among the options, vanadium pentoxide catalyzes sulfuric acid production, nickel metal facilitates hydrogenation and reforming, and acid/alkali traces serve other catalytic purposes. Iron chromate remains the standard catalyst for this specific industrial process.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the negatively charged sol from following.
questions.solution:
The charge on colloidal particles arises from preferential ion adsorption, electron capture during electro-dispersion, or dissociation of surface molecules.

Colloidal sols exhibit either positive or negative net charges:

Negatively charged sols: Metal sulfides ($As_2S_3$, $CdS$), acidic dyes (Eosin, Congo red), starch, gum, clay, charcoal, and metals ($Au$, $Ag$, $Pt$).

Positively charged sols: Metal hydroxides ($Fe(OH)_3$, $Al(OH)_3$), basic dyes (Methylene blue), and haemoglobin under specific pH conditions.

Analyzing the options: Eosin is an acidic dye with deprotonated groups, yielding negative charges. Titanium oxide ($TiO_2$) typically adsorbs positive ions. Methylene blue, a basic dye, protonates to form positive charges. Haemoglobin, being amphoteric, varies with pH but is often positive in acidic conditions.

Eosin definitively forms a negatively charged sol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following nanomaterial has all three dimensions less than 100 nm ?
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified by the number of dimensions confined to the nanoscale (less than 100 nm). Zero-dimensional (0D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions confined to the nanoscale; examples include nanoparticles, quantum dots, and nanoshells. One-dimensional (1D) nanomaterials have two nanoscale dimensions with a larger third dimension—nanotubes, nanowires, and nanofibers exhibit this structure. Two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials feature one nanoscale dimension and two larger dimensions, as seen in thin films, coatings, and graphene. Three-dimensional (3D) nanomaterials have all dimensions larger than 100 nm but contain internal nanoscale features, such as bulk nanostructured materials and composites.

Nanoshells, with a dielectric core and metallic shell, are spherical and have all dimensions (diameter) typically under 100 nm, classifying them as 0D nanomaterials. Nanotubes and nanofibers, with nanoscale diameters but macroscopic lengths, are 1D. Thin films, with nanoscale thickness but large length and width, are 2D. Thus, only nanoshells have all three dimensions less than 100 nm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which instrument is used for determination of particle size?
questions.solution:
Particle size determination requires direct imaging capabilities provided by electron microscopy techniques. SEM offers surface visualization for measuring particle dimensions through high-resolution topography, while TEM achieves higher resolution for nanoscale internal structure analysis and particle measurement.

Spectroscopic methods prove unsuitable for direct size determination: FTIR identifies functional groups and chemical composition, and UV-visible spectroscopy quantifies concentrations and electronic transitions, though it may provide indirect size information through plasmon resonance effects in specific cases.

The instruments directly capable of particle size determination are $\boxed{\text{A, B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following gases is least adsorbed on solid at similar conditions of temperature and pressure?
questions.solution:
The extent of physisorption depends directly on a gas's ease of liquefaction, which is governed by intermolecular forces and critical temperature. Stronger intermolecular forces and higher critical temperatures correspond to greater adsorption.

Examining the gases: $\mathrm{SO}_2$ ($T_c = 157.5^\circ\mathrm{C}$) exhibits significant dipole-dipole interactions; $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ ($T_c = 144^\circ\mathrm{C}$) experiences strong London dispersion forces; $\mathrm{NH}_3$ ($T_c = 132.4^\circ\mathrm{C}$) forms hydrogen bonds; $\mathrm{H}_2$ ($T_c = -239.9^\circ\mathrm{C}$) has minimal intermolecular forces due to its small size and nonpolar nature.

Since $\mathrm{H}_2$ has the lowest critical temperature and weakest intermolecular interactions, it is the least easily liquefied and consequently the least adsorbed.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the technique used to know binding nature of nanomaterials?
questions.solution: The binding nature of nanomaterials refers to their chemical bonds and functional groups. Electron microscopy techniques like SEM and TEM reveal morphological and structural features but not chemical bonding. XRD determines crystal structure and phase composition. Only FTIR spectroscopy directly identifies functional groups through characteristic infrared absorption frequencies.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following substances is classified as macromolecular colloid?
questions.solution:
Colloid classification depends on the dispersed phase particle structure. Multimolecular colloids form from aggregates of small molecules (e.g., gold sol), while macromolecular colloids consist of individual large molecules like proteins or synthetic polymers. Associated colloids (micelles) form aggregates only at higher concentrations, as with soaps.

Analyzing the options: soap and detergent form micelles (associated colloids), $\text{S}_8$ sulfur aggregates into multimolecular colloids, and nylon exists as individual macromolecules of colloidal size.

Nylon is therefore a macromolecular colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the temperature from following graph so that highest amount of a gas is adsorbed
questions.solution:
Adsorption isotherms plot the extent of adsorption $(x/m)$ against pressure $(p)$ at constant temperatures. Since adsorption is exothermic, Le Chatelier's principle indicates that lower temperatures favor greater adsorption.

The graph contains four isotherms labeled 195 K, 210 K, 244 K, and 273 K. The topmost curve, corresponding to 195 K, shows the highest $(x/m)$ values across all pressures, confirming that maximum adsorption occurs at the lowest temperature.

$\boxed{195\text{ K}}$

questions.solution:
The classification depends on the states of the dispersed phase and dispersion medium. In fog, a liquid (water droplets) is dispersed in a gas (air), which forms a liquid aerosol.

Other examples include mist and clouds. Conversely, foam is a gas in a liquid, gel is a liquid in a solid, and emulsion is a liquid in a liquid.

$\therefore$ The correct option is $\mathbf{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is classified as multimolecular colloid?
questions.solution:
Multimolecular colloids result from the aggregation of numerous small molecules or atoms into colloidal-sized particles. Individual components possess diameters below 1 nm, while the aggregated particles fall within the 1–1000 nm colloidal range.

Evaluating the options: starch and cellulose are macromolecular colloids composed of large polymer molecules intrinsically at colloidal scale. Plastics similarly constitute macromolecular colloidal systems.

S_8$ sulfur molecules demonstrate distinct behavior. When dissolved in alcohol and introduced to water, sulfur undergoes aggregation. Though individual S_8$ molecules are sub-colloidal, their association produces particles meeting colloidal dimensional criteria. This aggregation mechanism classifies sulfur as a multimolecular colloid.

The correct identification is C.

questions.q: Which of the following ion exihibits maximum power of coagulation for positively charged sol?
questions.solution:
Coagulating power depends on the valency of the active ion, as per the Hardy-Schulze rule.

For positively charged sols, anions serve as the active ions. Comparing valencies:

A) $\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}$: valency 2
B) $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$: valency 1
C) $\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-}$: valency 3
D) $\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{4-}$: valency 4

Since coagulating power increases with valency, the highest valency (4) corresponds to maximum coagulation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following process does NOT results in coagulation?
options: by mixing two oppositely charged sols
questions.solution:
Coagulation is the aggregation of colloidal particles into larger masses that sediment, following destabilization of the sol. Electrophoresis induces coagulation via charge neutralization at electrodes, boiling disrupts stabilizing layers through thermal agitation, and mixing oppositely charged sols causes mutual neutralization. Adding excess solvent, however, generally stabilizes the sol by reducing particle collision frequencies and diluting coagulating electrolytes, rather than promoting aggregation.

Thus, adding excess solvent does not typically result in coagulation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following represents the Freundlich's empirical equation for adsorption of gas on solid (for $\mathrm{n} \gt 1$)
questions.solution:
The Freundlich adsorption isotherm provides an empirical relationship describing the amount of gas adsorbed per unit mass of solid adsorbent in terms of pressure at a fixed temperature, expressed as

$\frac{x}{m} = kP^{\frac{1}{n}}$

where $x$ is the mass of the adsorbate, $m$ the mass of the adsorbent, and $P$ the pressure. Constants $k$ and $n$ (with $n \gt 1$) characterize the adsorbent-adsorbate system.

Comparing with the options: Option A matches the Freundlich isotherm exactly. Option B erroneously inverts the ratio $\frac{x}{m}$ to $\frac{m}{x}$. Option C uses an exponent of $n$ instead of $\frac{1}{n}$, and option D combines both errors.

The correct representation is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify sequential reactions involved in Sol-Gel process .
questions.solution:
The sol-gel process involves two sequential reactions for producing solid materials from molecular precursors.

Hydrolysis replaces alkoxy groups with hydroxyl groups:
$\mathrm{M(OR)_n + xH_2 O \rightarrow M(OH)_x(OR)_{n-x} + xROH}$

Polycondensation follows, forming metal-oxygen-metal bridges through either olation/oxolation or esterification:
$\mathrm{M-OH + HO-M \rightarrow M-O-M + H_2 O}$
$\mathrm{M-OR + HO-M \rightarrow M-O-M + ROH}$

This sequence establishes the correct order as hydrolysis followed by polycondensation, corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the property of colloidal solutions so that colloidal particles move freely towards respective electrodes under an applied electrical potential.
questions.solution:
Electrophoresis describes the movement of charged colloidal particles toward oppositely charged electrodes under an applied electric potential.

Colloidal particles carry surface charges, causing migration in an electric field. Brownian motion involves random thermal movement without directional bias. Electroosmosis concerns fluid movement relative to fixed charged surfaces. Dialysis removes dissolved impurities through selective diffusion.

The described behavior aligns precisely with electrophoresis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following gases is adsorbed to greater extent if adsorbent remains same at similar conditions of temperature and pressure?
questions.solution:
The extent of adsorption in physisorption depends on the ease of gas liquefaction, which correlates directly with critical temperature $T_c$.

The critical temperatures are: $\mathrm{H}_2$ at 33 K, $\mathrm{N}_2$ at 126 K, $\mathrm{O}_2$ at 155 K, and $\mathrm{SO}_2$ at 430.65 K.

Increasing order of $T_c$ is $\mathrm{H}_2 \lt \mathrm{N}_2 \lt \mathrm{O}_2 \lt \mathrm{SO}_2$.

$\mathrm{SO}_2$ has the highest critical temperature and will thus be adsorbed most extensively.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is effectively used to remove E. coli bacteria from water?
questions.solution:
Silver nanoparticles exhibit potent antimicrobial properties through several mechanisms that effectively eliminate E. coli. Silver ions $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ disrupt bacterial cell membrane integrity, penetrate cells to interfere with metabolic pathways, inhibit enzyme activity, and damage DNA.

Carbon black nanoparticles primarily function as adsorbents without significant intrinsic antimicrobial effects. Titanium dioxide nanoparticles $\mathrm{TiO_2}$ require UV activation for photocatalytic generation of reactive oxygen species. Silicon nanoparticles lack effective antimicrobial properties for direct bacterial removal.

Silver nanoparticles provide direct, light-independent antimicrobial action, making them the optimal choice for E. coli removal from water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not negatively charged sol?
questions.solution:
Charge determination for colloidal systems

Colloidal charge arises from preferential ion adsorption from solution or intrinsic molecular properties.

The $\mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{S}_3$ sol adsorbs sulfide ions ($\mathrm{S}^{2-}$) resulting in negative charge.

Clay particles develop negative charge through isomorphic substitution ($\mathrm{Al}^{3+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$) and surface hydroxyl dissociation.

Congo Red, an anionic dye, forms negatively charged colloidal particles through adsorption of dye anions.

Haemoglobin exhibits amphoteric behavior with isoelectric point near pH 6.8-7.1. Below this pH, amino group protonation yields net positive charge, distinguishing it from consistently negative sols.

$\mathrm{As}_2\mathrm{S}_3$, clay, and Congo Red sols are negatively charged, while haemoglobin is not.

The answer is $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify example of sorption from following.
options: Charcol is added to methylene blue solution.
Hydrogen gas is passed over platinum.
Oxygen gas is passed over finely divided nickel.
questions.solution:
Sorption describes the uptake of one substance by another, encompassing both adsorption and absorption. Adsorption involves accumulation on a surface, while absorption involves uniform distribution throughout a bulk material.

In the given examples: charcoal with methylene blue shows adsorption of dye molecules on the surface; chalk dipped in ink shows absorption as ink penetrates the bulk; hydrogen over platinum and oxygen over finely divided nickel both demonstrate adsorption of gases onto metal surfaces.

All processes are types of sorption.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match column I (process) with column II (application)
$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline & \text{Column I} & & \text{Column II} \\ \hline \text{A)} & \text{Dialysis} & \text{a)} & \text{Cleansing action of soap} \\ \hline \text{B)} & \text{Peptization} & \text{b)} & \text{Coagulation} \\ \hline \text{C)} & \text{Emulsification} & \text{c)} & \text{Colloidal Solution Preparation} \\ \hline \text{D)} & \text{Electrophoresis} & \text{d)} & \text{Purification of colloidal solution} \\ \hline \end{array}$
questions.solution:
Matching the processes with their applications:

Dialysis purifies colloidal solutions using a semi-permeable membrane, matching with (d).

Peptization forms colloids from precipitates with an electrolyte, matching with (c).

Emulsification disperses immiscible liquids, fundamental to the cleansing action of soap, matching with (a).

Electrophoresis moves charged colloids to electrodes causing coagulation, matching with (b).

Thus, $A \to d$, $B \to c$, $C \to a$, $D \to b$, corresponding to option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of electrons present in antibonding orbitals of \(\mathrm{N}_2\) molecule according to molecular orbital theory?
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{N}_2\) molecule is \((\sigma 1 \mathrm{~s})^2\left(\sigma^* 1 \mathrm{~s}\right)^2(\sigma 2 \mathrm{~s})^2\left(\sigma^* 2 \mathrm{~s}\right)^2\left(\pi 2 \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{x}}\right)^2\left(\pi 2 \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{y}}\right)^2\left(\sigma 2 \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{z}}\right)^2\)
\(\therefore \quad\) No. of electrons in antibonding orbitals \(=4\)

questions.solution: When soap is added to an oily or greasy part of cloth, the hydrocarbon part of soap dissolves in oil, keeping the head away from the oil. Big molecules of oil and soap break by rubbing into small emulsified oil droplets in water, which are washed away by stream of water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a character of catalyst?
options: It changes the position of equilibrium.
It increases the rates of both forward and Backward reactions equally in reversible reaction.
It affects the energies of reactants and products of the reaction.
It increases the activation energy of reactants.
questions.solution: Reactions can be sped up by the addition of a catalyst, including reversible reactions involving a final equilibrium state. Recall that for a reversible reaction, the equilibrium state is one in which the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal. In the presence of a catalyst, both the forward and reverse reaction rates will speed up equally, thereby allowing the system to reach equilibrium faster. However, it is very important to keep in mind that the addition of a catalyst has no effect whatsoever on the final equilibrium position of the reaction. It simply gets it there faster.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The precipitation power of an electrolyte increase with
questions.solution: The precipitation power of an electrolyte increases with charge of an ion. It can be explained on the basis of Hardy – Schulze rule. Greater the valence of the flocculating ion added, the greater is its power to cause precipitation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Blue colour of water in sea is due to
options: refraction of blue light by impurities
questions.solution: The colour of a colloidal solution depends on the wavelength of the light scattered by the dispersed particles, which in turn depends on the size and the nature of particle. The colour of water in sea is blue due to the scattering of light by water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following processes exhibits the decrease in internal energy of a system?
options: Isothermal expansion of an ideal gas.
Isothrmal compression of an ideal gas.
Adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas.
Adiabatic compression of an ideal gas
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + w$.

For an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant ($\Delta T = 0$). Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, $\Delta U = 0$ for both isothermal expansion and compression.

For an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings, so $q = 0$. The first law becomes $\Delta U = w$.

During adiabatic expansion, work is done by the gas on the surroundings, meaning $w \lt 0$. Consequently, $\Delta U \lt 0$, which indicates a decrease in the internal energy of the system.

During adiabatic compression, work is done on the gas, meaning $w \gt 0$, leading to an increase in internal energy.

Answer: Adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the change in internal energy if an ideal gas expands from $0.5\ \text{dm}^3$ to $3.5\ \text{dm}^3$ at constant pressure 2 bar by absorbing 1800 J heat energy.
questions.solution:
Given $V_1 = 0.5\ \text{dm}^3$, $V_2 = 3.5\ \text{dm}^3$, $P = 2\ \text{bar}$, and heat absorbed $q = 1800\ \text{J}$.

Work done during expansion at constant pressure is given by $W = -P(V_2 - V_1)$.

$W = -2 \times (3.5 - 0.5) = -6\ \text{bar}\cdot\text{dm}^3$

Since $1\ \text{bar}\cdot\text{dm}^3 = 100\ \text{J}$, we have $W = -600\ \text{J}$.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + W$.

Substituting the values, $\Delta U = 1800 - 600 = 1200\ \text{J}$.

Answer: $1200$ J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion of C, $\text{H}_2$, and $\text{CH}_4$ are $-390$, $-285$ and $-890$ kJ/mol. Find the enthalpy of formation of methane.
questions.solution:
The required reaction for the formation of methane is:

$\text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_4\text{(g)}$

The enthalpy of formation can be calculated using the enthalpies of combustion of the reactants and products:

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = \Delta H_c(\text{C}) + 2\Delta H_c(\text{H}_2) - \Delta H_c(\text{CH}_4)$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -390 + 2(-285) - (-890)$

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -390 - 570 + 890$

$\Delta H_f(\text{CH}_4) = -960 + 890 = -70 \text{ kJ/mol}$

Answer: $-70$ kJ

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the law for the statement "Overall the enthalpy change for a reaction is equal to sum of enthalpy changes of individual steps in the reaction"
questions.solution:
Hess's law of constant heat summation states that the total enthalpy change for a chemical reaction is independent of the path by which the reaction occurs.

If a reaction takes place in several steps, the overall enthalpy change is equal to the sum of the enthalpy changes of the individual steps. This is because enthalpy is a state function, meaning it depends only on the initial and final states of the system, not on the path taken.

Answer: Hess's law

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If $2$ mole of an ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly at $27^\circ$C from 1 $\text{dm}^3$ to $1\ \text{m}^3$ calculate work done? $[R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}]$
questions.solution:
Given:

$n = 2\text{ mol}$

$T = 27^\circ\text{C} = 300\text{ K}$

$V_1 = 1\text{ dm}^3$

$V_2 = 1\text{ m}^3 = 1000\text{ dm}^3$

$R = 8.314\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$

The work done in a reversible isothermal expansion is given by:

$W = -2.303 nRT \log_{10} \left( \dfrac{V_2}{V_1} \right)$

Substituting the given values:

$W = -2.303 \times 2 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log_{10} \left( \dfrac{1000}{1} \right)$

$W = -2.303 \times 600 \times 8.314 \times 3$

$W = -34464.8\text{ J}$

$W = -34.46\text{ kJ}$

Answer: $-34.46$ kJ

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is NOT a state function ?
questions.solution:
State functions are properties whose values depend only on the state of the system and are independent of the path followed to reach that state.

Pressure, volume, and temperature are state functions because they depend only on the initial and final states of the system.

Work and heat are path functions because their values depend on the specific path taken to go from the initial state to the final state.

Therefore, work is not a state function.

Answer: Work

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the work done for the following reaction at $27\,^\circ\text{C}$
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_{4(g)} + \text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{6(g)}$ ($R = 8.314\,\text{JK}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_{4(g)} + \text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{6(g)}$

Change in number of moles of gaseous species, $\Delta n_g = n_p - n_r$

$\Delta n_g = 1 - (1 + 1) = -1$

Work done, $W = -\Delta n_g RT$

$W = -(-1) \times 8.314 \times (27 + 273)$

$W = 1 \times 8.314 \times 300$

$W = 2494.2$ J

Answer: $2494.2$ J

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate standard Gibbs energy for any gaseous reaction if values of $K_p$ and $R$ respectively are $3.5 \times 10^{17}$ ; $8.314\,\text{JK}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by the relation:

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -RT \ln K_p = -2.303 RT \log K_p$

Assuming standard temperature $T = 298\,\text{K}$:

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -2.303 \times 8.314 \times 298 \times \log(3.5 \times 10^{17})$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -5705.8 \times (\log 3.5 + 17)$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -5705.8 \times (0.544 + 17)$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -5705.8 \times 17.544$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -100102\,\text{J mol}^{-1} \approx -100.1\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-100.1\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An ideal gas expands from initial volume $5\ \text{dm}^3$ to $15\ \text{dm}^3$ against a constant external pressure of $2$ atm. What is the work done by the gas ?
questions.solution:
The work done by a gas during expansion against a constant external pressure is given by the formula:

$W = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V$

Given:
$P_{\text{ext}} = 2\ \text{atm}$
$V_i = 5\ \text{dm}^3 = 5\ \text{L}$
$V_f = 15\ \text{dm}^3 = 15\ \text{L}$

Change in volume:
$\Delta V = V_f - V_i = 15 - 5 = 10\ \text{L}$

Substituting the values into the formula:
$W = -2\ \text{atm} \times 10\ \text{L} = -20\ \text{L}\ \text{atm}$

To convert the work done into Joules, use the conversion factor $1\ \text{L}\ \text{atm} = 101.32\ \text{J}$:
$W = -20 \times 101.32\ \text{J} = -2026.4\ \text{J}$

Answer: $-2026.4$ J

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas absorbs $120$ J of heat and expands by $300 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{m}^3$ against a constant external pressure of $2 \times 10^5\ \text{Nm}^{-2}$. What will be the change in internal energy of the system ?
questions.solution:
Heat absorbed by the gas, $q = +120\ \text{J}$

Work done by the gas during expansion against constant external pressure is given by $W = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V$

Substituting the given values:

$W = -(2 \times 10^5\ \text{Nm}^{-2}) \times (300 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{m}^3)$

$W = -60\ \text{J}$

According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta U = q + W$

$\Delta U = 120\ \text{J} - 60\ \text{J} = 60\ \text{J}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify from following, the relation between standard free energy change in a reaction and equilibrium constant $K_c$.
questions.solution:
The relation between the free energy change and the reaction quotient is given by $\Delta G = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln Q$.

At equilibrium, the free energy change $\Delta G = 0$ and the reaction quotient $Q = K_c$.

Substituting these values into the equation, we get $0 = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln K_c$.

Rearranging the terms yields $-\Delta G^\circ = RT \ln K_c$.

Answer: $-\triangle G^\circ = RT \ln K_c$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the standard enthalpy change for the following reaction,
$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{(g)} + 7\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 4\text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}\text{(l)}$
Given, $\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6) = -85\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{CO}_2) = -390\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta_f H^\circ(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = -285\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
The standard enthalpy of reaction is calculated using the formula:

$\Delta_r H^\circ = \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{reactants})$

For the given reaction:

$\Delta_r H^\circ = [4 \times \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{CO}_2) + 6 \times \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{H}_2\text{O})] - [2 \times \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6) + 7 \times \Delta_f H^\circ(\text{O}_2)]$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta_r H^\circ = [4(-390) + 6(-285)] - [2(-85) + 7(0)]$

$\Delta_r H^\circ = [-1560 - 1710] - [-170]$

$\Delta_r H^\circ = -3270 + 170 = -3100\ \text{kJ}$

Answer: $-3100\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct expression of the first law of thermodynamics for adiabatic processes ?
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, the change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = Q + W$.

For an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange between the system and the surroundings, which means $Q = 0$.

Substituting $Q = 0$ into the first law equation, we get $\Delta U = W$.

Multiplying both sides by $-1$, this can be written as $-\Delta U = -W$.

Answer: $-\Delta U = -W$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 1 mole of an ideal gas is compressed isothermally and reversibly from initial pressure $x$ kPa to final pressure $2x$ kPa at 300 K. Find the work done $(R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1})$
questions.solution:
For an isothermal reversible process, the work done is given by:

$W = nRT \ln\left(\dfrac{P_2}{P_1}\right)$

Substituting the given values:

$n = 1$ mol

$T = 300$ K

$P_1 = x$ kPa

$P_2 = 2x$ kPa

$R = 8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$

$W = 1 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \ln\left(\dfrac{2x}{x}\right)$

$W = 2494.2 \times \ln(2)$

$W = 2494.2 \times 0.693$

$W \approx 1729$ J

Answer: $1729$ J

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is correct expression of first law of thermodynamics for isothermal process?
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, the change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = Q + W$.

For an isothermal process, the temperature of the system remains constant, so $\Delta T = 0$.

Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, the change in internal energy is zero, $\Delta U = 0$.

Substituting $\Delta U = 0$ into the first law equation gives:

$0 = Q + W$

$W = -Q$

Answer: $\text{W} = -\text{Q}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reaction, $\Delta\text{H}^\circ = 40\ \text{kJ}$ and $\Delta\text{S}^\circ = 80\ \text{JK}^{-1}$. Find the temperature so that $\Delta\text{G}^\circ = 0$
questions.solution:
Using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$

For $\Delta G^\circ = 0$, we get:

$T = \dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{\Delta S^\circ}$

Given $\Delta H^\circ = 40\ \text{kJ} = 40000\ \text{J}$ and $\Delta S^\circ = 80\ \text{J K}^{-1}$.

Substituting the values:

$T = \dfrac{40000}{80} = 500\ \text{K}$

Answer: $500\ \text{K}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate $\Delta\text{H}$ for the following reaction at $300\ \text{K}$
$2\text{C}_{(s)} + 3\text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{6(g)}$ if $\Delta\text{U}$ for the reaction is $-80\ \text{kJ}$ ($\text{R} = 8.314\ \text{JK}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $2\text{C}_{(s)} + 3\text{H}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_{6(g)}$

Change in number of gaseous moles, $\Delta n_g = n_{p(g)} - n_{r(g)} = 1 - 3 = -2$

Given $\Delta\text{U} = -80\ \text{kJ}$

$T = 300\ \text{K}$

$R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1} = 8.314 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{kJ K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$

Using the relation $\Delta\text{H} = \Delta\text{U} + \Delta n_g RT$

$\Delta\text{H} = -80 + (-2) \times 8.314 \times 10^{-3} \times 300$

$\Delta\text{H} = -80 - 4.9884$

$\Delta\text{H} = -84.9884\ \text{kJ} \approx -85.00\ \text{kJ}$

Answer: $-85.00\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following processes is an endothermic ?
options: The aqueous NaOH and HCl solutions mixed together.
Formation of ammonia by Haber process.
questions.solution:
Mixing of aqueous NaOH and HCl is a neutralization reaction, which is highly exothermic.

Formation of ammonia by the Haber process is an exothermic reaction as heat is released.

Melting of ice requires the absorption of heat from the surroundings to overcome the intermolecular forces of attraction between water molecules. Thus, it is an endothermic process.

Freezing of liquid water releases heat to the surroundings, making it an exothermic process.

Answer: Ice melts at room temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the standard enthalpy of combustion of carbon monoxide if
$\Delta_f H^\circ (\text{CO}) = -110 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$\Delta_f H^\circ (\text{CO}_2) = -393 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction of carbon monoxide is given by:

$\text{CO(g)} + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$

The standard enthalpy of combustion is calculated using the standard enthalpies of formation:

$\Delta_c H^\circ (\text{CO}) = \sum \Delta_f H^\circ (\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_f H^\circ (\text{reactants})$

$\Delta_c H^\circ (\text{CO}) = \Delta_f H^\circ (\text{CO}_2) - \left[ \Delta_f H^\circ (\text{CO}) + \dfrac{1}{2} \Delta_f H^\circ (\text{O}_2) \right]$

Since the standard enthalpy of formation of $\text{O}_2$ in its standard state is zero:

$\Delta_c H^\circ (\text{CO}) = -393 - (-110 + 0)$

$\Delta_c H^\circ (\text{CO}) = -393 + 110 = -283 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-283 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the quantity of heat released from system when 2 moles of and ideal gas compressed isothermally from volume $25 \text{ dm}^3$ to $10 \text{ dm}^3$ at constant external pressure 4 bar.
questions.solution:
For an isothermal process of an ideal gas, the change in internal energy $\Delta U = 0$.

From the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta U = q + w \Rightarrow q = -w$

The work done during irreversible compression at a constant external pressure is given by:

$w = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V = -P_{\text{ext}} (V_2 - V_1)$

Given:

$P_{\text{ext}} = 4 \text{ bar}$

$V_1 = 25 \text{ dm}^3$

$V_2 = 10 \text{ dm}^3$

Substituting the values:

$w = -4 \times (10 - 25) = 60 \text{ bar} \cdot \text{dm}^3$

Since $1 \text{ bar} \cdot \text{dm}^3 = 100 \text{ J}$:

$w = 60 \times 100 \text{ J} = 6000 \text{ J} = 6.0 \text{ kJ}$

Therefore, $q = -6.0 \text{ kJ}$.

The quantity of heat released from the system is $6.0 \text{ kJ}$.

Answer: $6 \cdot 0 \text{ kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At $25\ ^\circ\text{C}$ standard enthalpy of combustion of $\text{H}_2$, Cyclohexene and cyclohexane are -241, -3800 and -3920 kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. What is the heat of hydrogenation of cyclohexene?
questions.solution:
The hydrogenation reaction of cyclohexene is given by:

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$

The enthalpy of hydrogenation can be calculated using the standard enthalpies of combustion of the reactants and products:

$\Delta H = \sum \Delta H_c(\text{Reactants}) - \sum \Delta H_c(\text{Products})$

$\Delta H = \Delta H_c(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}) + \Delta H_c(\text{H}_2) - \Delta H_c(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12})$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H = -3800 + (-241) - (-3920)$

$\Delta H = -4041 + 3920 = -121 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-121$ kJ

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A system is provided 50 J of heat and work done on the system is 10 J. What is change in internal energy ?
questions.solution:
According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta U = q + w$

where $q$ is the heat supplied to the system and $w$ is the work done on the system.

Given:

$q = +50$ J (heat is provided to the system)

$w = +10$ J (work is done on the system)

Substituting the values:

$\Delta U = 50 + 10 = 60$ J

Answer: $60$ J

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following equations is used to obtain enthalpy change of a reaction?
questions.solution:
The enthalpy change of a reaction is defined as the difference between the sum of the enthalpies of the products and the sum of the enthalpies of the reactants.

$\Delta H = \sum \Delta H_P - \sum \Delta H_R$

where $\sum \Delta H_P$ is the sum of enthalpies of products and $\sum \Delta H_R$ is the sum of enthalpies of reactants.

Answer: $\Delta H = \sum \Delta H_P - \sum \Delta H_R$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the process that proceeds with no heat exchange between system and surrounding.
questions.solution:
An adiabatic process is defined as a thermodynamic process in which there is no heat exchange between the system and its surroundings. In this process, $q = 0$.

An isothermal process occurs at constant temperature ($\Delta T = 0$).

An isobaric process occurs at constant pressure ($\Delta P = 0$).

An isochoric process occurs at constant volume ($\Delta V = 0$).

Answer: Adiabatic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the enthalpy change when 6 g. $\text{CO(g)}$ reacts with sufficient $\text{NO}_2\text{(g)}$ according to the following reaction
$4\,\text{CO(g)} + 2\,\text{NO}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 4\,\text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{N}_2\text{(g)}\,;\ \Delta_r H^0 = -1200\ \text{kJ}$
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{CO} = 12 + 16 = 28\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Number of moles of $\text{CO} = \dfrac{6}{28} = \dfrac{3}{14}\ \text{mol}$

From the given balanced equation, the enthalpy change for the reaction of $4\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO}$ is $-1200\ \text{kJ}$.

Enthalpy change for $1\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO} = \dfrac{-1200}{4} = -300\ \text{kJ}$

Enthalpy change for $\dfrac{3}{14}\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO} = -300 \times \dfrac{3}{14} = -64.285\ \text{kJ} \approx -64.29\ \text{kJ}$

Answer: $-64.29\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The heat of combustion of carbon to $\text{CO}_2$ is $-393.5\ \text{kJ/mol}$. The heat released upon formation of 35.2 g of $\text{CO}_2$ from carbon and oxygen gas is
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction of carbon is given by:

$\text{C(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$

The heat of combustion of carbon to $\text{CO}_2$ is $\Delta H = -393.5\ \text{kJ/mol}$.

Molar mass of $\text{CO}_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44\ \text{g/mol}$.

Number of moles in $35.2\ \text{g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is:

$n = \dfrac{35.2}{44} = 0.8\ \text{mol}$

The enthalpy change for the formation of $0.8\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is:

$\Delta H = 0.8\ \text{mol} \times (-393.5\ \text{kJ/mol}) = -314.8\ \text{kJ} \approx -315\ \text{kJ}$

The negative sign indicates that the heat is released during the process.

Answer: $-315\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct ?
options: For a chemical reaction to be spontaneous $\Delta G$ must be $-\text{ve}$.
Electrical work is equal to $\Delta G$
questions.solution:
Gibbs free energy ($G$) and standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^\circ$) depend on the quantity of the substance, hence they are extensive properties.

Standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$) is independent of the amount of substance, hence it is an intensive property.

For a spontaneous reaction at constant temperature and pressure, the change in Gibbs free energy ($\Delta G$) must be negative ($\Delta G \lt 0$).

The reversible electrical work done by a galvanic cell is equal to the decrease in its Gibbs free energy. Therefore, electrical work done by the system is equal to $-\Delta G$, not $\Delta G$.

Thus, the statement "Electrical work is equal to $\Delta G$" is incorrect.

Answer: Electrical work is equal to $\Delta G$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following relations is correct for a reaction $\text{S}_{(s)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightarrow \text{SO}_{2(g)}$ ?
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $\text{S}_{(s)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightarrow \text{SO}_{2(g)}$

The relationship between enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and internal energy change ($\Delta U$) is given by:

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$

where $\Delta n_g$ is the change in the number of moles of gaseous substances.

$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$

For the given reaction, $\text{SO}_{2}$ is the only gaseous product and $\text{O}_{2}$ is the only gaseous reactant. Solid sulfur ($\text{S}_{(s)}$) is not considered.

$\Delta n_g = 1 - 1 = 0$

Substituting $\Delta n_g = 0$ into the equation:

$\Delta H = \Delta U + (0)RT$

$\Delta H = \Delta U$

Answer: $\Delta H = \Delta U$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a particular reaction, 4 kJ heat is released by the system and 12 kJ work done on the system. Calculate the $\Delta H$ and $\Delta U$.
questions.solution:
Heat released by the system, $q = -4$ kJ.

Work done on the system, $w = +12$ kJ.

According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta U = q + w$

$\Delta U = -4 + 12 = 8$ kJ.

For a reaction at constant pressure, the enthalpy change is equal to the heat exchanged:

$\Delta H = q_p = -4$ kJ.

Answer: $\Delta H = -4$ kJ and $\Delta U = 8$ kJ

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the change in entropy of surrounding for the reaction,
$\text{H}_{2(g)} + 1/2\ \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(l)}$
at 298 K if standard enthalpy of formation of water is $-286$ kJ ?
questions.solution:
The standard enthalpy of formation of water is the enthalpy change of the system for the given reaction.

$\Delta H_{\text{sys}} = -286\ \text{kJ} = -286000\ \text{J}$

The heat absorbed by the surroundings at constant pressure is given by:

$q_{\text{surr}} = -\Delta H_{\text{sys}} = 286000\ \text{J}$

The change in entropy of the surroundings is calculated as:

$\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = \dfrac{q_{\text{surr}}}{T}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = \dfrac{286000}{298} = 959.7\ \text{J K}^{-1}$

Answer: $959.7\ \text{JK}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a reaction to be spontaneous at all temperatures, the values of enthalpy change and entropy change should be
questions.solution:
For a reaction to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy must be negative, i.e., $\Delta G \lt 0$.

The relationship between $\Delta G$, enthalpy change $\Delta H$, and entropy change $\Delta S$ is given by the Gibbs equation:

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

Since absolute temperature $T$ is always positive, for $\Delta G$ to be negative at all temperatures, both terms contributing to $\Delta G$ must favor spontaneity. This happens when:

$\Delta H \lt 0$ (exothermic reaction)
$\Delta S \gt 0$ (increase in entropy)

Under these conditions, the term $-T\Delta S$ is negative, and since $\Delta H$ is also negative, their sum $\Delta G$ will always be negative regardless of the temperature.

Answer: $\Delta H \lt 0$ and $\Delta S \gt 0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reaction, $\Delta H^0$ is $-345$ kJ and $\Delta S^0$ is $-123\ \text{JK}^{-1}$. At what temperature the change over from spontaneous to nonspontaneous will occur?
questions.solution:
The changeover from spontaneous to nonspontaneous occurs when $\Delta G^0 = 0$.

Using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G^0 = \Delta H^0 - T\Delta S^0$

Setting $\Delta G^0 = 0$ gives:

$T = \dfrac{\Delta H^0}{\Delta S^0}$

Substituting the given values (converting $\Delta H^0$ to Joules):

$T = \dfrac{-345 \times 10^3 \text{ J}}{-123 \text{ JK}^{-1}}$

$T = 2804.87 \text{ K}$

$T \approx 2805 \text{ K}$

Answer: $2805$ K

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following properties of a system depends upon the amount of matter and path?
questions.solution:
Properties that depend on the amount of matter present in the system are known as extensive properties.

Properties whose values depend on the specific path taken to go from the initial state to the final state are known as path functions.

Free energy, enthalpy, and entropy are state functions, meaning their values depend only on the initial and final states of the system and are independent of the path followed.

Heat is a path function because the amount of heat exchanged depends on the process or path taken. It also depends on the amount of matter (extensive in nature), as the heat required to change the state of a system is proportional to its mass or number of moles ($q = mc\Delta T$).

Answer: Heat

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following processes has $\Delta S$ negative?
options: Adsorption of a Gas on a Solid Surface
questions.solution:
Entropy ($\Delta S$) is a measure of randomness or disorder in a system.

For dissolving sugar in water, solid sugar molecules break apart and mix with water, increasing the randomness. Thus, $\Delta S \gt 0$.

For the adsorption of a gas on a solid surface, the gas molecules are restricted to the surface of the solid, which decreases their translational degrees of freedom. The randomness of the system decreases, leading to $\Delta S \lt 0$.

For the reaction $2\text{NH}_3(g) \rightarrow \text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g)$, the number of gaseous moles increases from $2$ to $4$ ($\Delta n_g = 2$). An increase in gaseous moles increases randomness, so $\Delta S \gt 0$.

For the sublimation of dry ice, solid $\text{CO}_2$ converts into gaseous $\text{CO}_2$. Since gases are more disordered than solids, $\Delta S \gt 0$.

Therefore, the only process with a negative $\Delta S$ is the adsorption of a gas on a solid surface.

Answer: Adsorption of a Gas on a Solid Surface

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}(l) + 3\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$
The value of enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) for above reaction at $27\,^\circ\text{C}$ is $-1366.5$ kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$. Then value of internal energy change for the same reaction at this temperature will be
questions.solution:
The given chemical equation is:

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}(l) + 3\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$

The change in the number of moles of gaseous species, $\Delta n_g$, is calculated as:

$\Delta n_g = n_{p(g)} - n_{r(g)} = 2 - 3 = -1$

The relationship between enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and internal energy change ($\Delta U$) is given by:

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$

Given:
$\Delta H = -1366.5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
$R = 8.314 \times 10^{-3} \text{ kJ K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$
$T = 27^\circ\text{C} = 300 \text{ K}$

Substituting the values into the equation:

$-1366.5 = \Delta U + (-1) \times (8.314 \times 10^{-3}) \times 300$

$-1366.5 = \Delta U - 2.4942$

$\Delta U = -1366.5 + 2.4942 = -1364.0058 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to one decimal place, we get $-1364.0 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $-1364.0$ kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following processes the internal energy of system remain constant?
questions.solution:
The internal energy of an ideal gas is a function of its temperature only, given by $U = \dfrac{f}{2} n R T$.

For the internal energy to remain constant, the change in temperature must be zero ($\Delta T = 0$).

A process in which the temperature of the system remains constant is known as an isothermal process.

Therefore, the internal energy of the system remains constant in an isothermal process.

Answer: Isothermal Process

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas expands from a volume of $1$ dm$^3$ to $1.25$ dm$^3$ under a pressure of $1$ bar. Find the change in internal energy if $150$ J of heat is supplied to the system.
questions.solution:
Given $V_1 = 1$ dm$^3$ and $V_2 = 1.25$ dm$^3$.

Change in volume, $\Delta V = 1.25 - 1 = 0.25$ dm$^3 = 0.25$ L.

External pressure, $P = 1$ bar.

Work done during expansion is given by $W = -P \Delta V$.

$W = -1 \times 0.25 = -0.25$ L bar.

Since $1$ L bar $= 100$ J, we have $W = -0.25 \times 100 = -25$ J.

Heat supplied to the system, $q = 150$ J.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = q + W$.

$\Delta U = 150 - 25 = 125$ J.

Answer: $125$ J

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion of cyclohexane, cyclohexene and $\text{H}_2$ are respectively $-3920, -3800$ and $-241$ KJ mol$^{-1}$. The enthalpy of hydrogenation of cyclohexene is
questions.solution:
The hydrogenation reaction of cyclohexene is given by:

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$

The enthalpy of hydrogenation can be calculated using the enthalpies of combustion of the reactants and products:

$\Delta H = \sum \Delta H_c(\text{reactants}) - \sum \Delta H_c(\text{products})$

$\Delta H = [\Delta H_c(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}) + \Delta H_c(\text{H}_2)] - \Delta H_c(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12})$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H = [-3800 + (-241)] - (-3920)$

$\Delta H = -4041 + 3920$

$\Delta H = -121 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-121$ KJ mol$^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the enthalpy change of the reaction,
$\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl(g)}$
if bond energies (kJ mol$^{-1}$):
H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 242, H–Cl = 431
questions.solution:
The enthalpy change of the reaction is given by the difference between the sum of bond energies of reactants and the sum of bond energies of products.

$\Delta H = \sum \text{BE(Reactants)} - \sum \text{BE(Products)}$

For the given reaction:
$\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl(g)}$

$\Delta H = [\text{BE(H-H)} + \text{BE(Cl-Cl)}] - [2 \times \text{BE(H-Cl)}]$

Substituting the given values:
$\Delta H = (436 + 242) - (2 \times 431)$

$\Delta H = 678 - 862$

$\Delta H = -184 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-184$ kJ/mol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reaction $\Delta H = -50$ kJ and $\Delta S = -100$ J/K find the temperature so that the reaction is spontaneous.
questions.solution:
For a reaction to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy must be negative, i.e., $\Delta G \lt 0$.

Using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

Substituting the given values ($\Delta H = -50000$ J and $\Delta S = -100$ J/K):

$-50000 - T(-100) \lt 0$

$-50000 + 100T \lt 0$

$100T \lt 50000$

$T \lt 500$ K

The reaction is spontaneous at temperatures below $500$ K. Among the given options, only $450$ K satisfies this condition.

Answer: $450$ K

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{H}_2$, $\text{Cl}_2$ and HCl are $434$, $242$ and $431$ kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. Calculate the enthalpy of formation of HCl.
questions.solution:
The reaction for the formation of HCl is:

$\dfrac{1}{2} \text{H}_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{Cl}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{HCl}(g)$

The enthalpy of formation is given by:

$\Delta_f H = \sum \text{BE}(\text{reactants}) - \sum \text{BE}(\text{products})$

$\Delta_f H = \left[ \dfrac{1}{2} \text{BE}(\text{H}_2) + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{BE}(\text{Cl}_2) \right] - \text{BE}(\text{HCl})$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta_f H = \left[ \dfrac{1}{2}(434) + \dfrac{1}{2}(242) \right] - 431$

$\Delta_f H = (217 + 121) - 431$

$\Delta_f H = 338 - 431 = -93 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-93$ kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The equilibrium constant for a reaction is $100$. What will be the value of standard Gibbs energy change at $298$ K ? ($R = 8.314$ J $\text{K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by the equation:

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -RT \ln K = -2.303 RT \log K$

Substituting the given values:

$R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$
$T = 298 \text{ K}$
$K = 100$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -2.303 \times 8.314 \times 298 \times \log(100)$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -2.303 \times 8.314 \times 298 \times 2$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -11411.7 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta G^{\circ} \approx -11.411 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-11.411$ KJ/mol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following processes exhibits, $\Delta U = 0$?
questions.solution:
The internal energy of an ideal gas is a function of temperature only.

The change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = n C_v \Delta T$.

In an isothermal process, the temperature of the system remains constant, which implies $\Delta T = 0$.

Substituting $\Delta T = 0$ yields $\Delta U = 0$.

Therefore, an isothermal process exhibits $\Delta U = 0$.

Answer: Isothermal process

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the work done when $1$ mole of an ideal gas is expanded reversibly and isothermally from initial pressure $10$ bar to final pressure $1$ bar at constant temperature $300$ K. [$R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
For a reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, the work done is given by the formula:

$W = -2.303 nRT \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$

Given:
$n = 1 \text{ mol}$
$R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$
$T = 300 \text{ K}$
$P_1 = 10 \text{ bar}$
$P_2 = 1 \text{ bar}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$W = -2.303 \times 1 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{10}{1}\right)$

$W = -2.303 \times 2494.2 \times 1$

$W = -5744.14 \text{ J}$

$W = -5.744 \text{ kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the enthalpy change for the following reaction, using given bond energy (kJ/mol)
(C-H = $414$, H-O = $463$, H-Cl = $431$, C-Cl = $326$ and C-O = $335$)
$\text{CH}_3\text{OH}_{(g)} + \text{HCl}_{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}_{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O}_{(g)}$
questions.solution:
The enthalpy of reaction is given by:

$\Delta H = \sum \text{BE(Reactants)} - \sum \text{BE(Products)}$

$\Delta H = [3 \times \text{BE(C-H)} + \text{BE(C-O)} + \text{BE(O-H)} + \text{BE(H-Cl)}] - [3 \times \text{BE(C-H)} + \text{BE(C-Cl)} + 2 \times \text{BE(O-H)}]$

Canceling the common bond energies on both sides:

$\Delta H = \text{BE(C-O)} + \text{BE(H-Cl)} - \text{BE(C-Cl)} - \text{BE(O-H)}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H = 335 + 431 - 326 - 463$

$\Delta H = 766 - 789 = -23 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-23 \text{ kJmol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the work done in the oxidation of one mole $\mathrm{HCl}_{(\mathrm{g})}$ at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, according to reaction.
$4 \mathrm{HCl}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{O}_{2_{(\mathrm{g})}} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cl}_{2_{(\mathrm{g})}}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})} \quad\left(\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)$
questions.solution:
The work done during gaseous reactions under constant temperature and pressure is given by $W = -\Delta n_g RT$, where $\Delta n_g$ is the change in the number of moles of gas.

For $4\mathrm{HCl}_{(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{O}_{2_{(\mathrm{g})}} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cl}_{2_{(\mathrm{g})}} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})}$, the gaseous moles are: reactants = 5, products = 4, so $\Delta n_g = -1$.

Per mole of $\mathrm{HCl}_{(\mathrm{g})}$, $\Delta n_g = -1/4 = -0.25$.

At $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ and $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$, $W = -(-0.25) \times 8.314 \times 300 = 623.55\ \mathrm{J}$.

This value corresponds to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is an example of an intensive property of the system?
questions.solution:
Intensive properties remain invariant with respect to the quantity of substance, while extensive properties scale proportionally with the amount.

Volume is extensive, as it increases with the quantity of matter.
Enthalpy and entropy are both extensive thermodynamic quantities dependent on system size.

Molar volume, defined as $v = V/n$, represents the ratio of two extensive properties.
This quotient yields an intensive property, as demonstrated by the constant molar volume of substances like water under fixed conditions.

The intensive property is molar volume.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reaction $\Delta H=-225 \mathrm{~kJ}$ and $\Delta S=-150 \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$. Find the temperature so that $\Delta \mathrm{G}$ is zero.
questions.solution:
The temperature where $\Delta G$ becomes zero corresponds to the condition $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = 0$.

For $\Delta H = -225\ \mathrm{kJ}$ and $\Delta S = -150\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$, convert $\Delta H$ to consistent units: $\Delta H = -225,\!000\ \mathrm{J}$.

Solving $0 = \Delta H - T\Delta S$ yields $T = \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S} = \frac{-225,\!000\ \mathrm{J}}{-150\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}} = 1,\!500\ \mathrm{K}$.

The temperature at which $\Delta G = 0$ is therefore $1,\!500\ \mathrm{K}$.

The correct option is A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following processes occurs in the reaction given below
$\mathrm{C}_{\text {(graphite) }} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{g})} \text { ? }$
questions.solution:
The reaction $\mathrm{C}_{\text{(graphite)}} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C}_{(\mathrm{g})}$ represents the direct transformation of solid carbon into gaseous carbon.

Vaporization and fusion describe liquid-gas and solid-liquid phase transitions respectively, while ionization involves electron transfer. Sublimation specifically denotes the direct solid-to-gas transformation without an intermediate liquid phase.

This corresponds precisely to option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the work done in kJ when 3 moles of an ideal gas at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ expand isothermally and reversibly from 10 atm . to $1 \mathrm{~atm}\left[\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution:
The work done in an isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas is given by $W = -nRT \ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$.

For an isothermal process, Boyle's law implies $P_1V_1 = P_2V_2$, so $\frac{V_2}{V_1} = \frac{P_1}{P_2}$.
Substituting gives $W = -nRT \ln\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$.

Using the values $n = 3$ mol, $T = 300$ K, $R = 8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$, $P_1 = 10$ atm, and $P_2 = 1$ atm:

$W = -(3)(8.314)(300) \ln(10)$

Since $\ln(10) \approx 2.303$, we compute:

$W = -3 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times 2.303 = -17230.9$ J

Converting to kilojoules: $W = \frac{-17230.9}{1000} = -17.2309$ kJ, which rounds to $-17.23$ kJ.

The value $-17.23$ kJ corresponds to option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a reversible expansion, one mole of gas is expanded isothermally at 200 K till its volume increases 10 times. Calculate $\Delta S_{\text {total }}$ at equilibrium?
questions.solution:
For a reversible process, the total entropy change $\Delta S_{\text{total}}$ is defined as $\Delta S_{\text{system}} + \Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$.

During a reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, the entropy change of the system is $\Delta S_{\text{system}} = nR \ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$. The surrounding's entropy change is $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = -\frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}$, equal to $-\Delta S_{\text{system}}$. Consequently, the sum is $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{system}} + (-\Delta S_{\text{system}}) = 0$.

Given that $n = 1$ mol, $T = 200$ K, and $\frac{V_2}{V_1} = 10$, the system's entropy change is $\Delta S_{\text{system}} = 8.314 \cdot \ln(10) \approx 19.14 \text{ J K}^{-1}$ and $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} \approx -19.14 \text{ J K}^{-1}$, confirming the net effect.

$\boxed{\text{Zero J}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the work done if 1 mole of certain gas compressed isothermally and reversibly at 300 K from initial pressure $x$ bar to final pressure $2 x$ bar $\left[\mathrm{R}=8 \cdot 314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution:
Work during isothermal reversible compression of an ideal gas:

The work done is given by $\mathrm{W} = -\mathrm{nRT} \ln\left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_1}{\mathrm{P}_2}\right)$.

Substituting the given values: $n = 1\ \text{mol}$, $T = 300\ \text{K}$, $R = 8.314\ \text{J}\ \text{K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$, and $\frac{\mathrm{P}_1}{\mathrm{P}_2} = \frac{x}{2x} = \frac{1}{2}$.

$\mathrm{W} = -(1) \times (8.314) \times (300) \times \ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$

$\mathrm{W} = -2494.2 \times \ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$

Since $\ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\ln(2) \approx -0.6931$:

$\mathrm{W} = -2494.2 \times (-0.6931) = 1728.86\ \text{J}$

Converting to kilojoules: $\mathrm{W} = 1.72886\ \text{kJ} \approx 1.729\ \text{kJ}$

The positive value indicates work is done on the system during compression, and this matches option A.

$\boxed{A}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the standard enthalpy change of following reaction.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{CH}_{4(\mathrm{~g})}+2 \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{~g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\ell)} \\
& \text { if } \quad \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}\left(C H_4\right)=-75 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\
& \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}\left(C \mathrm{O}_2\right)=-390 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\
& \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)=-286 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
The standard enthalpy change of the reaction is calculated using the formula:

$\Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ} = \sum n \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum m \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\text{reactants})$

For the reaction $\mathrm{CH}_{4(\mathrm{g})} + 2\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(\ell)}$ with given enthalpies: $\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\mathrm{CH}_4) = -75\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\mathrm{CO}_2) = -390\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, $\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}) = -286\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, and noting $\Delta_{\mathrm{f}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ}(\mathrm{O}_2) = 0\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$:

$\Delta_{\mathrm{r}} \mathrm{H}^{\circ} = [1 \times (-390) + 2 \times (-286)] - [1 \times (-75) + 2 \times 0] = [-390 - 572] - [-75] = -962 + 75 = -887\ \mathrm{kJ}$

The standard enthalpy change of the reaction is $-887\ \mathrm{kJ}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify from following the correct set of thermodynamic conditions for the reaction to be spontaneous at all temperature.
questions.solution:
The spontaneity of a reaction is determined by the sign of the Gibbs free energy change, given by $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$, where $\Delta G \lt 0$ indicates a spontaneous process.

For a reaction to be spontaneous at all temperatures, both terms must contribute negatively to $\Delta G$. When $\Delta H \lt 0$ and $\Delta S \gt 0$, the equation becomes $\Delta G = (\text{negative}) - T(\text{positive})$. Since $-T\Delta S$ is always negative under these conditions, $\Delta G$ remains negative regardless of temperature.

In contrast, other combinations show temperature dependence or constant non-spontaneity:
$\Delta H \gt 0$, $\Delta S \gt 0$: spontaneous only at high temperatures
$\Delta H \lt 0$, $\Delta S \lt 0$: spontaneous only at low temperatures
$\Delta H \gt 0$, $\Delta S \lt 0$: non-spontaneous at all temperatures

The condition satisfying spontaneity at all temperatures corresponds to $\Delta H \lt 0$ and $\Delta S \gt 0$.

Answer: $\boxed{C}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the change in internal energy of the system if work done by the system is 18 joule and absorbs heat 50 joule in a particular reaction.
questions.solution:
The change in internal energy, $\Delta U$, is determined by the First Law of Thermodynamics: $\Delta U = q + w$, where $q$ is the heat absorbed and $w$ is the work done on the system.

Given $q = +50\text{ J}$ and $w = -18\text{ J}$ (indicating work done by the system), substitute into the equation:

$\Delta U = 50\text{ J} + (-18\text{ J}) = 32\text{ J}$.

Thus, $\Delta U = 32\text{ J}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify from following the correct set of thermodynamic conditions for the reaction to be nonspontaneous at all temperature.
questions.solution:
Spontaneity is determined by the Gibbs free energy change:

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T \Delta S$

For a reaction to be nonspontaneous at all temperatures, $\Delta G \gt 0$ must hold regardless of $T$.

A reaction with $\Delta H \gt 0$ and $\Delta S \lt 0$ gives $\Delta G = \text{positive} - T(\text{negative}) = \text{positive} + T(\text{positive})$.
Since both terms are positive, $\Delta G \gt 0$ for all $T$, ensuring nonspontaneity.

Other combinations depend on temperature: $\Delta H \lt 0$ and $\Delta S \lt 0$ can be spontaneous at low $T$, $\Delta H \gt 0$ and $\Delta S \gt 0$ can be spontaneous at high $T$, and $\Delta H \lt 0$ and $\Delta S \gt 0$ is always spontaneous.

Final answer: $\boxed{D}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate $\Delta S_{\text {total }}$ for a certain reaction if $\Delta H=-150 \mathrm{~kJ}$ and $\Delta S=32 \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$ at 300 K .
questions.solution:
The total entropy change for a reaction combines system and surroundings contributions: $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{system}} + \Delta S_{\text{surroundings}}$.

The entropy change of the surroundings follows from the enthalpy change at constant temperature: $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = -\frac{\Delta H}{T}$.

Given $\Delta H = -150 \times 10^3\ \mathrm{J}$ and $T = 300\ \mathrm{K}$, substitution yields $\Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = -\frac{-150 \times 10^3}{300} = 500\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$.

Adding the system entropy change $\Delta S_{\text{system}} = 32\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$ gives $\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 32 + 500 = 532\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$.

The value $532\ \mathrm{JK}^{-1}$ corresponds to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
