& \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{a}}-(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{a}}) \overline{\mathrm{c}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}=\overline{\mathrm{c}} \\
& \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{a}}-\overline{\mathrm{c}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}=\overline{0} \quad \quad \ldots\left[\because \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{a}}=|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2=1\right] \\
& \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{a}}-\overline{\mathrm{c}}=-\overline{\mathrm{b}} \\
& \Rightarrow|(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{a}}-\overline{\mathrm{c}}|=|-\overline{\mathrm{b}}| \\
& \Rightarrow\left|(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}})^{\overline{\mathrm{a}}-\overline{\mathrm{c}}}\right|^2=|\overline{\mathrm{b}}|^2 \\
& \Rightarrow|(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2+|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^2-2\{(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}\}=|\overline{\mathrm{b}}|^2 \\
& \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}})^2|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2+|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^2-2(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}})(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}})=|\overline{\mathrm{b}}|^2 \\
& \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}})^2\left\{|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2-2\right\}+|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^2=|\overline{\mathrm{b}}|^2
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow-(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}})^2+4=1 \quad \ldots\left[\because|\overline{\mathrm{~b}}|^2=1,|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^2=4\right] \\
& \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}})^2=3 \\
& \Rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}= \pm \sqrt{3} \\
& \Rightarrow|\overline{\mathrm{a}}||\overline{\mathrm{c}}| \cos \theta=\sqrt{3}
\end{aligned}$
where $\theta$ is an acute angle between $\overline{\mathrm{a}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}\Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{6}$

Vectors $\overline{\mathrm{a}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ are not perpendicular
$\begin{aligned}

questions.q:
Let $\overline{\mathrm{a}}, \overline{\mathrm{b}}, \overline{\mathrm{c}}$ be three non-coplanar vectors and $\overline{\mathrm{p}}, \overline{\mathrm{q}}, \overline{\mathrm{r}}$ defined by the relations
$\overline{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}}{[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{~b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]}, \overline{\mathrm{q}}=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}}}{[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{~b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]}, \overline{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}}{[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{~b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]}$
then the value of the expression $(\bar{a}+\bar{b}) \cdot \bar{p}+(\bar{b}+\bar{c}) \cdot \bar{q}+(\bar{c}+\bar{a}) \cdot \bar{r}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \overline{\mathrm{p}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}) & =\overline{\mathrm{p}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{p}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{b}} \\ & =\frac{(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \cdot \overline{\mathrm{a}}}{[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]}+\frac{(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \cdot \overline{\mathrm{b}}}{[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]} \\ & =\frac{[\overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}} \overline{\mathrm{a}}]}{[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]}+\frac{[\overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}} \overline{\mathrm{b}}]}{[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]} \\ & =1+0=1\end{aligned}$
Similarly, $\overline{\mathrm{q}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}})=1$ and $\overline{\mathrm{r}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}})=1\begin{aligned}
& (\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}) \cdot \overline{\mathrm{p}}+(\stackrel{\rightharpoonup}{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}) \cdot \overline{\mathrm{q}}+(\overline{\mathrm{c}}+\overline{\mathrm{a}}) \cdot \overline{\mathrm{r}} \\
& =1+1+1 \\
& =3
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Let $\overline{\mathrm{a}}=5 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{k}}, \overline{\mathrm{b}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $\bar{c}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$
Then, required unit vectors are given by $\bar{\alpha}= \pm \frac{\bar{a} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})}{|\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})|}$
Now, $\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})=(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{b}}-(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \overline{\mathrm{c}}\begin{aligned} & =9(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})-18(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \\ & =27 \hat{j}-9 \hat{k} \end{aligned}\therefore \quad|\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})|=\sqrt{729+81}=\sqrt{810}=9 \sqrt{10}$ Hence, required unit vectors are $\bar{\alpha}= \pm \frac{27 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-9 \hat{\mathrm{k}}}{9 \sqrt{10}}= \pm \frac{3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}}{\sqrt{10}}$

questions.q: Let $\overline{\mathrm{A}}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{k}, \overline{\mathrm{~B}}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{C}}=4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+7 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$. If a vector $\bar{R}$ satisfies $\bar{R} \times \bar{B}=\bar{C} \times \bar{B}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{R}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{A}}=0$, then $\overline{\mathrm{R}}$ is given by
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \overline{\mathrm{R}} \times \overline{\mathrm{B}}=\overline{\mathrm{C}} \times \overline{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{A}} \times(\overline{\mathrm{R}} \times \overline{\mathrm{B}})=\overline{\mathrm{A}} \times(\overline{\mathrm{C}} \times \overline{\mathrm{B}}) \\ & \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{B}}) \overline{\mathrm{R}}-(\overline{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{R}}) \overline{\mathrm{B}}=(\overline{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{B}}) \overline{\mathrm{C}}-(\overline{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{C}}) \overline{\mathrm{B}} \\ & \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{B}}) \overline{\mathrm{R}}-0=(\overline{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{B}}) \overline{\mathrm{C}}-(\overline{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{C}}) \overline{\mathrm{B}}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{R}}=\overline{\mathrm{C}}-\left(\frac{\overline{\mathrm{A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{C}}}{\overline{\mathrm{~A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{~B}}}\right) \overline{\mathrm{B}} \\
& \overline{\mathrm{~A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{C}}=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \cdot(4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+7 \hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\
& =2(4)+0(-3)+1(7) \\
& =15 \\
& \overline{\mathrm{~A}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{~B}}=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \cdot(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\
& =2(1)+0(1)+1(1) \\
& =3 \\
& \therefore \quad \overline{\mathrm{R}}=4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+7 \hat{\mathrm{k}}-\left(\frac{15}{3}\right)(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\
& =4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+7 \hat{\mathrm{k}}-5(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\
& =-\hat{i}-8 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}
\end{aligned}$

& \hat{\mathrm{j}} \times(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \hat{\mathrm{j}})=(\hat{\mathrm{j}} \cdot \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \overline{\mathrm{a}}-(\hat{\mathrm{j}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{a}}) \hat{\mathrm{j}} \\

questions.solution:
Volume of parallelopiped $=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & \alpha & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \alpha \\ \alpha & 0 & 1\end{array}\right|\therefore \quad \mathrm{V}=1+\alpha^3-\alpha$
For maxima or minima,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{d} \alpha}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 \alpha^2-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \alpha= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{~d} \alpha^2}=6 \alpha$
For $\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$,
$\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{~d} x^2} \gt 0\therefore \quad \mathrm{V}$ is minimum at $\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

$\begin{aligned}

& \Rightarrow 2 \lambda+2+9+3 \lambda=0 \\

& \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{-11}{5}

questions.q: The vectors are $\bar{a}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-2 \hat{k}, \bar{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$. If $\bar{c}$ is a vector such that $\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|$ and $|\overline{\mathrm{c}}-\overline{\mathrm{a}}|=2 \sqrt{2}$, angle between $\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $\frac{\pi}{4}$, then $|(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}|$ is
questions.solution:
Given that angle between $\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $\frac{\pi}{4}\therefore \quad|(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times \bar{c}|=|(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})||\bar{c}| \sin \frac{\pi}{4}$... (i)
Now, $\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{\mathrm{i}} & \hat{\mathrm{j}} & \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right|\begin{aligned}
& =\hat{\mathrm{i}}(0+2)-\hat{\mathrm{j}}(0+2)+\hat{\mathrm{k}}(2-1) \\
& =2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\
\therefore \quad \mid & |\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-2)^2+1}=3
\end{aligned}$
Given, $\overline{\mathrm{a}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{2^2+1^2+(-2)^2}=3$
Given, $|\overline{\mathrm{c}}-\mathrm{a}|=2 \sqrt{2}$
Squaring on both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& |\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^2+\mid-\mathrm{a}^2-2-\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=8 \\
& \Rightarrow\left|\mathrm{c}^2+3^2-2\right| \mathrm{c} \mid=8 \quad \ldots[\because \cdot \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|]
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow|\bar{c}|^2-2|\vec{c}|+1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(|\bar{c}|-1)^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow|\vec{c}|=1
\end{aligned}$
From (i),
$\begin{aligned}
|(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}| & =|(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})||\overline{\mathrm{c}}| \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{4} \\
& =3 \times 1 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\
& =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\bar{a}=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+\hat{k}, \bar{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \bar{c}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, then a vector in the plane of $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$, whose projection on $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, is
questions.solution:
Let $\overline{\mathrm{r}}$ be the vector coplanar to $\overline{\mathrm{a}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$. Then,
$\begin{aligned}
\overline{\mathrm{r}} & =\overline{\mathrm{a}}+\mathrm{m} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \\
& =(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})+\mathrm{m}(\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \\
& =\hat{\mathrm{i}}(1+\mathrm{m})+\hat{\mathrm{j}}(2-\mathrm{m})+\hat{\mathrm{k}}(1+\mathrm{m})
\end{aligned}$
Since the projection of $\overline{\mathrm{r}}$ along $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\overline{\mathrm{r}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}}{\overline{\mathrm{c}}}= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{(1+\mathrm{m})+(2-\mathrm{m})-(1+\mathrm{m})}{\sqrt{3}}= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\
& \Rightarrow(1+\mathrm{m})+(2-\mathrm{m})-(1+\mathrm{m})= \pm 1 \\
\therefore \quad & \mathrm{m}=3 \text { or } \mathrm{m}=1
\end{aligned}$
Substituting $\mathrm{m}=3$ in equation (i), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \overline{\mathrm{r}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}(1+3)+\hat{\mathrm{j}}(2-3)+\hat{\mathrm{k}}(1+3) \\
& \Rightarrow \overline{\mathrm{r}}=4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{k}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Given: $(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{1}{3}|\overline{\mathrm{b}}||\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^{-}$
We know that,
$(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}=(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{b}}-(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \overline{\mathrm{a}}^{-}$
On comparing, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{3}|\overline{\mathrm{b}}||\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|=-\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}} \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{3}|\overline{\mathrm{b}}||\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|=-|\overline{\mathrm{b}}||\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}| \cos \theta \\
\Rightarrow \cos \theta & =\frac{-1}{3} \\
\Rightarrow \cos ^2 \theta & =\frac{1}{9} \\
\sin ^2 \theta & =1-\cos ^2 \theta \\
& =1-\frac{1}{9} \\
\therefore \quad & \sin ^2 \theta=\frac{8}{9} \\
\therefore \quad & \sin \theta=\sqrt{\frac{8}{9}}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{3}
\end{aligned}$

Comparing
$\begin{aligned}

Also, $\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{r}}=3\begin{aligned}

questions.q: Let two non-collinear vectors $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ form an acute angle. A point $\mathrm{P}$ moves, so that at any time $t$ the position vector $\overline{\mathrm{OP}}$, where $\mathrm{O}$ is origin, is given by $\hat{a} \sin t+\hat{b} \cos t$, when $P$ is farthest from origin $\mathrm{O}$, let $\mathrm{M}$ be the length of $\overline{\mathrm{OP}}$ and $\hat{\mathrm{u}}$ be the unit vector along $\overline{\mathrm{OP}}$, then
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{M}=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{OP}}| \\

& =\sqrt{(\hat{a} \sin t)^2+(\hat{b} \cos t)^2+2(\hat{a} \sin t) \cdot(\hat{b} \cos t)} \\
& =\sqrt{\sin ^2 t+\cos ^2 t+\hat{a} \cdot \hat{b}(2 \sin t \cos t)} \\
& =\sqrt{1+\hat{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \hat{\mathrm{b}}(\sin 2 \mathrm{t})} \\

& \therefore \quad 2 \mathrm{t}=\sin ^{-1}(1) \\

& \text { Now, } \hat{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{OP}}}{|\overline{\mathrm{OP}}|} \\
& =\frac{\hat{a} \sin t+\hat{b} \cos t}{|\hat{a} \sin t+\hat{b} \cos t|} \\

&

questions.solution:
$(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}})+(\lambda \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}})=(2+\lambda) \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
Unit vector along the above vector is
$\frac{(2+\lambda) \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}}{\sqrt{(2+\lambda)^2+6^2+(-2)^2}}=\frac{(2+\lambda) \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}}{\sqrt{\lambda^2+4 \lambda+44}}$
Scalar product of $(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})$ with this unit vector is 1 .
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad & (\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \cdot \frac{(2+\lambda) \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}}{\sqrt{\lambda^2+4 \lambda+44}}=1 \\
& \frac{(2+\lambda)+6-2}{\sqrt{\lambda^2+4 \lambda+44}}=1 \\
& \sqrt{\lambda^2+4 \lambda+44}=\lambda+6 \\
\therefore \quad & \lambda^2+4 \lambda+44=(\lambda+6)^2 \\
& 8 \lambda=8 \\
& \lambda=1
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $[(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{c}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{a}})] \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{c}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}})=54$, then the value of $\left[\begin{array}{lll}\bar{a} & \bar{b} & \bar{c}\end{array}\right]$ is
questions.solution:
R.H.S. of the given equality can be written as
$\begin{aligned}
&(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}) \cdot[(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \times(3 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&=(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}) \cdot[3(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
&+6(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+4(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
&+9(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+3(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+6(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&=(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}})[0+(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
&-6(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+0+4(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
&=(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}})[-5(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})-3(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})+(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})-7(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&=-10[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})]+2[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]-14[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&-15[\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})]+3[\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]-21[\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&-5[\overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})]+[\overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]-7[\overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&= 0+2[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]+0 \\
&+0+0 \\
&=-5[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]+0+21[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}] \\
&= 18[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}} \overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]=54
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]=3$

questions.q: The volume of parallelopiped, whose coterminous edges are given by $\bar{u}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\lambda \hat{k}$, $\bar{v}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}, \bar{w}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is 1 cu. units. If $\theta$ is the angle between $\bar{u}$ and $\bar{w}$, then the value of $\cos \theta$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Volume of parallelepiped }=\left[\begin{array}{lll}\overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{w}}\end{array}\right] \\ & \quad\left|\begin{array}{lll}1 & 1 & \lambda \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right|=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda=2 \\ & \therefore \quad \cos \theta=\frac{2+1+2}{\sqrt{6} \cdot \sqrt{6}}=\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^1 \frac{8 \log (1+x)}{1+x^2} \mathrm{~d} x=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { let } x=\tan \theta \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{d} x=\sec ^2 \theta \mathrm{d} \theta \text {, when } x=0, \theta=0 \text {; when } x=1 \text {, } \\ & \theta=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 8 \frac{\log (1+\tan \theta)}{1+\tan ^2 \theta} \cdot \sec ^2 \theta d \theta=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 8 \log (1+\tan \theta) \mathrm{d} \theta \quad \ldots \ldots(\mathrm{i})\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} 8 \log \left(1+\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right) \mathrm{d} \theta\left[\because \int_0^a f(x) \mathrm{d} x=\int_0^a f(a-x) \mathrm{d} x\right]\right.$
$\left[\because \tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right)=\frac{1-\tan \theta}{1+\tan \theta}\right]$ from (i) $+($ ii $)\begin{aligned} & 2 I=\int_0^{\pi / 4} 8 \log \left\{(1+\tan \theta) \times \frac{2}{(1+\tan \theta)}\right\} d \theta \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{I}=8 \int_0^{\pi / 4} \log 2 \mathrm{~d} \theta=8 \log 2[\theta]_0^{\pi / 4}=8 \log 2 \times \frac{\pi}{4} \end{aligned}\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}=\pi \log 2$

questions.q: If the vectors $2 \hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k}$ and $\bar{b}$ are collinear and $|\bar{b}|=14$, then $\bar{b}$ has the value

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $|\bar{a}|=5,|\bar{b}|=13$ and $|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|=25$. If $\frac{\pi}{2} \lt  \theta \lt  \pi$ where $\theta$ is angle between $\bar{a}, \bar{b}$ then $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}$ has the value
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| \sin \theta \\ & \Rightarrow 25=5 \times 13 \sin \theta \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \theta=\frac{5}{13} \\ & \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{-12}{13} \quad\left[\because \frac{\pi}{2} \lt  \theta \lt  \pi\right] \\ & \text { now } \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \cos \theta=5 \times 13 \times \frac{-12}{13}=-60\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sum of the distinct real values of $\mu$, for which the vector $\mu \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \hat{i}+\mu \hat{j}+\hat{k}, \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\mu \hat{k}$ are coplanar is
questions.solution:
From the condition for co-planarity
$\begin{aligned}
& \left|\begin{array}{lll}
\mu & 1 & 1 \\
1 & \mu & 1 \\
1 & 1 & \mu
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(2+\mu)(\mu-1)^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \mu=-2 \text { or } \mu=1 \\
& \text { sum }=-2+1=-1
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\bar{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}, \bar{b}=2 \hat{i}-\hat{k}$, then point of intersection of the lines $\bar{r} \times \bar{a}=\bar{b} \times \bar{a}$ and $\bar{r} \times \bar{b}=\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ is
questions.solution: $\vec{r} \times \vec{a}=\vec{b} \times \vec{a}$ and $\vec{r} \times \vec{b}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \vec{r} \times \vec{a}=-\vec{r} \times \vec{b} \quad \text { [from (i) and (ii)] } \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{r} \times(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=\overrightarrow{0} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{r} \| \vec{a}+\vec{b} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{r}=\lambda(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=\lambda(3 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})\end{aligned}$ Taking $\lambda=1, \vec{r}=3 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\widehat{k} \equiv(3,1,-1)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the points $A(3,2,1), B(4, x, 5), C(4,2,-2)$ and $D(6,5,-1)$ are coplanar, then $x$ has the value
questions.solution:
For coplanarity
$\begin{aligned} & {\left[\begin{array}{ccc}6-3 & 5-2 & -1-1 \\ 4-3 & x-2 & 5-1 \\ 4-3 & 2-2 & -2-1\end{array}\right]=0} \\ & \Rightarrow\left[\begin{array}{ccc}3 & 3 & -2 \\ 1 & x-2 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & -3\end{array}\right]=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 3\{-3(x-2)-0\}-3\{1 \times(-3)-1 \times 4\}-2(1 \times 0-1 \times(x-2))=0 \\ & \Rightarrow-7 x+35=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x=5\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\quad \bar{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \vec{b}=-\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k} \quad$ and $\quad \bar{c}=2 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \quad$ then $(\bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot[(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times(\bar{a} \times \bar{c})]$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & (\vec{a}-\vec{b}) \cdot[(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times(\vec{a} \times \vec{c})] \\ & =(\vec{a}-\vec{b}) \cdot\{[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] \vec{a}-[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{a}] \vec{c}\} \\ & =(\vec{a}-\vec{b}) \cdot \vec{a}\{[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}]\} \\ & =(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}-\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a})[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\left\{\left(1^2+1^2+1^2\right)-(-1+2-2)\right\}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right| \\ & =4 \times\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right| \\ & =4 \times 1 \times(0-3)=-12\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\bar{a}=3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+x \hat{k}$ and $\bar{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$, for some real $x$. Then $|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|=r$ is possible, if
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 2 & x \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right|=(2+x) \hat{i}+(x-3) \hat{j}+(-3-2) \hat{k} \\ & \text { now } r=|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=\sqrt{(2+x)^2+(x-3)^2+(-5)^2} \\ & =\sqrt{2 x^2-2 x+38} \\ & =\sqrt{2\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\frac{75}{2}} \\ & \Rightarrow r_{\min }=\sqrt{\frac{75}{2}} \text { at } x=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow r \geq 5 \cdot \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A unit vector $\hat{a}$ makes angles $\frac{\pi}{3}$ with $\hat{i}, \frac{\pi}{4}$ with $\hat{j}$ and $\theta \in(\theta, \pi)$ with $\widehat{k}$, then a value of $\theta$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \alpha=\frac{\pi}{3}, \beta=\frac{\pi}{4} \text { and } \gamma=0 \\ & \because \cos ^2 \alpha+\cos ^2 \beta+\cos ^2 \gamma=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \cos ^2 \frac{\pi}{3}+\cos ^2 \frac{\pi}{4}+\cos ^2 \theta=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}+\cos ^2 \theta=1\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \cos ^2 \theta=\frac{1}{4}\Rightarrow \cos \theta= \pm \frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$ or $\frac{2 \pi}{3}$ as $\theta \in(0, \pi)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area of the parallelogram with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ as two adjacent sides is 15 sq. units, then the area of the parallelogram having $3 \vec{a}+\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a}+3 \vec{b}$ as two adjacent sides, in square units, is
questions.solution:
Area of parallelogram $=|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=15$ [given]
Area of second parallelogram $=|(3 \vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times(\vec{a}+3 \vec{b})|\begin{aligned} & =|3 \vec{a} \times \vec{a}+9 \vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{a}+3 \vec{b} \times \vec{b}| \\ & =|0+9 \vec{a} \times \vec{b}-\vec{a} \times \vec{b}+0| \\ & =|8 \vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=8|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=8 \times 15=120\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $O$ be the origin and let $P Q R$ be an arbitrary triangle. The point $S\overline{O P} \cdot \overline{O Q}+\overline{O R} \cdot \overline{O S}=\overline{O R} \cdot \overline{O P}+\overline{O Q} \cdot \overline{O S}=\overline{O Q} \overline{O Q} \cdot \overline{O R}+\overline{O P} \cdot \overline{O S}$ that $\overline{O P} \cdot \overline{O Q}+\overline{O R} \cdot \overline{O S}=\overline{O R} \cdot \overline{O P}+\overline{O Q} \cdot \overline{O S}=\overline{O Q} \cdot \overline{O R}+\overline{O P} \cdot \overline{O S}$, then the triangle $P Q R$ has $S$ as its
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{O P} \cdot \overrightarrow{O Q}+\overrightarrow{O R} \cdot \overrightarrow{O S}=\overrightarrow{O R} \cdot \overrightarrow{O P}+\overrightarrow{O Q} \cdot \overrightarrow{O S} \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{O P} \cdot(\overrightarrow{O Q}-\overrightarrow{O R})=\overrightarrow{O S} \cdot(\overrightarrow{O Q}-\overrightarrow{O R}) \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{O P} \cdot \overrightarrow{R Q}=\overrightarrow{O S} \cdot \overrightarrow{R Q} \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{R Q} \cdot(\overrightarrow{O P}-\overrightarrow{O S})=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{R Q} \cdot \overrightarrow{P S}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{P S} \perp \overrightarrow{Q R}\end{aligned}$
Similarly $\overrightarrow{Q S} \perp \overrightarrow{P R}$ and $\overrightarrow{R S} \perp \overrightarrow{P Q}$
i.e., $S$ is the orthocenter

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{3},|\vec{b}|=5, \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}=10$ and angle between $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ is $\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$. If $\vec{a}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b} \times \vec{c}$, then value of $|\vec{a} \times(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})|$ is
questions.solution: $|\vec{a} \times(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})|=|\vec{a}| \times|\vec{b} \times \vec{c}| \sin \frac{\pi}{2}$ from (i) and (ii) $|\vec{a} \times(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})|=\frac{15}{2} \times 4=30$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are unit vectors such that $\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=\overrightarrow{0}$, then the value of $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|=|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{c}|^2+2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) \\ & \Rightarrow 0=1^2+1^2+1^2+2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the vector $\bar{a}=2 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}, \bar{b}=-\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\bar{c}=3 \hat{i}+\hat{j}$ are such that $(\bar{a}+\lambda \bar{b})$ is perpendicular to $\bar{c}$, then the value of $\lambda$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because \vec{a}+\lambda \vec{b} \perp \vec{c} \\ & \Rightarrow(\vec{a}+\lambda \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow\{(2 \widehat{i}+2 \widehat{j}+3 \widehat{k})+\lambda(-\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+\hat{k})\} \cdot(3 \hat{i}+\hat{j})=0 \\ & \Rightarrow\{(2-\lambda) \hat{i}+(2+2 \lambda) \hat{j}+(3+\lambda) \widehat{k}\} \cdot(3 \hat{i}+\hat{j})=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(2-\lambda) \times 3+(2+2 \lambda) \times 1+(3+\lambda) \times 0=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda=8\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $a$, so that the volume of parallelepiped formed by $\hat{i}+a \hat{j}+\hat{k}, \hat{j}+a \hat{k}$ and $a \hat{i}+\hat{k}$ becomes minimum is
questions.solution:
Volume of parallelepiped $=\left|\begin{array}{lll}1 & a & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & a \\ a & 0 & 1\end{array}\right|=a^3-a+1=V(a)$
Now $V^{\prime}(a)=3 a^2-1\stackrel{+}{\stackrel{\max .}{1}-\min _1^1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}\Rightarrow$ volume is minimum at $x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are vectors such that $|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|=\sqrt{29}$ and $\bar{a} \times(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k})=(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}) \times \bar{b}$, then a possible value of $(\bar{a}+\bar{b}) \cdot(-7 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \vec{a} \times(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \widehat{k})=(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \widehat{k}) \times \vec{b}=-\vec{b} \times(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \widehat{k}) \\ & \Rightarrow(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \widehat{k})=\overrightarrow{0} \\ & \Rightarrow(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \| 2 \widehat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \widehat{k} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a}+\vec{b}=\lambda(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \widehat{k}) \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|=\lambda \sqrt{2^2+3^2+4^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{29}= \pm \lambda \sqrt{29} \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda= \pm 1 \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a}+\vec{b}= \pm(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \widehat{k}) \\ & \Rightarrow(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \cdot(-7 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})= \pm(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+4 \widehat{k}) \cdot(-7 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \\ & = \pm(-14+6+12) \\ & = \pm 4\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\vec{u}, \vec{v}$ and $\vec{w}$ be vectors such that $|\vec{u}+\vec{v}+\vec{w}=\overline{0}|$. If $|\vec{u}|=3$, $\overrightarrow{|v|}=4$ and $\overrightarrow{|w|}=5$, then the value of $|\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}+\vec{v} \cdot \vec{w}+\vec{w} \cdot \vec{u}|$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |\vec{u}+\vec{v}+\vec{w}|^2=|\vec{u}|^2+|\vec{v}|^2+|\vec{w}|^2+2(\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}+\vec{v} \cdot \vec{w}+\vec{w} \cdot \vec{u}) \\ & \Rightarrow 0^2=3^2+4^2+5^2+2(\vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}+\vec{v} \cdot \vec{w}+\vec{w} \cdot \vec{u}) \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{u} \cdot \vec{v}+\vec{v} \cdot \vec{w}+\vec{w} \cdot \vec{u}=-25\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For non-zero vectors $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c},|(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{c}|=|\bar{a}||\bar{b}||\bar{c}|$ holds and only if
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & |(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{c}| \\ & =|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}| \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}||\vec{c}| \cos \theta=|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}| \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \sin \phi|\vec{c}| \cos \theta=|\vec{a}||\vec{b}||\vec{c}| \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \phi=1 \text { and } \cos \theta=1 \\ & \phi=90^{\circ} \text { and } \theta=0^{\circ} \\ & \text { where } \phi \text { is the angle between } \vec{a} \text { and } \vec{b} \text { and } \theta \text { is the angle between } \vec{c} \text { and } \\ & \text { normal to the plane containing } \vec{a} \text { and } \vec{b} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \perp \vec{b}, \vec{b} \perp \vec{c} \text {, and } \vec{c} \perp \vec{a} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}=\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\overline{A B}=(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}-\hat{k})$ and $A(1,2,-1)$ is the given point, then the coordinates of $B$ are
questions.solution:
Let $B(x, y, z)$ then $\overrightarrow{A B}=(x-1) \hat{i}+(y-2) \hat{j}+(z+1) \widehat{k}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow x-1=2, y-2=3 \text { and } z+1=-1 \\
& \Rightarrow x=3, y=5 \text { and } z=-2 \\
& \Rightarrow B \equiv(3,5,-2)
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area of the triangle with vertices $\hat{i}+y \hat{j}, \hat{i}+2 \hat{k}$ and $3 \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is $\sqrt{6}$ sq. units, then the values of $y$ are
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{A B}=(\hat{i}+2 \hat{k})-(\hat{i}+y \hat{j})=0 \hat{i}-y \hat{j}+2 \widehat{k} \\ & \overrightarrow{B C}=(3 \hat{j}+\hat{k})-(\hat{i}+2 \hat{k})=-\hat{i}+3 \hat{j}-\hat{k} \\ & \text { Now area of triangle }=\frac{1}{2}|\overrightarrow{A B} \times \overrightarrow{B C}|=\sqrt{6} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 0 & -y & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -1\end{array}\right|=\sqrt{6} \\ & \Rightarrow|(y-6) \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-y \hat{k}|=2 \sqrt{6} \\ & \Rightarrow(y-6)^2+(-2)^2+(-y)^2=(2 \sqrt{6})^2 \\ & \Rightarrow y^2-12 y+36+4+y^2=24 \\ & \Rightarrow y^2-6 y+8=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y=2,4\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\bar{a}+2 \bar{b}+3 \bar{c}=\overline{0}$ and $(\bar{b} \times \bar{b})+(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})+(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})=\lambda(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})$, then $\lambda$ has the value
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow(\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}) \times(\vec{a}+2 \vec{b}+3 \vec{c})=\overrightarrow{0} \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \vec{a} \times \vec{b}+3 \vec{a} \times \vec{c}+\vec{b} \times \vec{a}+3 \vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{a}+2 \vec{c} \times \vec{b}=\overrightarrow{0} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}-2 \vec{c} \times \vec{a}=\overrightarrow{0} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{a}=3 \vec{c} \times \vec{a}=3 \vec{c} \times(-2 \vec{b}-3 \vec{c}) \quad[\text { from (1)] } \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{a}=-6 \vec{c} \times \vec{b} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \times \vec{b}+\vec{b} \times \vec{c}+\vec{c} \times \vec{a}=6 \vec{b} \times \vec{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda=6 \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The position vectors of vertices of $\triangle A B C$ are $4 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}$; $\hat{i}+4 \hat{j}-3 \hat{k}$ and $-\hat{i}+5 \hat{j}+\hat{k}$ respectively, then $m \angle A B C=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \angle A B C=\text { angle between } \overrightarrow{B A} \text { and } \overrightarrow{B C} \\ & =\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{\overrightarrow{B A} \cdot \overrightarrow{B C}}{|\overrightarrow{B A}||\overrightarrow{B C}|}\right)=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{(3 \hat{i}-6 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \cdot(-2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+4 \hat{k})}{\sqrt{3^2+(-6)^2+3^2} \sqrt{(-2)^2+1^2+4^2}}\right) \\ & =\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{6-6+12}{\sqrt{54} \sqrt{21}}\right)=\cos ^{-1}(0)=\frac{\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\bar{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \bar{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2 \hat{k}, \bar{c}=x \hat{i}+(x-2) \hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\bar{c}$ is linear combination of $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$, then $x$ has the value
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \vec{c}=\vec{b}+\lambda \vec{a} \\ & \Rightarrow x \hat{i}+(x-2) \hat{j}-\widehat{k}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2 \widehat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\widehat{k}) \\ & \Rightarrow x=1+\lambda, x-2=-1+\lambda \text { and }-1=2+\lambda \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda=-3 \text { and } x=-2\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The volume of the tetrahedron having vertices $(1,-6,10)$, $(-1,-3,7),(5,-1, \lambda)$ and $(7,-4,7)$ is $11 \mathrm{cu}$. Units, then $\lambda=$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Volume of a tetrahedron }=\frac{1}{6}\left|\begin{array}{lll}x_2-x_1 & y_2-y_1 & z_2-z_1 \\ x_3-x_1 & y_3-y_1 & z_3-z_1 \\ x_4-x_1 & y_4-y_1 & z_4-z_1\end{array}\right| \\ & =\frac{1}{6}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}-2 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & 5 & \lambda-10 \\ 6 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right| \\ & \Rightarrow 11=\frac{1}{6}\{22 \lambda-88\} \Rightarrow \lambda=7\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $|\bar{a}|=3,|\bar{b}|=5$ and $|\bar{c}|=7$ and $\bar{a}+\bar{b}+\bar{c}=\overline{0}$, then the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a}+\vec{b}=-\vec{c} \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|^2=|\vec{c}|^2 \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2+2|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \cos \theta=|\vec{c}|^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 3^2+5^2+2 \times 3 \times 5 \cos \theta=7^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\frac{15}{30}=\frac{1}{2}=\cos \frac{\pi}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $|\bar{a}|=\sqrt{26},|\bar{b}|=7$ and $|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|=35$, then $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & |\vec{a}|=\sqrt{26},|\vec{b}|=7,|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|=|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \sin \theta=35 \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{26} \times 7 \sin \theta=35 \\ & \Rightarrow \sin \theta=\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}} \\ & \Rightarrow \cos \theta= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{26}}\end{aligned}$
Now $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=|\vec{a}||\vec{b}| \cos \theta=\sqrt{26} \times 7 \times \frac{ \pm 1}{\sqrt{26}}= \pm 7$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \vec{a}+\vec{b}=\lambda \vec{c} \quad \ldots(i) \text { and } \vec{b}+\vec{c}=\mu \vec{a} \quad \ldots(i i) \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a}-\vec{c}=\lambda \vec{c}-\mu \vec{a} \quad \text { form (i) and (ii) } \\ & \Rightarrow(1+\mu) \vec{a}=(1+\lambda) \vec{c} \\ & \Rightarrow \mu=\lambda=-1 \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}|^2=|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{c}|^2+2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) \\ & \Rightarrow 0=2+2+2+2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}+\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=-3\end{aligned}$

$\vec{r}=t \vec{a}+u \vec{b}$ [as vector lies in the plane of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ where $t$ and $u$ are scalars]
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \vec{r}=t(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})+u(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \\ & =(t+u) \hat{i}+(t-u) \hat{j}+(t+u) \hat{k} \ldots(i) \\ & \frac{\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c}}{|\vec{c}|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \frac{(t+u)-(t-u)-(t+u)}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & \Rightarrow-(t-u)=1 \Rightarrow u=t+1 \ldots \ldots . .(i i)\end{aligned}$
from (i) and (ii)
$\vec{r}=(2 t+1) \hat{i}-\hat{j}+(2 t+1) \widehat{k}$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \vec{b} \times \vec{c}=\vec{b} \times \vec{a} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{b} \times \vec{c}-\vec{b} \times \vec{a}=\overrightarrow{0} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{b} \times(\vec{c}-\vec{a})=\overrightarrow{0} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{c}-\vec{a} \| \vec{b} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{c}-\vec{a}=\lambda \vec{b} \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{c}=\vec{a}+\lambda \vec{b} \\ & \because \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}=0 \Rightarrow(\vec{a}+\lambda \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{a}=0 \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\lambda \vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 11^2+(-2)^2+1^2+\lambda(1 \times 1+(-2) \times(-1)+1 \times 1) \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda=-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Now } \vec{c} \cdot \vec{b}=(\vec{a}+\lambda \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{b} \\ & =\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}+\lambda \vec{b} \cdot \vec{b} \\ & =4-\frac{3}{2} \times 3=4-\frac{9}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

Here, $\vec{p}=\vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right|=2 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+\widehat{k} \Rightarrow|\vec{p}|=3$

$\begin{aligned}

& =(\bar{a}+\bar{b}) \cdot[(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})+(\bar{b} \times \bar{a})+(\bar{c} \times \bar{c})+(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})] \\

& =[\bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})]+0+0+0+0+0+0+[\bar{b} \cdot(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})] \\
& =2 \bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})
\end{aligned}$

Also }|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=3 \\ & \overline{\mathrm{c}}-\overline{\mathrm{a}}=2 \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{c}}-\overline{\mathrm{a}})^2=8 \\ & \therefore \quad \overline{\mathrm{c}}-\overline{\mathrm{a}}=2 \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow(\overline{\mathrm{c}}-\overline{\mathrm{a}})^2=8 \\ & \therefore \quad|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^2+|\overline{\mathrm{a}}|^2=2 \overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{a}}=8 \\ & \therefore \quad|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^2+9-2|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|=8 \\ & \therefore \quad|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|^2-2|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|+1=0 \Rightarrow(|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|-1)^2=0 \Rightarrow|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|=1 \\ & |(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}|=|\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}| \cdot|\overline{\mathrm{c}}| \cdot \sin 60^{\circ}=(3)(1)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
\begin{aligned}
& \vec{a}=x \vec{b}+y \vec{c} \\
& \therefore 4 \hat{i}+13 \hat{j}-18 \hat{k}=(\hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})(x)+(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}-4 \hat{k})(y) \\
& =(x+2 y) \hat{i}+(-2 x+3 y) \hat{j}+(3 x-4 y) \hat{k} \\
& \therefore x+2 y=4,-2 x+3 y=13 \text { and } 3 x-4 y=-18

Solving, we get $x=-2, y=3 \Rightarrow x+y=1$

questions.solution:
Let $\vec{b}=x \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k}$ and we have $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=1$
\begin{aligned}
& \therefore(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})(x \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k})=1 \Rightarrow x+y+z=1 \\
& \vec{a} \times \vec{b}=\vec{c} \Rightarrow\left|\begin{array}{lll}
\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\
1 & 1 & 1 \\
x & y & z
\end{array}\right|=\hat{j}-\hat{k} \\
& \therefore(z-y) \hat{i}-(z-x) \hat{j}+(y-x) \hat{k}=\hat{j}-\hat{k} \\
& \therefore z-y=0, x-z=1, y-x=-1 \\
& \therefore y=z, z=x-1, y=x-1 \\
& \text { Thus } \vec{b}=x \hat{i}+(x-1) \hat{j}+(x-1) \hat{k} \\
& \therefore x+(x-1)+(x-1)=1 \\
& \Rightarrow x=1, y=0, z=0 \\
& \therefore \vec{b}=\hat{i}
\end{aligned}

questions.solution:
Let $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}_1}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}_2}=-\hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}\therefore\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}_1}\right|=\sqrt{14}$ and $\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}_2}\right|=\sqrt{19}$
\begin{aligned}
& \text { Also } \overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}_1} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}_2}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{\mathrm{i}} & \hat{\mathrm{j}} & \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\
3 & -1 & -2 \\
-1 & 3 & -3
\end{array}\right|=9 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+11 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+8 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\
& \therefore\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}_1} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{d}_2}\right|=\sqrt{81+121+64}=\sqrt{266} \\
& \left|\mathrm{~d}_1 \times \mathrm{d}_2\right|^2=\left|\mathrm{d}_1\right|^2\left|\mathrm{~d}_2\right|^2 \sin ^2 \theta \\
& \therefore 266=(14)(19) \sin ^2 \theta \\
& \therefore \sin ^2 \theta=1 \quad \Rightarrow \sin \theta=1 \quad \ldots\left[\because 0 < \theta \leq \frac{\pi}{2}\right]
\end{aligned}

Area of parallelogram $=\frac{1}{2}\left|\mathrm{~d}_1\right|\left|\mathrm{d}_2\right| \sin \theta$
=\frac{\sqrt{266}}{2}

& +4 \overline{\mathrm{b}}(0)+4 \overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+8 \overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}}) \\
& =\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})+0+0+0+0+0+0+8 \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
& =9[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]=9(4)=36
\end{aligned}

& |(3 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}})| \\
& (3 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \\
& =6(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+9(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+3(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \\
& =0+9(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})-2(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+0=7(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})
\end{aligned}

Hence area of the required parallelogram $=7 \times 20=140$

questions.q: If $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]=3$, then the volume of the parallelopiped with $2 \bar{a}+\bar{b}, 2 \bar{b}+\bar{c}, 2 \bar{c}+\bar{a}$ as coterminus edges is
questions.solution:
Volume of parallelepiped

\begin{array}{l}
=(2 \bar{a}+\bar{b}) \cdot[(2 \bar{b}+\bar{c}) \times(2 \bar{c}+\bar{a})] \\
=(2 \bar{a}+\bar{b}) \cdot[(4 \bar{b} \times \bar{c})+(2 \bar{b} \times \bar{a})+(2 \bar{c} \times \bar{c})+(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})] \\
=[8 \bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})]+[4 \bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{a})]+[2 \bar{a} \cdot(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})]+[4 \bar{b} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})]+[2 \bar{b} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{a})]+[\bar{b} \cdot(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})] \\
=[8 \bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})]+0+[\bar{b} \cdot(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})] \\
=8[\bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})]+[\bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})]=9 \bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) \\
=9[\bar{a} \quad \bar{b} \quad \bar{c}]=9(3)=27
\end{array}

questions.q:
If $\bar{a}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(3 \hat{\imath}+\hat{k}), \overline{\mathrm{b}}=\frac{1}{7}(2 \hat{\imath}+3 \hat{\jmath}-6 \hat{k})$, then the value of
$(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot[(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b})]$ is
questions.solution:
Given vectors $\bar{a} \& \bar{b}$ are unit vectors.
$\begin{array}{l}
\text { Now }(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot[(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b})] \\
\quad=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot[(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b}) \times(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})] \\
\quad=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot[\bar{a} \times(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})+2 \bar{b} \times(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})] \\
\quad=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b})[(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{a}-(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a}) \cdot \bar{b}+2(\bar{b} \cdot \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{a}-2(\bar{b} \cdot \bar{a}) \cdot \bar{b}] \\
\quad=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b})[(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) \bar{a}-\bar{b}+2 \bar{a}-2(\bar{b} \cdot \bar{a}) \bar{b}] \\
\text { Here } \quad \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}=\frac{3(2)}{7 \sqrt{10}}-\frac{1(6)}{7 \sqrt{10}}=0
\end{array}
Hence given expression becomes
$\begin{array}{l}
=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b})[-\bar{b}+2 \bar{a}]=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b})^{2} \\
=-\left[4 \bar{a}^{2}+\bar{b}^{2}-4 \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}\right]=-(4+1)=-5
\end{array}

Given $\bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})=4\therefore$ Volume of parallelopiped
$\begin{array}{l}
=(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \cdot[(\overline{\mathrm{b}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \times(\overline{\mathrm{c}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{a}})] \\
=(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \cdot[(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})+4(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})] \\
=[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]+[2 \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})]+[4 \overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})]+ \\
=[2 \overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]+[4 \overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})]+[8 \overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})] \\
=[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]+0+[8 \overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})] \\
=9[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]=9(4)=36
\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
The vector perpendicular to the vectors $4 \mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+3 \mathbf{k}$ and $-2 \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}-2 \mathbf{k}$ whose magnitude
is 9
questions.solution:
Let $\mathbf{a}=4 \mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+3 \mathbf{k}, \mathbf{b}=-2 \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}-2 \mathbf{k}$
and $\quad \mathbf{c}=x \mathbf{i}+y \mathbf{j}+z \mathbf{k}$
Given, $\quad$ a $\cdot \mathbf{c}=0$
i.e., $\quad 4 x-y+3 z=0$...(i)
and $\quad$ b. $\mathbf{c}=0$
i.e., $-2 x+y-2 z=0$...(ii)
Also, $|\mathbf{c}|=9$
i.e., $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=81$...(iii)
Now, from Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

2 x+z=0 \Rightarrow z=-2 x

On putting this value in Eq. (iii), we get

\begin{aligned}
x^{2}+y^{2}+4 x^{2} &=81 \\
\Rightarrow \quad 5 x^{2}+y^{2} &=81...(iv)
\end{aligned}

On multiplying Eq. (i) by 2 and Eq. (ii) by 3 and then adding, we get

\begin{array}{r}
8 x-2 y+6 z=0 \\
\frac{-6 x+3 y-6 z=0}{2 x+y=0} \\
\Rightarrow \quad y=-2 x
\end{array}

On putting this value in Eq. (iv), we get

5 x^{2}+4 x^{2}=81

\begin{array}{lcc}
\Rightarrow & 9 x^{2}=81 \\
\Rightarrow & x^{2}=9 \\
\Rightarrow & x=\pm 3 \\
\therefore & y=\mp 6 & \text { and } z=\mp 6
\end{array}

$\therefore$ Required vector, $\mathbf{c}=x \mathbf{i}+y \mathbf{j}+z \mathbf{k}$
\begin{array}{l}
=\pm 3 \mathbf{i} \mp 6 \mathbf{j} \mp 6 \mathbf{k} \\
=3 \mathbf{i}-6 \mathbf{j}-6 \mathbf{k}
\end{array}

or

=-3 \mathbf{i}+6 \mathbf{j}+6 \mathbf{k}

questions.q:
The line joining the points $6 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}+4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}},-4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}$ and the line joining the
points $-\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-5 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}$ intersect
at
questions.solution:
The equations of the lines joining $6 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}+4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}},-4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}} \quad$ and
$-\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-5 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}$ are respectively

\overrightarrow{\mathbf{r}}=6 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}+4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}+m(-6 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-8 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}) ...(i)

and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{r}}=-\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}+n(2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}})$ ...(ii)
For the point of intersection, the Eqs. (i) and
(ii) should give the same value of $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{r}}$. Hence equating the coefficients of vectors $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}$ in the two expressions for $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{r}}$, we get

\begin{array}{l}
6 m+2 n=7 \\
2 m-2 n=1
\end{array}

and

8 m-2 n=7

On solving Eqs. (iii) and (iv), we get $m=1, n=\frac{1}{2} .$ These values of $m$ and $n$, also satisfy the Eq. (v).
$\therefore$ The lines intersect. Putting the value of $m$ in Eq. (i), we get the position vector of the point of intersection as $-4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}$.

questions.q: $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times[\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}})]$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times[\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}&\times(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}})] \\ &=\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times\{(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}) \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}) \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}\} \\ &=(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}})(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}})-(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}})(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}) \\ &=(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}) 0+(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}})(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}) \\ &=(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}})(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}) \end{aligned}$

If the vectors $\hat{\mathbf{i}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}},-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}$ represents
the diagonals of a parallelogram, then its area will be
questions.solution:
Let 
$\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}=-\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}$
Now, $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}=\left|\begin{array}{rrr}\hat{\mathbf{i}} & \hat{\mathbf{j}} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right|=-4 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-\hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Hence, required area $=\frac{1}{2}|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}|=\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{16+4+1}=\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}|=2,|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}|=3$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}$ are mutually
perpendicular, then the area of the triangle whose vertices are $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{0}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}$ is
questions.solution:
Let the position vectors of the points $A, B, C$ are

\begin{array}{l}
\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}, \mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b} \text { and } \theta=90^{\circ} . \\
\therefore \text { Area of triangle }=\frac{1}{2}|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{A B}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{A C}}| \\
\left.\quad=\frac{1}{2} \mid \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}\right) \times(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}) \mid \\
=\frac{1}{2}|2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}| \\
=|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}||\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}| \sin \theta \\
=3 \times 2 \sin 90^{\circ} \\
=6
\end{array}

questions.q:
If the vectors $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+\lambda \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}},-2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}$
and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}+5 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}$ are coplanar, then the value of $\lambda$ is
questions.solution:
Since, the given three vectors are coplanar, therefore one of them should be expressible as a linear combination of the remaining two ie, there exist two scalars $x$ and $y$ such that

\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+\lambda \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}+3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}=x(-2 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}+3&\overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}-4 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}) \\
+& y(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}-3 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}+5 \overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}})
\end{aligned}

On comparing the coefficient of $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{b}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{c}}$ on both sides, we get

-2 x+y=1 ; 3 x-3 y=\lambda

and $-4 x+5 y=3$
On solving first and third equations, we get

x=-\frac{1}{3}, y=\frac{1}{3}

Since, the vectors are coplanar, therefore these values of $x$ and $y$, also satisfy the second equation ie, $-1-1=\lambda$
\therefore \quad \lambda=-2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A current of 4 A is flowing at 230 V in the primary coil of a transformer. If the voltage produced in the secondary coil is 2300 V and 40 % of power is lost, then the current in the secondary will be
questions.solution:
Power in primary coil, $P_p = V_p I_p$

$P_p = 230 \times 4 = 920$ W

Since $40\%$ of power is lost, the efficiency of the transformer is $\eta = 60\%$.

Power in secondary coil, $P_s = \eta P_p$

$P_s = 0.60 \times 920 = 552$ W

Using $P_s = V_s I_s$

$552 = 2300 \times I_s$

$I_s = \dfrac{552}{2300} = 0.24$ A

Answer: $0.24$ A

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a L-R circuit of 4 mH inductance and $3\ \Omega$ resistance, e.m.f. $E = \cos(1000t)$ V is applied. The amplitude of current is
questions.solution:
Given $L = 4 \times 10^{-3}$ H, $R = 3\ \Omega$, and $E = \cos(1000t)$ V.

The peak voltage is $E_0 = 1$ V and the angular frequency is $\omega = 1000$ rad/s.

The inductive reactance is $X_L = \omega L = 1000 \times 4 \times 10^{-3} = 4\ \Omega$.

The impedance of the L-R circuit is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\ \Omega$.

The amplitude of the current is $I_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{Z} = \dfrac{1}{5} = 0.2$ A.

Answer: $0.2$ A

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Given below are the two circuits, choose the correct option.
options: At resonance, current in (B) is less than that in (A)
The r.m.s. current in (B) can be larger than that in (A)
The r.m.s. current in (A) is always equal to that in (B)
The r.m.s. current in (B) can never be larger than that in (A)
questions.solution:
For circuit (A), the impedance is purely resistive:

$Z_A = R = 30\ \Omega$

The r.m.s. current in circuit (A) is:

$I_A = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z_A} = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{R}$

For circuit (B), which is a series LCR circuit, the impedance is given by:

$Z_B = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$

Since the square of any real number is non-negative, $(X_L - X_C)^2 \ge 0$. Therefore, the impedance of circuit (B) will always be greater than or equal to the resistance $R$:

$Z_B \ge R$

$Z_B \ge Z_A$

The r.m.s. current in circuit (B) is:

$I_B = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z_B}$

Since $V_{rms}$ is the same for both circuits ($210\text{ V}$) and $Z_B \ge Z_A$, it follows that:

$I_B \le I_A$

At resonance, $X_L = X_C$, which gives $Z_B = R$ and $I_B = I_A$. For all other conditions, $Z_B \gt R$ and $I_B \lt I_A$.

Thus, the r.m.s. current in (B) can never be larger than that in (A).

Answer: The r.m.s. current in (B) can never be larger than that in (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an LCR series circuit an alternating voltage source of frequency $F$ is connected. The current leads the voltage by $45^\circ$. The value of $L$ is
questions.solution:
In an LCR series circuit, the phase difference $\phi$ between the voltage and current when the current leads the voltage is given by $\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_C - X_L}{R}$.

Given that the current leads the voltage by $45^\circ$, we have $\phi = 45^\circ$.

$\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{X_C - X_L}{R}$

$1 = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2\pi FC} - 2\pi FL}{R}$

$R = \dfrac{1}{2\pi FC} - 2\pi FL$

$2\pi FL = \dfrac{1}{2\pi FC} - R$

$2\pi FL = \dfrac{1 - 2\pi FCR}{2\pi FC}$

$L = \dfrac{1 - 2\pi FCR}{4\pi^2 F^2C}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1 - 2\pi FCR}{4\pi^2 F^2C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the circuit shown charge q varies with time t as $q = t^2 - 5$, where q is in coulomb and t is in second. At time $t = 3$ second, voltage $V_{AB}$ in volt will be
questions.solution:
Given charge on the capacitor, $q = t^2 - 5$.

The current $i$ in the circuit is the rate of flow of charge:
$i = \dfrac{dq}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(t^2 - 5) = 2t$

The rate of change of current is:
$\dfrac{di}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(2t) = 2 \text{ A/s}$

At time $t = 3 \text{ s}$:
Charge, $q = (3)^2 - 5 = 4 \text{ C}$
Current, $i = 2(3) = 6 \text{ A}$
Rate of change of current, $\dfrac{di}{dt} = 2 \text{ A/s}$

Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law from point A to point B:
$V_A - V_C - V_L - V_R = V_B$
$V_A - \dfrac{q}{C} - L\dfrac{di}{dt} - iR = V_B$
$V_A - V_B = \dfrac{q}{C} + L\dfrac{di}{dt} + iR$

Substituting the given values ($C = 4 \text{ F}$, $L = 0.5 \text{ H}$, $R = 2 \ \Omega$):
$V_{AB} = \dfrac{4}{4} + 0.5(2) + 6(2)$
$V_{AB} = 1 + 1 + 12 = 14 \text{ V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When an inductance '$L$' and resistor '$R$' are connected in series to $25$V, $50$ Hz supply, a current of $0.5$ A flows in the circuit. The current lags behind in phase from applied voltage by $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ radian. The value of R is $\left(\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$
questions.solution:
The impedance of the LR series circuit is given by:

$Z = \dfrac{V}{I}$

Substituting the given values:

$Z = \dfrac{25}{0.5} = 50 \, \Omega$

The power factor of the circuit is related to the resistance and impedance by:

$\cos \phi = \dfrac{R}{Z}$

Given that the current lags the voltage by $\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ radian ($60^\circ$):

$R = Z \cos \phi$

$R = 50 \times \cos 60^\circ$

$R = 50 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 25 \, \Omega$

Answer: $25\,\Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which graph shows the correct variation of r.m.s. current '$i$' with frequency '$f$' of a.c. in case of series resonant circuit ?
questions.solution:
In a series LCR circuit, the impedance is given by:

$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(X_L - X_C\right)^2} = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(2\pi f L - \dfrac{1}{2\pi f C}\right)^2}$

The r.m.s. current is:

$i = \dfrac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z}$

At the resonant frequency $f_r = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance ($X_L = X_C$). At this point, the impedance $Z$ is minimum ($Z = R$) and the current $i$ is maximum.

For frequencies $f \lt f_r$, $Z$ is large and $i$ is small. As $f$ increases towards $f_r$, $Z$ decreases and $i$ increases.
For frequencies $f \gt f_r$, $Z$ increases again and $i$ decreases.

Thus, the graph of current $i$ versus frequency $f$ is a bell-shaped curve with a peak at the resonant frequency. Graph (P) correctly represents this variation.

Answer: $(P)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a series LCR circuit, the voltage across R is $100$ V, $R = 1\,\text{K}\,\Omega$ and $C = 2\,\mu\text{F}$. The angular frequency $\omega$ is $200$ rad s$^{-1}$. At resonance, the voltage across '$L$' is
questions.solution:
The current in the series LCR circuit is given by $I = \dfrac{V_R}{R}$.

Substituting the given values:

$I = \dfrac{100}{1000} = 0.1$ A

The capacitive reactance is $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$.

$X_C = \dfrac{1}{200 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{10^6}{400} = 2500 \, \Omega$

The voltage across the capacitor is $V_C = I X_C$.

$V_C = 0.1 \times 2500 = 250$ V

At resonance, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance ($X_L = X_C$), so the voltage across the inductor equals the voltage across the capacitor.

$V_L = V_C = 250$ V

Answer: $250$ V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In series LCR circuit $R = 10\,\Omega$ and impedance is $30\,\Omega$. An r.m.s. voltage $210$ V, is applied across the circuit. The true power consumed in AC circuit is
questions.solution:
Given $R = 10 \, \Omega$, $Z = 30 \, \Omega$, and $V_{\text{rms}} = 210$ V.

The rms current in the circuit is given by:

$I_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z} = \dfrac{210}{30} = 7$ A

The true power consumed in the AC circuit is:

$P = I_{\text{rms}}^2 R$

Substituting the values:

$P = (7)^2 \times 10 = 49 \times 10 = 490$ W

Answer: $490$ W

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a.c. source is connected across a pure capacitor, the correct phase relation between current and emf is shown in figure.
questions.solution:
In an AC circuit containing a pure capacitor, the alternating current leads the alternating emf by a phase angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ or $90^{\circ}$.

Mathematically, if the emf is given by $e_c = E_0 \sin(\omega t)$, the current is given by $I_c = I_0 \sin\left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

In a phasor diagram, the phasor representing the current $I_c$ must be rotated counterclockwise by $90^{\circ}$ relative to the phasor representing the emf $e_c$.

Analyzing the given figures:
(A) $I_c$ and $e_c$ are in phase (represents a pure resistor).
(B) $I_c$ leads $e_c$ by $90^{\circ}$ (represents a pure capacitor).
(C) $I_c$ lags $e_c$ by $90^{\circ}$ (represents a pure inductor).
(D) $I_c$ and $e_c$ are out of phase by $180^{\circ}$.

Therefore, figure (B) correctly shows the phase relation for a pure capacitor.

Answer: (B)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In an LCR circuit at resonance, the a.c. source current is
A) maximum in a series LCR circuit only.
B) maximum in a parallel LCR circuit only.
C) maximum in both series and parallel LCR circuits.
D) minimum in both series and parallel LCR circuits.
The correct answer is
questions.solution:
In a series LCR circuit, the impedance is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

At resonance, $X_L = X_C$, which makes the impedance minimum ($Z = R$).

Since $I = \dfrac{V}{Z}$, the current is maximum in a series LCR circuit at resonance.

In a parallel LCR circuit, the admittance is given by $Y = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{R}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{X_C} - \dfrac{1}{X_L}\right)^2}$.

At resonance, $X_L = X_C$, which makes the admittance minimum ($Y = \dfrac{1}{R}$) and the impedance maximum.

Since $I = V Y$, the current is minimum in a parallel LCR circuit at resonance.

Thus, the a.c. source current is maximum in a series LCR circuit only.

Answer: A

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An alternating voltage $e = 150\sqrt{2}\sin 100t$ volt is applied to a capacitor of capacity $2\ \mu\text{F}$. The root mean square value of current in the circuit is
questions.solution:
Given alternating voltage $e = 150\sqrt{2}\sin(100t)$ V.

Comparing with the standard equation $e = E_0\sin(\omega t)$, we get:

Peak voltage $E_0 = 150\sqrt{2}$ V

Angular frequency $\omega = 100$ rad/s

The root mean square voltage is:

$E_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{150\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 150$ V

The capacitive reactance is:

$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{100 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}} = 5000\ \Omega$

The root mean square current in the circuit is:

$I_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{E_{\text{rms}}}{X_C} = \dfrac{150}{5000} = 0.03$ A

$I_{\text{rms}} = 30$ mA

Answer: $30$ mA

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a series LCR circuit inductive reactance $X_L$ is equal to resistance $R$ and also equal to twice the capacitive reactance $X_C$. The impedance of the circuit and the phase difference between voltage V and current i are respectively
questions.solution:
Given $X_L = R$ and $X_L = 2X_C$.

This gives $X_C = \dfrac{R}{2}$.

The impedance of the series LCR circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

Substituting the values:

$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(R - \dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2} = \sqrt{R^2 + \dfrac{R^2}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}R}{2}$.

The phase difference $\phi$ between voltage and current is given by $\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_L - X_C}{R}$.

$\tan \phi = \dfrac{R - \dfrac{R}{2}}{R} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

$\phi = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}R}{2},\ \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an LCR series circuit, the potential difference across the terminals of the inductor, capacitor and resistor is 60 V, 30 V and 40 V respectively. Then supply voltage will be equal to
questions.solution:
Given:

$V_L = 60$ V

$V_C = 30$ V

$V_R = 40$ V

The supply voltage $V$ in an LCR series circuit is given by the phasor sum of the voltages:

$V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$V = \sqrt{40^2 + (60 - 30)^2}$

$V = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2}$

$V = \sqrt{1600 + 900}$

$V = \sqrt{2500} = 50$ V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the series LCR circuit shown in figure the impedance is
questions.solution:
Given parameters from the circuit:
Resistance, $R = 300\ \Omega$
Inductance, $L = 1\text{ H}$
Capacitance, $C = 20\ \mu\text{F} = 20 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}$
Frequency of the AC source, $f = \dfrac{50}{\pi}\text{ Hz}$

The angular frequency $\omega$ is given by:
$\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \left(\dfrac{50}{\pi}\right) = 100\text{ rad/s}$

Inductive reactance, $X_L$:
$X_L = \omega L = 100 \times 1 = 100\ \Omega$

Capacitive reactance, $X_C$:
$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{100 \times 20 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{1}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = 500\ \Omega$

The impedance $Z$ of the series LCR circuit is:
$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2}$

Substituting the values:
$Z = \sqrt{300^2 + (500 - 100)^2}$
$Z = \sqrt{300^2 + 400^2}$
$Z = \sqrt{90000 + 160000}$
$Z = \sqrt{250000} = 500\ \Omega$

Answer: $500\,\Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A series combination of resistor 'R' and capacitor 'C' is connected to an a.c. source of angular frequency '$\omega$'. Keeping the voltage same, if the frequency is changed to $\left(\dfrac{\omega}{3}\right)$ the current becomes half of the original current. Then the ratio of capacitive reactance and resistance is
questions.solution:
Initial current $I_1 = \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2}}$ where $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$

When frequency is changed to $\dfrac{\omega}{3}$, the new capacitive reactance becomes $X_C' = \dfrac{1}{(\omega/3)C} = 3X_C$

New current $I_2 = \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + (3X_C)^2}} = \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + 9X_C^2}}$

Given $I_2 = \dfrac{I_1}{2}$

$\dfrac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + 9X_C^2}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2}}$

Squaring both sides:

$R^2 + 9X_C^2 = 4(R^2 + X_C^2)$

$R^2 + 9X_C^2 = 4R^2 + 4X_C^2$

$5X_C^2 = 3R^2$

$\dfrac{X_C^2}{R^2} = \dfrac{3}{5} = 0.6$

$\dfrac{X_C}{R} = \sqrt{0.6}$

Answer: $\sqrt{0.6}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In an a.c. circuit, a resistance R is connected in series with an inductance 'L'. If phase angle between voltage and current is $45^\circ$, the value of inductive reactance will be
($\sin 45^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \cos 45^\circ$)
questions.solution:
In a series RL circuit, the phase angle $\phi$ between the voltage and the current is given by the relation:

$\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_L}{R}$

Given that the phase angle $\phi = 45^\circ$:

$\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{X_L}{R}$

Since $\tan 45^\circ = 1$:

$1 = \dfrac{X_L}{R}$

$X_L = R$

The inductive reactance is equal to the resistance $R$.

Answer: $R$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An a.c. source is applied to a series LR circuit with $X_L = 3R$ and power factor is $X_1$. Now a capacitor with $X_c = R$ is added in series to LR circuit and power factor is $X_2$. The ratio $X_1$ to $X_2$ is
questions.solution:
For the series LR circuit, the impedance is $Z_1 = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$.

Given $X_L = 3R$, $Z_1 = \sqrt{R^2 + (3R)^2} = \sqrt{10}R$.

The power factor $X_1 = \dfrac{R}{Z_1} = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{10}R} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}$.

When a capacitor with $X_C = R$ is added in series, the new impedance is $Z_2 = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

Substituting the values, $Z_2 = \sqrt{R^2 + (3R - R)^2} = \sqrt{R^2 + 4R^2} = \sqrt{5}R$.

The new power factor $X_2 = \dfrac{R}{Z_2} = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{5}R} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$.

The ratio $\dfrac{X_1}{X_2} = \dfrac{1/\sqrt{10}}{1/\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{10}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Thus, $X_1 : X_2 = 1 : \sqrt{2}$.

Answer: $1 : \sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a series LCR circuit alternating e.m.f. and current are given by the equations $V = V_0\sin(\omega t)$ and $I = I_0\sin\left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ respectively. The average power dissipated in the circuit over one cycle of a.c. is $(\cos 60^\circ = 0.5)$
questions.solution:
The given equations for alternating e.m.f. and current are:

$V = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$

$I = I_0 \sin\left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

The phase difference between the voltage and current is $\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{3} = 60^\circ$.

The average power dissipated in an a.c. circuit over one cycle is given by:

$P_{avg} = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos \phi$

Substituting $V_{rms} = \dfrac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $I_{rms} = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$:

$P_{avg} = \left(\dfrac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \left(\dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \cos 60^\circ$

Since $\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$:

$P_{avg} = \dfrac{V_0 I_0}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{V_0 I_0}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{V_0 I_0}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an a.c. circuit with pure capacitance 'C' and a.c. source $E = E_0\sin\omega t$, the equation of instantaneous current is given by
questions.solution:
The instantaneous voltage across the capacitor is given by $E = E_0\sin\omega t$.

The charge on the capacitor at any instant is $q = CE = CE_0\sin\omega t$.

The instantaneous current $I$ is the rate of flow of charge, given by $I = \dfrac{dq}{dt}$.

Differentiating $q$ with respect to $t$, we get:

$I = \dfrac{d}{dt}(CE_0\sin\omega t) = E_0\omega C\cos\omega t$

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos\theta = \sin\left(\theta + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, the current can be written as:

$I = E_0\omega C\sin\left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Answer: $I = E_0\omega C\sin\left(\omega t + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In LCR circuit, at a particular angular frequency the capacitive reactance and inductive reactance is same. If the angular frequency is doubled, the ratio of the reactance of the capacitor to that of the inductor will be
questions.solution:
Let the initial angular frequency be $\omega_0$.

At $\omega_0$, the capacitive reactance $X_C$ and inductive reactance $X_L$ are equal:

$X_C = X_L \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\omega_0 C} = \omega_0 L$

When the angular frequency is doubled, the new angular frequency is $\omega = 2\omega_0$.

The new capacitive reactance is:

$X_C' = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{2\omega_0 C} = \dfrac{X_C}{2}$

The new inductive reactance is:

$X_L' = \omega L = 2\omega_0 L = 2X_L$

The ratio of the new capacitive reactance to the new inductive reactance is:

$\dfrac{X_C'}{X_L'} = \dfrac{\dfrac{X_C}{2}}{2X_L} = \dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{X_C}{X_L}\right)$

Since $X_C = X_L$, the ratio becomes $\dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer has 120 turns in the primary coil and carries 5A current. Input power is one kilowatt. To have 560 V output, the number of turns in secondary coil will be
questions.solution:
Input power is given by $P_{in} = V_p I_p$

$1000 = V_p \times 5$

$V_p = 200$ V

Using the transformer ratio formula:

$\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$

$\dfrac{560}{200} = \dfrac{N_s}{120}$

$N_s = \dfrac{560 \times 120}{200}$

$N_s = 336$

Answer: $336$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In LCR series circuit at resonance
options: the current leads the voltage by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
the current and voltage are in phase.
questions.solution:
In an LCR series circuit, the impedance is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

At resonance, the inductive reactance is equal to the capacitive reactance, i.e., $X_L = X_C$.

Substituting this in the impedance formula, we get $Z = R$. This is the minimum possible impedance, which results in maximum current.

The phase difference $\phi$ between the voltage and current is given by $\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_L - X_C}{R}$.

Since $X_L = X_C$, $\tan \phi = 0 \Rightarrow \phi = 0$.

Thus, the current and voltage are in phase.

Answer: the current and voltage are in phase.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The LC series resonant circuit produces a resonant frequency '$f$'. If L is tripled and 'C' is increased by 3C, the resonant frequency will be
questions.solution:
The resonant frequency of an LC series circuit is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$.

Given that the inductance $L$ is tripled, the new inductance is $L' = 3L$.

The capacitance $C$ is increased by $3C$, so the new capacitance is $C' = C + 3C = 4C$.

The new resonant frequency $f'$ is given by:

$f' = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{L'C'}}$

Substituting the values of $L'$ and $C'$:

$f' = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{(3L)(4C)}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{12LC}}$

$f' = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}} \left( \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} \right)$

$f' = \dfrac{f}{2\sqrt{3}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{f}{2\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The resistor '$R$' inductance '$L$' and capacitance '$C$' are connected in series with an a.c. source. When 'L' is removed from the circuit, the phase difference between voltage and current in the circuit is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. If instead, C is removed from the circuit, the phase difference is again $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. The power factor of the circuit is
questions.solution:
When $L$ is removed, the circuit becomes an $RC$ circuit. The phase difference is $\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

$\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_C}{R} \Rightarrow \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{X_C}{R} \Rightarrow X_C = R\sqrt{3}$

When $C$ is removed, the circuit becomes an $RL$ circuit. The phase difference is again $\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

$\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_L}{R} \Rightarrow \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{X_L}{R} \Rightarrow X_L = R\sqrt{3}$

In the series $RLC$ circuit, the net reactance is $X = X_L - X_C$.

Since $X_L = X_C = R\sqrt{3}$, we have $X = 0$.

The impedance of the circuit is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = R$.

The power factor of the circuit is $\cos \phi = \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{R}{R} = 1$.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inductor of inductance $2\ \mu\text{H}$ is connected in series with a resistance, a variable capacitor and an a.c. source of 10 kHz. The value of capacitance for which maximum current is drawn in to the circuit is $\dfrac{1}{x}\ \text{F}$, where the value of x is (Take $\pi^2 = 10$)
questions.solution:
Maximum current is drawn in a series LCR circuit at resonance.

At resonance, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance, so $\omega L = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$.

$C = \dfrac{1}{\omega^2 L} = \dfrac{1}{(2\pi f)^2 L}$

Given $L = 2\ \mu\text{H} = 2 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{H}$ and $f = 10\ \text{kHz} = 10^4\ \text{Hz}$.

$C = \dfrac{1}{4\pi^2 f^2 L}$

Substituting the values and using $\pi^2 = 10$:

$C = \dfrac{1}{4 \times 10 \times (10^4)^2 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}$

$C = \dfrac{1}{40 \times 10^8 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}$

$C = \dfrac{1}{80 \times 10^2} = \dfrac{1}{8000}\ \text{F}$

Comparing with $C = \dfrac{1}{x}\ \text{F}$, we get $x = 8000$.

Answer: $8000$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Series LCR circuit containing an a.c. source of 100V has a inductor and a capacitor of reactance $24\ \Omega$ and $16\ \Omega$ respectively. If a resistance of $6\ \Omega$ is connected in series, then the potential difference across the series combination of inductor and capacitor only is
questions.solution:
Given $V = 100\text{V}$, $X_L = 24\ \Omega$, $X_C = 16\ \Omega$, and $R = 6\ \Omega$.

The net reactance of the circuit is $X = X_L - X_C = 24 - 16 = 8\ \Omega$.

The impedance of the series LCR circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

Substituting the values, $Z = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\ \Omega$.

The rms current in the circuit is $I = \dfrac{V}{Z} = \dfrac{100}{10} = 10\text{A}$.

The potential difference across the series combination of the inductor and capacitor is $V_{LC} = I \times |X_L - X_C|$.

$V_{LC} = 10 \times 8 = 80\text{V}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Alternating current of peak value $\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)$ A flows through the primary coil of a transformer. The coefficient of mutual inductance between primary and secondary coils is 1H. The peak value of induced e.m.f. in the secondary coil is
(Frequency of a.c. = 50 Hz)
questions.solution:
The current in the primary coil is $I = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$.

The induced e.m.f. in the secondary coil is given by $e = -M \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

$e = -M \dfrac{d}{dt} (I_0 \sin(\omega t)) = -M I_0 \omega \cos(\omega t)$

The peak value of the induced e.m.f. is $e_0 = M I_0 \omega$.
